solution_summary: The shared approach aggregates session information and then generates outputs based on probabilities and ranks. Logistic regression improves separation between countries, and rank averaging combines predictions. The author did not select this approach for a final submission and reports that the chosen ensembles performed worse. Final submission selection used both public leaderboard and cross-validation scores.

The final approach used a Boltzmann ensemble adapted from an earlier competition solution by John Mitchell. It combined five strong public notebooks with two of the author's own high scoring notebooks. The writeup credits the notebook authors but provides no further implementation or validation details.

solution_title: #39 Solution soon. Congrats to everyone. Thanks to Hengck23
solution_summary: This post thanks teammates and community contributors and announces a forthcoming writeup and code release. It links a repository and collects background papers, software, and architecture references concerning RNA structure and sequence modeling. It does not describe an implemented competition pipeline or report its results.

solution_title: My Strategy & The Dangers of Public Notebooks
solution_summary: The author developed a leaderboard-tuned last-value forecast as a hedge and a main autoregressive tree-model ensemble. The main pipeline combined custom preprocessing with a public baseline's preprocessing and incorporated the discrete nature of microbusiness density. It forecast every test period recursively using XGBoost, CatBoost, and LightGBM, after removing a meta-model. GRUs, linear regression, and ARMA were unsuccessful, and the author also removed submission code that incorrectly scaled private-period predictions.

solution_title: 13th place solution - How I survived the shakeup
solution_summary: The solution combined Swin, ViT, ResNeXt, and EfficientNet models using ridge regression trained on out-of-fold predictions. Training decisions prioritized stable cross-validation under a 10-fold split stratified by 20 target bins, with fixed short training runs instead of early stopping. Binary cross-entropy worked best overall, while a Swin model trained with binned multiclass cross-entropy was the strongest individual model. Horizontal-flip inference and architectural diversity helped the ensemble reach a CV score of 17.134049.

solution_title: My Part of Team's Solution (Punch Cards Are All You Need, LB Rank 24)
solution_summary: The author trained bi-encoders to predict markdown-code adjacency from cosine similarity, using multiple-negatives ranking loss and hard negatives from the same notebook. Synthetic beginning and ending code cells improved handling of introductory and summary markdown cells. The final team solution combined CodeBERT and GraphCodeBERT bi-encoders with a pointwise DeBERTa-v3-base model. Ensembling fractional predictions with optimized weights and confidence-dependent adjustments achieved 0.8824, while length-sorted batching kept inference efficient.
compute: Single model trained for 3 epochs in 17 hours on an A6000; inference took 1 hour 20 minutes.

solution_summary: The solution combined three prompt attacks designed to produce different scoring patterns across the hidden judges. Gemma chat-template injection, identity-conditioned instructions, and a modified essay-counting prompt produced complementary disagreements. The author submitted six variants of each attack and optimized the submission seed and final essay indices using public leaderboard feedback. The final submission scored 29.829 on the private leaderboard, with imperfect reliability of the third attack limiting performance.
compute: Approximately three weeks spent developing the third attack.

solution_title: [Working Note] When a Guardrail Erases Its Own Benchmark
solution_summary: The team audited the public guardrail and scorer to determine which failure predicates could actually receive credit. This reduced public optimization to maximizing sentinel-bearing posts within the replay budget, using lower generation overhead and a template-state multi-post construction. Repeated evaluations revealed substantial score noise, so small single-run gains were treated cautiously. Public exfiltration finalists scored zero privately, while a retained clean confused-deputy hedge transferred exactly at 11.915.
compute: Hosted evaluator; inference engine settings were fixed. Minimal reachability proof was CPU-only.

solution_title: Solution Write up For CommonLit - Evaluate Student Summaries
solution_summary: The author fine-tuned separate DeBERTa backbones for student summaries and prompts, with two additional heads predicting wording and content scores. These predictions were fed into a LightGBM ensemble alongside n-gram features. DeBERTa used random holdout validation, while LightGBM used K-fold cross-validation. The author proposed larger backbones and prompt-separated validation as future improvements.

The author improved an MLP by adding LayerNorm to gene and cell features, normalizing them row-wise. This reduced the private score from 0.01625 to 0.01616 and the public score from 0.01834 to 0.01824. Adding row-wise normalized features to TabNet also helped, although the reported public improvement was smaller.

solution_title: 203 Place Solution for the Detect Sleep States Competition
solution_summary: The submitted approach used a neural network followed by peak-based postprocessing to detect sleep events. The author credited public notebooks and code by tubotubo. Boosting models, TSFresh, and blending with public kernels were reported as unsuccessful, with no numerical results provided.

The approach trained U-Net and LinkNet segmentation models with EfficientNet-B3 backbones on downscaled, overlapping image crops. Base training combined Dice and binary cross-entropy losses with Lookahead and cosine warm restarts, followed by lower-rate Adam fine-tuning using test-set pseudo-labels. Individual models achieved a private score of 0.945, while the submitted merged version scored 0.943. Offline analysis showed that pseudo-labeling increased Dice scores but also false detections, and merging amplified shared prediction errors.

This component searches for input crops whose properties match those observed in the training outputs. It compares attributes such as color counts and symmetry, repeatedly sampling crops until a match is found. The published implementation solves four public tasks, while additional properties and some luck allowed it to solve six.

The solution combined SE-ResNeXt101, PNASNet5Large, and SENet154 with test-time augmentation, achieving a leaderboard score of 0.650. Five-fold iterative stratification supported validation, while cosine warm restarts enabled convergence in about 15 epochs. Scheduled mixup and increased dropout improved individual models. Inference thresholds were adjusted to match the validation-derived average of 5.2 labels per image.
compute: 15 epochs with 3 restarts to converge; GPU model unspecified.

solution_summary: The team combined simulated annealing, a genetic algorithm, and iterated local search with controlled kicks to optimize word orderings. Rapid annealing, cutoff restarts, and fixing the first word helped escape persistent local optima. Genetic crossover reused diverse local solutions, while threshold-based local search and score-history exclusion further expanded exploration. The genetic algorithm improved id 3 from about 195.0 to 191.7 and id 5 from 28.8 to 28.5.
compute: Approximately 30 minutes per simulated annealing trial; GPU resources used, hardware unspecified.

solution_title: 1st place - A lot of features, a lot of models, and a little bit of luck
solution_summary: The solution centered on extensive feature engineering, especially numerical digit interactions and target/count encodings. Encodings also used the original dataset and auxiliary targets such as employment status and debt-to-income ratio. A diverse ensemble contained 100 models, with XGBoost providing the strongest individual result at approximately 0.92818 CV and 0.92923 private score. Ridge and HC were the strongest ensemble methods, while nonlinear stacking performed substantially worse.

The solution decomposed sales into day-of-week, country GDP, store, product, and day-of-year effects before forecasting the remaining curve. A constant forecast trajectory performed much better than continuing the upward trend. Holiday adjustments substantially improved leaderboard scores and were estimated from median normalized values from the previous year. These adjustments accounted for delayed effects, moving holidays, and three Kenyan holidays absent from the holiday package.

The post presents a BERT fine-tuning baseline for detecting insincere Quora questions and points to related project code and execution scripts. Its reported validation F1 is 0.63 for the positive class and 0.81 macro averaged. A tensor2tensor comparison performs worse, with positive-class F1 of 0.21 and macro F1 of 0.58. The post supplies limited pipeline details beyond the baseline and validation results.

The solution reconstructed ordered column and row groups to recover leaked targets and build grouped features. Recovered test targets augmented training for gradient boosting models, with the strongest submissions using 97 and 110 column groups. Features combined raw columns, group statistics, and sums of important groups, followed by importance-based selection and four-fold tuning. The final prediction was a weighted sum of 23 LightGBM and XGBoost models, with weights adjusted using out-of-fold and leak predictions.

solution_title: 39th solution-Attention Gated Resnet18 ( single model without cv)
solution_summary: The solution used Attention Gated Networks with ResNet18 backbones, combining attended features from the final three blocks. Three crop-size models were ensembled using full-resolution predictions and a fixed threshold of 0.2. Training used competition PNGs and external HPA RGBY images, SGD with momentum, and a combined soft F1 and focal loss. The reported score pairs were 0.604/0.540 for the size ensemble and 0.601/0.547 with oversampling; cross-validation was not used.

The authors initialized football policies by cloning strong submissions, then improved them with a custom IMPALA actor-critic system. KL penalties preserved useful initial behavior and stabilized successive rounds of reinforcement learning. A deeper convolutional network combined player relationships, game state, and action-history features, with additional information available only to the critic. Training mixed self-play with a diverse fixed opponent pool, while a separate internal evaluation pool reduced the noise of leaderboard comparisons. Simple goal-based rewards worked better than elaborate mode-specific rewards, and their strongest individual agent outperformed attempted combinations.
compute: Each experiment ran in one Docker container with actor and learner in separate threads; inference took 0.01–0.15 seconds per action.

solution_title: 102nd Place Solution - Clustering And Refinement with Reconstruction Loss To Beat Public Codes
solution_summary: The solution refines initial velocity maps from models or public prediction CSVs using clustering and a physics-based loss. Replacing cluster velocities with their medians improved MAE from 25.6 to 25.4, with replacement skipped for maps exhibiting many clusters. FlatVel samples were identified through shot symmetry and constrained to share velocities across each depth before physics refinement. Compute and memory limits restricted final refinement to two steps per test sample, while training or fine-tuning alternative neural models did not beat the public baselines.
compute: Physics refinement required shot splitting and gradient accumulation; final processing used two steps per test sample. A 40-step example took a few minutes. TPU v4 use is also mentioned.

solution_title: Our Approach - Similarity-Based Sampling Bad Teaching (12th on public leaderboard)
solution_summary: The solution performs machine unlearning through a student trained against a good teacher and a bad teacher. The student starts from the original model, while the bad teacher receives limited pretraining on retained data. Similarity-based sampling and weighting emphasize retained examples near forgotten examples, and batch ordering emphasizes forgetting before reconstruction. The authors report strong local and public results, but their submission did not reach final evaluation, possibly because of a timeout.

The final submission used CatBoost with geometry features derived from pairwise atomic distances. Percentiles and counts for atom pairs, improved by duplicating atoms across periodic boundaries, were the main contribution and produced a score below 0.062. LSTM representations added to CatBoost gave inconsistent improvements and were excluded from the final submission. Standalone LSTM and CNN models performed worse, while a small number of high-error samples dominated validation loss.

solution_title: My simple trick for this competition
solution_summary: The post describes combining a binary outlier predictor with a regression model for non-outliers. The final prediction interpolates between the fixed outlier value of -33.21928 and the non-outlier regression output using the binary prediction. This improved local cross-validation by 0.015 compared with direct training on the same features. The reported classifier AUC was 0.914, and the non-outlier regression CV score was 1.545.

The author trained paired models with half-point targets rounded upward and downward, then averaged their predictions to reflect the original integer rubric. The final submission used an OOF-informed weighted ensemble of DeBERTa variants, several other transformers, and an embedding-based SVR. Adversarial training, layer-wise learning rates, weight initialization, pretrained weight decay, and a maximum text length of 768 were reported as helpful. Despite agreement between cross-validation and the public leaderboard, the submission suffered a substantial private-leaderboard decline.
compute: Training used Kaggle notebooks and the free Colab plan; hardware and training duration were not specified.

solution_title: 303rd / Bronze: Sub-voxel localization + a learned coordinate head
solution_summary: The solution refined detections from a public temporal-UNet3D and ILP pipeline using local soft-argmax, with z refinement providing most of the initial gain. Its stronger variant used a public learned coordinate head for y/x and supplied refined z coordinates to the edge model. Motion-relinker tuning and protected raw-ILP overrides raised the public score to 0.955, while a separate soft-argmax variant scored 0.954. Both variants were selected to hedge coordinate-transfer risk, and development replay was interpreted cautiously because the detector and edge model had seen its movies.

solution_summary: The solution ensembled ImageNet-pretrained EfficientNetB3 U-Nets trained at two patch scales with five folds grouped by whole-slide image. Excluding uninformative regions and using strong augmentation helped maintain agreement between local validation and the public leaderboard. Inference combined flip augmentation, overlapping tiles, and simple averaging across folds and models. Pseudo-labels and the supplied d48 hand labels brought little private-score benefit, while choosing a threshold for public performance proved costly. The reported scores were 0.9429 local CV, 0.927 public, and 0.947 private.

solution_summary: The author's contribution used a 2.5D U-Net with an EfficientNet B7 backbone, taking slices n−2, n, and n+2 as three input channels. Images were resized to 640 pixels and cropped to 384×384 during training, with around 100 epochs and AdamW optimization. Lighter augmentation improved the public score from 0.882 to 0.884 and the private score from 0.870 to 0.872. The team used both case-grouped and case-stratified folds to address test cases shared with training, although the author felt they overemphasized those shared cases.

solution_title: just a short tutorial to get 25th place
solution_summary: The author removed classes associated with attributes and followed a linked Torchvision tutorial. Input images had a minimum edge length of 800 pixels. The reported public and private scores were 0.22209 and 0.20699, respectively, with no further training or modeling details provided.

The solution fine-tuned Gemma-2-9B-IT for three-class preference classification using LoRA in BF16. A first model trained on official and deduplicated supplementary data generated pseudo-labels for 30,000 UltraFeedback samples, after which a fresh model was trained on the combined data. Custom truncation preserved portions of the prompt and both responses, while inference used longer sequences and response-order swapping. Rule-based probability overrides handled empty or identical responses.
compute: 4× A100 40GB; approximately 10 hours for Stage1 and 15 hours for Stage2 per experiment.

solution_summary: The author combined EfficientNet image features with metadata and a spatial attention head, using noisy-student weights in the illustrated B3 model. External 2018 data and malignant upsampling were retained, while the 2019 portion was excluded after experiments. Sprinkle augmentation reduced overfitting but slowed learning, prompting the addition of attention. The final ensemble averaged strong CV models selected for lower prediction correlations across image sizes, EfficientNet variants, and data ratios.

solution_summary: The solution uses R scripts to load data, extract features, merge datasets, and fit XGBoost models for click prediction. Feature extraction includes phone, search, and visit datasets. A reduced-data run is recommended to verify expected results before running the full submission pipeline. The full pipeline has substantial memory requirements attributed to the implementation and R's memory handling.

solution_summary: The solution combined LightGBM, MLP, and 1D CNN models with target-specific ensemble weights. Eight prediction periods used different gaps between prediction dates and historical target features to respect test-time availability. Roughly 440 features captured player engagement history, recent baseball activity, and aggregated event-model predictions. Time-based validation across several months guided feature selection, while shared streaming feature generation kept training and inference consistent.

The team combined sensor-based tree models with neural models using video from both camera views and tracking features. Their video pipeline used 2.5D convolutions, residual 3D blocks and GeM pooling, while separate tree models handled player-to-player and player-to-ground contact. A second stage used four LightGBM models with temporal shifts of predictions and sensor data, followed by averaging and temporal smoothing. The combined CNN/GBDT component achieved 0.778 cross-validation and 0.773 private scores.

solution_summary: The solution ensembled eight landmark embedding models, combining DOLG architectures with EfficientNet–Swin hybrids and retrained models from earlier solutions. Training progressed from clean data at low resolution to a larger noisy dataset at higher resolutions. Dynamic-margin sub-ArcFace heads and a staged freezing procedure supported effective embedding training. Recognition postprocessing reused the previous year’s method, primarily to identify non-landmark images, and validation used the labeled 2019 test set.

solution_summary: The team combined more than 120 base models through two layers of stacking. Their strongest individual network used a two-level bidirectional GRU, max pooling, skip connections, and concatenated 900-dimensional GloVe and FastText embeddings. Neural networks, Extra Trees, and LightGBM formed first-level meta-models using predictions, uppercase counts, and rank-transformed inputs. A final weighted average of ranked meta-model outputs reached 0.9881, while a third stacking layer added no value.

The solution combined optimized regular tree tilings, a modified Sparrow packer, and a C++ billiard refinement algorithm. Treating a fixed block of trees as one object helped Sparrow handle larger configurations, while billiard typically reduced its resulting side length by about 0.2%. The team generated more diverse starting configurations by splicing and symmetrizing existing solutions. Population-based refinement and collision repairs during expansion further improved the search.

The final submissions combined EfficientNet B4 and ViT models or used only ViT models. EfficientNet used 2020 data, while transformer experiments also included selected classes from the 2019 dataset. Heavy image augmentation, label smoothing of 0.3, AdamP, and cosine warm restarts supported training. A blend weighted 0.4 toward EfficientNet and 0.6 toward ViT scored 0.9011 privately; a variant using a ViT trained only on 2020 data reached 0.9017.
compute: 10 training epochs plus 4 fine-tuning epochs.

solution_summary: The team combined diverse image models, primarily Swin Transformers, with weighted ensembling and a ridge ensemble for one group of models. Some networks also incorporated the provided binary attributes and image dimensions. Image hashes linked overlapping images to metadata from the previous PetFinder competition, which fed a second-stage GBDT alongside neural predictions. Training this second stage on the entire current dataset appeared helpful, although metadata feature experiments frequently overfit and worsened leaderboard scores.
The post links to the team's report and code repository. It states that the code uses the Apache License 2.0. The provided text contains no description of the modeling pipeline or results.

The final approach lightly modified the public ARChitects2024 solution, which other experiments did not surpass. Each task received 24 epochs of test-time training with a batch size of four and two gradient accumulation steps. Training examples, inference examples, and DFS branching were reduced to save time, and two subprocesses accelerated inference. Two submissions were selected for consistent behavior, although some tasks still exceeded the 12-hour limit.
compute: 12-hour runtime limit; some tasks did not finish; two inference subprocesses.

solution_summary: The pipeline first localized disc levels and spinal canals with CenterNet detectors, then classified severity from cropped sagittal and axial slices. Separate center and side classifiers combined 2D slice encoders with attention, sharing learning across disc levels and normalizing left and right inputs. Annotation correction, auxiliary losses, severe-class weighting, and diverse models supported accuracy. Averaging 30 models improved CV from a best single-model score of 0.3858 to 0.3643, followed by temperature scaling for spinal canal predictions.

The solution retrieves candidate items using multiple strategies and ranks them with interaction features and gradient-boosted classifiers. Recent popularity, repurchases, collaborative filtering, and embedding similarity drive retrieval and feature construction. A six-week training window and last-week validation showed stable validation-to-leaderboard correlation, while weekly negative downsampling controlled dataset size. The final ensemble of five LightGBM and seven CatBoost classifiers achieved a reported leaderboard score of 0.0371.
compute: Desktop with 128 GB RAM, 64 CPU vcores and TITAN RTX; teammate desktop with 64 GB RAM; final-week 300 GB RAM GCP instances and rented vast.ai GPU server.

solution_title: Circular way to think about solution
solution_summary: The author proposes building a closed route by expanding a small circular linked list. Each iteration considers adjacent route nodes and inserts an unvisited neighbor at the position with the lowest incremental cost. The insertion objective adds two edge costs and subtracts the replaced edge cost. The implementation became progressively slower despite caching, and no competitive score is reported.

solution_title: 173rd Place Solution: From 0.880 Baseline to 0.957 SOTA
solution_summary: The author developed a 3D cell detection and tracking pipeline through 66 controlled iterations, combining U-Net detection, spatial augmentation, graph optimization, and biological motion constraints. Division maturity, sister symmetry and divergence, bidirectional edge support, and clearance-gated relinking improved tracking, reaching a public score of 0.957 from roughly 0.880. solution_title: 66th Place Solution for the Bengali.AI Speech Recognition Competition

solution_title: 182nd Place Solution for the "ICR - Identifying Age-Related Conditions" Competition (plus the better one)

Two sequence-to-sequence LSTMs forecast 28 days of sales at store-item and department-store levels. Averaging predictions from 20 checkpoints per model reduced training instability. Four chronological validation windows guided development and supported stable local and leaderboard performance.

The approach used a symbolic search pipeline driven by task properties such as shapes, colors, grids, and symmetries. Tasks were simplified before searching sequences of operations, with three candidates retained according to training pixel errors. Some tasks were also decomposed into individual shapes or non-common colors and solved again. General preprocessing accounted for many improvements, and merging complementary solutions from another teammate produced a reported leaderboard score of about 0.81.

The final pipeline used RealMLP_TD_Classifier with a fixed feature set and averaged 15 models across three seeds and five stratified folds. Features included ratios, count encodings, quantile bins, and target-encoded category combinations. High-confidence test predictions were added as pseudo-labels before retraining from scratch. Additional features, LightGBM blending, and logit stacking degraded validation or public performance. The submitted pseudo-label round achieved 0.95472 OOF AUC and the same private score.

solution_summary: The solution filtered MegaDetector predictions without training a model or tracking animals. Images were split into low-density and high-density groups using a threshold of eight detections, with separate filtering rules for each. High-density images used a zero confidence threshold and modified NMS, while low-density images used overlap-dependent confidence thresholds and an additional filtering pass. The final sequence count was the maximum image count, and the best reported public score was 0.247.

solution_title: 8th Place Solution -- Decision tree part + source code
solution_summary: This team component treats each task as ten-class pixel classification using engineered features and decision trees. It explores combinations of color transformations, spatial augmentation, and featurizers tailored to input-output size relationships. A logistic regression confidence model trained on the evaluation set selects three candidate predictions. It solved 8 of 102 leaderboard tasks, 76 of 419 evaluation tasks, and 136 of 416 training tasks.

The solution combined 18 LightGBM and XGBoost models using grouped cross-validation and validation on truncated samples. Game event aggregates were included, although their high feature importance translated into little leaderboard improvement. The XGBoost pipeline also incorporated prior test assessments into training and used two truncation seeds per fold. A custom voting rule selected strongly supported classes and otherwise used distances to model thresholds, producing public and private scores of 0.549.

solution_title: 13th Place - From LB 710 to LB 726 - How To
solution_summary: The best submission used a TensorFlow RoBERTa-base span extractor with a modified head that predicted the end position before conditioning the start prediction on its logits. Preserving whitespace, splitting punctuation tokens, and choosing conservative training spans helped model annotation quirks. Label smoothing, random masking, learning-rate decay, sentiment-based sample weights, and full-data retraining improved performance. Repeated cross-validation supported the changes, and final post-processing brought the reported scores to 0.718 CV, 0.724 public, and 0.726 private.

The solution used a modified Faster R-CNN with independent region-proposal and character-classification networks operating on images resized to 512×512. Wide ResNet-34 backbones, clustered anchor sizes, ROI Align, and extensive dropout were central design choices. The final proposal network used color images, while classification used grayscale to limit overfitting. Language-model correction experiments failed to improve the best detector output and were abandoned.

solution_title: Fighting Against Variance Under Compute Constraints
solution_summary: The final system used three base mathematical solver attempts, standardized their reasoning through summarization, and invoked five tool-enabled judges when the base answers disagreed. Speculative decoding with an Eagle3 draft model made the workflow fit the runtime limit despite reducing concurrency. Final selection prioritized judge agreement, then combined votes, with average trace length as a last tie-breaker. The selected 65k-context configuration achieved 47/50 locally in 3h 48m and a public score of 42.

solution_summary: The solution used XGBoost with leak-derived information, group features, and a stratified split based on people IDs. The number of people per group was particularly useful, especially for single-person groups. A separate model predicting whether a group had all-zero, all-one, or mixed outcomes supplied a fuzzed and binned feature to the final XGBoost model, improving the reported score from 0.992914 to 0.993118. Runs across different machines produced variable models, and the author submitted the better result from the dual E5605 machine.

solution_title: 3rd Place Solution - Congratulations New Competition Grandmaster Amed!
solution_summary: The final submission combined 24 diverse models, mostly DeBERTa-v3-large variants, without pseudo labels. Greedy hill climbing selected models and ensemble weights, including negative weights, reaching CV 0.4420 compared with the best single-model CV of 0.4470. Model diversity came from backbones, regression heads, pooling, training settings, and an embedding-based SVR. Pseudo labels improved local validation substantially but did not improve leaderboard performance and were excluded.

The solution used diverse neural question-pair models to generate out-of-fold features for XGBoost. Its strongest network combined a Siamese bidirectional LSTM, recurrent highway layers, attention, and frozen GloVe embeddings, reaching 89.1% validation accuracy. Character, character-trigram, and convolutional networks added complementary signals alongside semantic and linguistic features. A graph-like feature derived from predicted duplicates helped further, and confident predictions were clipped.

solution_summary: The solution used CNN backbones followed by transformer encoders and decoders to translate molecular images into strings. Progressive resolution increases and roughly 1.3 million pseudo-labeled samples improved the models. Four models were combined through step-wise logits and beam search, with RDKit selecting chemically valid predictions. Merging earlier submissions and retrying invalid outputs with a larger beam improved the leaderboard score from 0.56 to 0.54.

solution_title: Learning to Build a Long-Running Agent Workflow
solution_summary: The author describes an experiment-management workflow rather than a detailed model architecture. Separate analysis, worker, and acceptance agents prioritized tasks, optimized candidates, and evaluated changes against a frozen canonical submission. Persistent documentation, model hashes, and explicit adoption rules made experiments reproducible and allowed work to continue across conversations. Official A/B evaluation was important because local validation did not always match leaderboard behavior.

solution_title: 123rd place — not where I aimed, but here's what I learned
solution_summary: The solution segments papyrus surfaces in CT scans using a 3D TransUNet with a SEResNeXt101 encoder and 160³ voxel inputs. Training combines recall-focused Tversky loss with CenterlineDice to preserve surface continuity, using Keras 3 and JAX on TPU v4-32. Inference averages sliding-window predictions and six flip variants, then blends two checkpoints and applies morphological cleanup. The reported score was 0.579; larger spatial context, loss alignment with the evaluation metrics, and checkpoint blending were central to the approach.
compute: Kaggle TPU v4-32, 32 cores; batch size 16; 800-epoch training budget with early stopping patience 60.

solution_summary: The team averaged a diverse collection of PyTorch and TensorFlow models, including nf-resnet50, ResNeXt50, EfficientNets, and base and large vision transformers. Models varied in image size and test-time augmentation, and some used 2019 competition data. Training augmentations combined crops, geometric and color changes, blur, noise, and dropout. Average ensembling was the most consistently useful component; an unselected blend achieved 0.8978 public and 0.9019 private scores.

The solution used a one-layer bidirectional GRU alongside a dense branch for statistical text features. Frozen embeddings combined pretrained GloVe and wiki-news vectors, competition-trained fastText vectors, and binary token attributes. Batch-specific sequence lengths accelerated training, enabling an ensemble of six independently seeded models. Five-fold validation guided tuning, and averaged predictions were thresholded at 0.36; the reported final-model CV score was 0.70974.

solution_title: A Review of the CTF Competition
solution_summary: The author solved half of the CTF challenges using a mixture of exhaustive searches, optimization, data inspection, and external images. Movement-event counts identified human cells, while systematic coordinate searches optimized baseball pitch patterns. Other successes came from searching numeric keys, reenacting a video, inspecting model metadata, and exploiting unusual scoring inputs. External hot-dog and handwritten-character images also yielded flags.

solution_summary: The solution adapted public notebooks around DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B-AWQ, combining a mathematics prompt with time management and voting across generated answers. It removed very short prompts and conflicting labels, adjusted learning rate and batch size, and merged LoRA weights from two epochs. DeBERTa performed substantially worse, and a generation head did not beat the classification head.

The author trained a small neural network on historical regular-season and tournament games, combining team statistics, seeds, conference indicators, and Ken Pom metrics. The final network had hidden layers of 7, 5, and 3 nodes and outperformed random forests and boosted trees. Validation used separate tournament-year holdouts, with log loss between 0.42 and 0.45; the competition result was 0.42788. solution_title: 8th Place Solution for the Child Mind Institute - Detect Sleep States Competition
solution_summary: The solution separated precise event localization from event scoring using a local 1D U-Net regressor and a global-context DensityNet. The regressor predicted relative onset and wakeup positions, while Gaussian accumulation and peak detection produced candidate events. DensityNet used Transformer modules to estimate event densities and event-presence probabilities, which scored those candidates over overlapping daily windows. Prediction shifts, event augmentation, and matrix-profile filtering improved the final detections; the reported augmentation gain was approximately 0.002 mAP.

solution_title: 8th place solution (Flying Over the 1st place again)
solution_summary: The solution improved existing diamond price predictions through domain-informed postprocessing. It capped excessive prices using training-group upper bounds derived from quartiles and the interquartile range. It also raised implausibly low predictions to training minima within carat windows matched on cut, clarity, and color. Correcting training outliers improved CV but harmed leaderboard performance, whereas prediction adjustments produced substantial reported gains.

The author converted point clouds into RGB images and applied an SSD detector. Image brightness encoded point-cloud density, while hue encoded the weighted center of the vertical position. The post links implementation code but gives no validation scores or training details.

The final pipeline used DBSCAN clustering with helix unrolling, multiple z shifts, and track extension after unsuccessful exploration of deep learning approaches. Six geometric features and Bayesian tuning of feature weights, iteration count, and DBSCAN epsilon improved clustering quality. Hits were merged into the longest eligible tracks, and six extension rounds refined the results. The solution scored 0.59229 on the private leaderboard and processed each event in roughly nine to ten minutes on a 96-core GCP machine.

solution_summary: The solution used BERT with five folds and three training epochs, closely following a public notebook. A special token separated question titles from bodies, although its benefit was uncertain. A small LightGBM postprocessor reduced the number of distinct prediction values to improve Spearman correlation. This added about 0.02 on the private leaderboard, yielding a score of 0.39507.

The agent used repeated forward simulation with persistent unit roles and goal state machines to plan actions. Its economy emphasized early lichen growth, adding robots when estimated power income supported further expansion. Factory placement balanced resources and terrain, with an aggressive ice-denial strategy supported by water transporters and blockade units. Prioritized action selection and exclusive assignments coordinated units, although ice conflicts performed poorly against an opponent that moved ice flexibly with heavy robots.

Additional waypoints from the host's step-position function made this construction effective. Pseudo-labeling and the teammate's cost-minimization post-processing were also important.

The solution combined multitask classification–segmentation models with a separate ensemble of opacity detectors. Both branches used external chest X-ray pretraining, staged transfer learning, and pseudo-labeling. A manually supervised lung localizer improved classification crops, while test-time augmentation and weighted ensembles improved final predictions. The reported public and private scores were 0.658 and 0.635.

Retrieval reranking used inferred landmark labels and cosine confidence to softly promote matching index images and demote mismatches.

solution_summary: The solution stacked public LSTM predictions into a LightGBM model. Subject-level and sequence-level aggregates supplied information that sequence-only LSTMs missed, including subject aggregates of their predictions. The author reran the LSTMs to obtain out-of-fold training predictions and test predictions. This stacking approach produced better synergy than simple blending.

The author developed rock-paper-scissors agents from uniform randomness through multistage statistical prediction to decision trees. Statistical Prediction repeatedly recalibrated weighted guesses using opponent frequencies and prediction history, achieving a reported best score of 894.1. The later decision-tree agent used roughly nine moves of history and defensive randomness on 66% of turns. Two prediction layers worked better with defensive randomness, and the tree approach reached a reported best score of 971.0.

The solution used a single GPU-trained RAPIDS XGBoost regressor with ten-fold stratified validation. Optuna optimized quadratic weighted kappa after converting regression outputs into classes using fold-specific optimized cutoffs. Test predictions were averaged across folds and rounded to integers. Inference sampled 42 solutions per problem, retried noninteger execution results, and selected answers using reward-weighted voting with a geometric-mean aggregation and a penalty for zero. On the ten AIMO training problems, policy fine-tuning improved accuracy from 1/10 to 2/10, and reward-based selection increased it to 4/10.

solution_summary: The author framed package recommendation as binary classification and combined four complementary models: a metadata baseline, latent factors, user-specific topic preferences, and user-specific task-view preferences. Post-processing recalled labels for previously observed user-package pairs and forced positive predictions for inferred dependencies. solution_summary: The solution combined a decision-tree approach with cropping, grid-based DSL methods, tile-based DSL methods, and public kernels. The decision-tree component solved seven tasks, while the grid DSL solved three. Tile DSL methods solved seven tasks after accounting for overlap between two contributors, and public kernels contributed two tasks. The team ensembled two independently developed pipelines built around approximate customer and card identities. Grouped transaction statistics, temporal features, and categorical encodings supplied LightGBM, CatBoost, and XGBoost models, with CatBoost performing best. One pipeline used month-based grouped validation and multiple seeds, while the other split transactions by ProductCD and used stratified validation. Combining the pipelines provided a substantial gain, whereas neural networks, denoising autoencoders, and stacking did not work well.

The author built a time-series solution associated with an LSTM notebook, separating stocks using features 41–43. Dense time embeddings derived from feature_64 represented irregular observation times, while linear regression denoised targets and substantially improved stability. Training excluded dates before 85 and zero-weight rows, with four-fold combinatorial purged validation. The model had fewer than 100,000 parameters and received only limited manual hyperparameter tuning.

The author adapted SECOND for 3D object detection on the Lyft dataset. They adjusted anchor ranges and object sizes and added the competition metric for validation. An 80:20 scene-based split supported model selection, with VoxelNet and PillarFeatureNet working best.

solution_title: Approach: Maximum non-contiguous sub-matrix sum heuristic
solution_summary: The author developed a GPU cube solver that combines move sequences affecting a fixed number of elements across cube sizes, sharing face moves to reduce cost. The approach generates one- and two-dimensional move sets, checks special cases, and repeatedly selects moves using score per move count. A heuristic handles noncontiguous row and column combinations, while pruning rows and columns without positive scores accelerates later iterations. The implementation remained incomplete, but a laptop run solved a size-33 cube in under an hour using about 15,000 moves.

Predictions came from an ensemble of public and privately trained DeBERTa-v3-large models, with private training using a filtered 60k dataset and validation on a 500-sample dataset. Sublinear term frequency improved the private leaderboard score by 0.003 while reducing the public score by 0.004. solution_title: 5th Place Solution Overview, Looked till 100th but was right at 5th :)
solution_summary: The team combined essay-reconstruction features with several neural networks and three tree models, achieving a best 10-fold CV score of 0.5860. Transformers contributed little, and trusting local cross-validation was central to the team's selection process.

The solution emphasized one engineered feature set shared by XGBoost, LightGBM, and TabM, with five seeds per model. Digit extraction, numeric bins, higher-order digit interactions, and original-data encodings supplied the main improvements. Ridge regression combined their OOF predictions with AutoGluon predictions, reaching 0.92805 CV and 0.92912 privately. Fold-specific feature caching accelerated tuning, and reliable CV guided the choice to use fold averages instead of full-data training.

A lightweight all-pairs matching pass generated nearest-neighbor shortlists from inlier counts, with extra pairs added to ensure coverage of every image. Rotation correction and parallel COLMAP processing improved robustness and efficiency. The best completed submission ran in 7 hours and 40 minutes; several alternatives were excluded because of accuracy, runtime, or setup problems.

solution_title: 29th Place Solution for the CommonLit - Evaluate Student Summaries Competition
solution_summary: The final prediction averaged a LightGBM stack of nine DeBERTa/BART models with a separate long-input DeBERTa-v3-large model. The stack incorporated text-length, overlap, similarity, edit-distance, and readability features. Position-specific masks helped the long-input model distinguish summary tokens from prompt material, while validation grouped examples by prompt. The final average achieved CV 0.471 and public score 0.433; weight optimization and a similarity-matrix CNN did not improve the approach.

solution_title: Ablation Study on Publicly-Shared Solutions through Late Submission
solution_summary: This post reports a post-competition ablation study of a two-stage sleep-event detection pipeline. A lightweight 1D CNN with a U-Net encoder generated event probabilities, followed by AP-oriented postprocessing and XGBoost regression using prediction-derived features. Matching the processing sequence between training and inference restored validation-to-leaderboard correlation, while the imputation flag and rolling-mean postprocessing were particularly useful. The best reported local AP was 0.8282, with private leaderboard AP of 0.838.

One pipeline used a pretrained Mask R-CNN detector without its mask head, added depth prediction, and estimated pose from cropped vehicles. A second pipeline used CenterNet to jointly predict vehicle geometry and pose. Predictions from different detectors were matched with the Hungarian algorithm and averaged when distance and yaw differences were sufficiently small.

solution_summary: The pipeline filtered and epoched EEG signals, extracted XDAWN covariance features, selected electrodes, and projected covariance matrices into tangent space before Elastic Net prediction. Session metadata and averaging 500 models trained on random subject subsets helped generalization. Repeated subject-wise cross-validation guided parameter selection. A second variant exploited feedback timing leakage and adjusted predictions for subject class balance, achieving private AUC 0.87224 versus 0.84585 without leakage.

solution_summary: The author used shuffled five-fold cross-validation and grid search to select tree models and feature subsets. The main ensemble combined LightGBM using 20 important features with two XGBoost models using different feature selections, achieving a cross-validation score of 0.602019. Added features, outlier removal, and one-hot encoding were excluded from these selected models. The final submission blended this ensemble with a baseline at weights of 0.7 and 0.3, achieving a private leaderboard score of 0.55396.

The author built 173 models and combined them through stacking, hillclimbing, and Ridge regression. Target-dependent XGBoost loss weights addressed systematic overprediction of low scores and underprediction of high scores. Diversity came from disagreement-based selection, alternative regression objectives, outlier probabilities, and models specialized by internet access. The resulting ensemble outperformed every individual model, although no numeric final score is supplied.

The solution trained separate two-player and four-player transformer agents through pure self-play PPO with prioritized sampling of past opponents. A reachability tensor supplied travel times, launch angles, ship counts, graph features, and action masks, while semantic actions substantially accelerated learning. Custom attention biases, global conditioning, and a sparse action head helped the model reason about planetary relationships efficiently. Entropy scheduling was the most influential training choice; the submitted checkpoints accumulated about 8.4 billion and 2.7 billion training steps for the two modes.
compute: Early experiments on RTX 3090, later RTX 5090 and RTX 6000 Pros; used at most 2 GPUs. Two RTX 6000 GPUs achieved about 19k SPS for 2p and 15k for 4p. Submitted checkpoints trained for about 8.4B and 2.7B steps, respectively.

solution_title: 6th Place Solution for Google Code Golf Championship
solution_summary: The solution primarily relied on handwritten code golf, supplemented by ZLIB compression and variable-name optimization. Short programs used techniques including BFS, rotation unrolling, byte-string constants, and exec-based loop unrolling. Longer programs were compressed with zopfli, then optimized for compressed size through static-analysis-constrained renaming followed by simulated annealing. Hand golfing contributed 955,251 score points, compression added 2,276, and code optimization added about 400.
compute: Static analysis took approximately 3 hours for all handwritten submissions; simulated annealing took approximately 12 hours.

solution_summary: The agent used cached geometry and a strategic simulator to enable fast end-to-end JAX PPO training. An entity transformer processed planet features, incoming fleet summaries, and projected future states, then selected sources, targets, and ship quantities through conditional heads. Separate two-player and four-player policies learned through checkpoint-based self-play evaluated on held-out maps. A lighter policy-only action rerun performed better for one two-player submission, while an explicit two-source capture option was excluded from the final submission.
compute: Two RTX 5090 machines used separately for two-player and four-player training near the end.

solution_summary: The author was using Mask R-CNN and reported that it worked reasonably well and was easy to modify. They proposed a U-Net-like segmentation approach followed by instance separation and possibly a separate attribute classifier. They highlighted fixed-size object masks and resampling as potential limitations of Mask R-CNN mask quality. Attribute prediction remained difficult, and no final pipeline or numerical result was provided.

The author focused on manually optimizing a single RealMLP model, using Trompt initially for fast feature experiments. They added 22 features, with combined quantile and k-means numerical discretization providing particularly useful improvements. The final submission nevertheless used hill climbing to combine their neural models with several public neural and boosted-tree models. This ensemble achieved CV 0.91979, public 0.91730, and private 0.91835.
compute: RealMLP experiments could train for 3 epochs in several minutes.

solution_summary: The solution fed roughly 80 engineered features into a fully connected network with 128- and 64-unit hidden layers and a 199-way softmax output. Most features counted defenders in boxes and radial regions around the rusher at the current time and at projected times of 0.5 and 1.0 seconds. Minimum and mean defender distances supplemented standard rusher information. Rethinking the spatial and temporal features produced the main breakthrough, while simple offensive-player counts did not significantly improve performance.

The solution equally averaged ranked predictions from 11 subject-specific models to improve robustness with minimal weight tuning. Models used short EEG windows and engineered spectral, statistical, correlation, information-theoretic, and Riemannian tangent-space features. XGBoost, nearest neighbors, logistic regression, a linear SVM, and a GLM supplied complementary predictions, with maximum or mean aggregation back to ten-minute segments. Validation preserved one-hour sequence groups and used two complementary fold schemes because reliable evaluation was difficult. The reported ensemble scores were 0.81308 and 0.80701.
compute: Alex/Gilberto's four models: under half a day including feature extraction. Feng's four models: under 6 hours including feature extraction on an 8 GB RAM MacBook Pro.

solution_summary: This component used Cellpose to predict flow fields that separate touching cells and reconstruct instance masks. LiveCell pretraining, extensive augmentation, cell-type-specific postprocessing, and model ensembling improved performance. Cell diameter estimation was critical: the final ten-model ensemble initialized it with a size model and refined it from successive predicted masks. A single model reached 0.333 public score and a five-model ensemble reached 0.335, while the approach contributed diversity to the team's ensemble.

solution_title: Detailed Post and Kernel about a Deep NLP solution that is worth 35th place

The official final score was not computed because the author missed the Phase 1 submission deadline.

The author developed hundreds of tabular models using boosted trees, RealMLP, logistic regression, and random forests, combining raw inputs with transformed features and original data. The most useful manual features reconstructed daily activity totals or individual activity components through sums and differences. More than 200 public prediction sets supplied useful ensemble diversity, while additional neural models and elaborate blenders offered little improvement. Model decisions primarily followed out-of-fold performance, and the final reported scores were 0.97055 OOF and 0.97123 on the private leaderboard.

solution_title: 26th Place Solution : Effective Cluster Separation and Neighbour Search
solution_summary: The team trained separate image and text embedding models with ArcFace and softmax supervision. Image inference used a larger resolution than training, while text processing translated key English words into Indonesian. Their main improvement modified embeddings using three nearest neighbors, then combined model-specific neighbor distances through outer joins instead of concatenating embeddings. Thresholds depended on predicted match counts, bringing the reported leaderboard score to 0.764; the final ensemble mentions five models but names only four.

solution_title: #3 solution | Many individual models and many ensembles
solution_summary: The solution treated most features as categorical and built a diverse collection of CatBoost, factorization-machine, embedding-network, LAMA, and AutoGluon models. Denoising-autoencoder latent features improved CatBoost and embedding models by about 0.0002. CatBoost was strongest individually, while field-aware factorization machines supplied complementary predictions. The final submission stacked 38 models with a LAMA DenseLight neural network, with LightGBM providing a nearly equivalent alternative.

solution_title: [Top 12% Solution] Active Control Curriculum & Preference Repair
solution_summary: The author fine-tuned Nemotron using a DPO LoRA adapter and a dynamic curriculum driven by observed reasoning failures. The pipeline combined targeted repairs, puzzle-type-matched preservation anchors, hard negatives, and synthetic logic tasks while enforcing a compact reasoning format. ERATO and vLLM supported periodic evaluation on unseen transformation rules. Final checkpoint selection relied too heavily on public scores, and an earlier adapter reportedly generalized better on the private evaluation.

The solution classified ovarian cancer subtypes using multiple instance learning with CTransPath and LunitDINO backbones and DSMIL and Perceiver classifiers. Images were downsampled to x10 and divided into 256×256 tissue patches, with duplicate WSI tissue areas removed to reduce memory use. Perceiver training used binary cross-entropy, mixup, and label smoothing, while DSMIL used cross-entropy. The final approach detected outliers when the maximum sigmoid probability was below 0.4, improving the reported private score from 0.58 to 0.60. Mask annotations and additional datasets were not used in the final submission.

solution_title: [88th place] How I went from 1232 on public leaderboard to 88th place
solution_summary: The author emphasized generating substantial amounts of high-quality synthetic data and maintaining a clean codebase. They deliberately limited submissions to reduce the risk of overfitting the public leaderboard. They developed independently without borrowing public notebook models or code, but stopped submitting during the final two months. The post provides no model architecture, training configuration, or detailed evaluation results.

The solution used a two-stage XLM-RoBERTa pipeline with one encoder and no ensemble. The first stage learned retrieval embeddings using attention pooling, contrastive loss, distance polarized regularization, and negatives mined each epoch. The second stage fine-tuned the first-stage weights to classify topic-content pairs retrieved among the top 50 candidates. Language filtering and score and distance thresholds produced a cross-validation F2 of about 0.6319, with an approximately 0.05 improvement from adding the second stage. Both stages together ran in about six hours.
compute: Approximately 6 hours for stage 1 and stage 2 combined.

solution_title: Solution #17 - Searching for the perfect helix
solution_summary: The final approach reconstructs particle tracks using DBSCAN with features derived from helix geometry. It scans curvature radius and longitudinal origin, uses the Hough equation to estimate helix centers, and clusters on center angle and an arc-length-to-longitudinal-displacement ratio. This replaced an earlier three-model ensemble that scored just over 0.66 and required many hours per event. The redesigned method eventually achieved 0.695 with a few hours of processing per event, although rotations beyond 180 degrees were not handled correctly.
compute: Final approach: a few hours of processing per event; earlier three-model approach: several hours per model per event with 10 z-shifts.

solution_title: 24th place solution and my way to get it
solution_summary: The solution blended models trained at several image resolutions, mainly EfficientNet B5–B7 with ImageNet or NoisyStudent initialization, alongside ResNet152 and InceptionResNetV2. Training combined 2018, 2019, and 2020 data, while validation used only 2020 data through a triple-stratified K-fold pipeline. TPU training enabled larger models and images after early GPU experiments with smaller models plateaued. The author's own blend scored 0.9602 publicly and 0.9406 privately, and final submissions also mixed in selected public predictions chosen for diversity.

solution_summary: The solution extracted text from different HTML fields and trained a separate bag-of-words logistic regression classifier for each field. A second logistic regression model combined their predictions through stacking. Count and length features were explored, but internal cross-validation favored using only text features. The submission achieved public and private scores of 0.87777 and 0.88764.

Both reported solutions ensembled EfficientNet-b2 through b5 models with noisy-student weights, trained for about 20 epochs on 600-by-600 images. The best private score of 0.981 used ImageNetPolicy, horizontal flips, Ranger, binary cross-entropy with logits, and test-time augmentation. Another submission scored 0.975 using additional PCA jitter, RAdam, and smoothed predictions. CutMix, Mixup, weighted loss, focal loss, and larger images did not improve the leaderboard score.

The author fine-tuned pretrained Inception v3 using competition data and Gleb's data, with random 480×480 crops from the central 80% of training images. Augmentation reproduced eight manipulations and preserved JPEG grid alignment. Soft pseudo-labels from unaltered test images supported further fine-tuning. Sensor-noise reference patterns then corrected predictions for both unaltered and manipulated images, providing the largest improvement and reaching a private leaderboard score of 0.987.

The authors adapted Iocaine Powder by adding two randomized strategies based on the opponent's move history. They introduced score decay to favor recent behavior and periodically selected random moves. They submitted variants with different parameters and observed frequent switching between the two random strategies against stronger opponents.

solution_title: 5th place solution (best single model, private LB 0.71443)
solution_summary: The author's contribution combines five EfficientNetV2L-based U-Net models using single frames and multi-frame inputs. Multi-frame variants share an encoder across frames and fuse features with 3D convolutions. Correcting image-mask misalignment was essential for effective flip and rotation augmentation, and training combined consensus and individual-labeler targets. Eight-way test-time augmentation improved scores by 0.005–0.01; the best reported ensemble scored 0.71756 privately but was not selected as the final submission.

The solution uses a random forest over decision scores from one-versus-rest SGD classifiers and sentiment lexicon counts. The SGD classifiers operate on word bag-of-words features and WordNet synset bag-of-words features. Prediction also includes a duplicate check, although the text describes the compared datasets ambiguously. The supplied configuration reportedly scores about 0.65844 and takes approximately three minutes to generate a submission.

solution_title: [0.801 Private, 60th place] Single LGB using 1% of data
solution_summary: The solution used a single LightGBM model trained on one million rows with 220 engineered features, achieving 0.800 public and 0.801 private scores. Its strongest features modeled question-to-question answer relationships, supplemented by user history, question difficulty, timing, and embedding distances. Matching users and content to public Ednet data supplied additional behavioral metadata and roughly six million interactions for initializing question-pair statistics. solution_title: 102nd Place: Local LLM Report Labeling and Anatomy-Informed 2.5D CNNs
solution_summary: The team generated soft finding labels from reports using two local LLMs, repeated responses, and rules for under-reported findings. A localization stage corrected orientation and centered MRI crops before independent plane-specific 2.5D CNNs predicted findings. Anatomical spatial priors, learnable depth attention, and soft top-k feature aggregation were central to the image models. The final ensemble combined four backbones with finding-specific plane weights and achieved 0.962 public and 0.947 private AUC.

solution_title: 6th place solution End to End Sequence to Sequence with sliding window.
solution_summary: The solution used an end-to-end sequence-to-sequence model over CT slices. Sliding windows selected fixed-length sequences from each CT volume, and an LSTM predicted slice labels at each time step. The windowing approach also supported test-time augmentation.

The recognition solution used precomputed embeddings from the train4.1m dataset and penalized embeddings resembling non-landmark images. These recognition-specific strategies improved a single model from 0.37843/0.36045 to 0.45724/0.43252 on public/private scores. The final submission ensembled BEiT, Swin, b4, b6, XCiT, v2m and b5 models. Model training details were deferred to a separate retrieval writeup.

solution_title: 178th Place Solution for the Open Problems – Single-Cell Perturbations
solution_summary: The author combined prediction blends and ridge models using cell type and compound name as features. Biological exploration informed the selection of cell types and compounds expected to have similar responses. Selecting B cells, regulatory T cells, and NK cells helped, while adding CD8 T cells worsened the score. The approach used four-fold cross-validation and per-row RMSE to guide model selection for compounds.

The solution divided the spatial prediction problem into cells and tuned models on a central spatial subset using a chronological holdout. The final ensemble summed probabilities equally across 13 models spanning nearest neighbors, tree methods, naive Bayes, and kernel density estimation. Random hyperparameter search and greedy ensemble selection balanced local performance with model diversity. Bayesian optimization of ensemble weights produced only a negligible improvement, so equal weighting was retained.

solution_summary: The solution combined eight cell classifiers and four whole-image classifiers, averaging their predicted probabilities. It used competition data and HPA public data, with self-supervised learning and asymmetric loss identified as important improvements. Cells inherited whole-image labels during training, while cells with weak green-channel signals were reassigned to class 18. Training all 12 models took about 48 hours on eight 1080Ti GPUs.

solution_summary: The agent repeatedly fitted a bagging classifier to predict the opponent's next move from the preceding five turns of both players. The tree count grew with match progress to keep the training subset per tree roughly constant. It countered predicted moves only when confidence exceeded 70%, otherwise playing randomly. A 200-turn random opening delayed training-data collection and helped obscure its strategy.

The final submission ensembled 55 models spanning U-Net pipelines, recurrent networks, WaveNet, and transformers. Features included normalized movement signals, cyclic hour encodings, signal differences, and downsampled summary statistics. Training benefited from noisy-sample removal, full-data training, exponential moving averages, label smoothing, and combined BCE and peak-specific Dice losses. Postprocessing detected device nonwear and boosted the strongest event candidates within 24-hour periods, improving the reported private score from 0.812 to 0.823.

solution_title: 15th place solution - Dive into compute_f without Grid Generation + Simple 100% KNN Floor
solution_summary: The solution used site-specific TF-IDF KNN models for floor classification and a multistage waypoint ensemble trained with iterative pseudo-labeling. LSTM and convolutional attention models fed convolutional stacking and LightGBM models with temporal and relative-position features, followed by weight optimization and Ridge regression. Repeated geometric postprocessing was central, combining grid snapping, path translation, sensor-based cost minimization, rotation correction, and hallway constraints. The floor model achieved reported 100% accuracy on both public and private data.

For CITE, the author combined log-transformed raw data, complementary dimensionality reductions, and selected gene features in a heterogeneous ensemble. Donor-grouped validation guided a three-layer stack whose reported CV score was 0.89677, with additional independent models included in the ensemble. The custom neural network replaced attention dot products with an MLP, alongside CNN, kernel ridge, and boosting models. For Multiome, the pipeline reduced inputs and normalized targets with truncated SVD, then combined neural and boosting predictions.

solution_summary: The solution represents wells as multichannel TVT-by-MD images and ensembles CNNs with UNet-style decoders. Its central investment was realistic synthetic geology, used for roughly 25 epochs of pretraining before brief fine-tuning on real wells. Auxiliary trajectory reconstruction, sibling-well type-log correction, and larger-canvas reinference improve accuracy and coverage. Cross-validation was more informative than the noisy public scores, although the late MaxViT-base variant encountered a submission-time construction error.

The author focused on limiting overfitting on a small dataset through simple modeling and substantial feature engineering. The final approach used XGBoost with parameters selected through RandomizedSearchCV. Validation used stratified cross-validation, and the reported public score was 0.18.

The main model combined WaveNet blocks, squeeze-and-excitation modules, dense concatenations, and a bidirectional LSTM in PyTorch. Inputs used drift-cleaned, Kalman-filtered, standardized signals together with random-forest probabilities, squared signal, and selected lags. GroupKFold with groups of 4,000 and a predicted test class-10 count check guided experiments and submission selection. Training coordinated macro-F1 checkpointing with cross-entropy loss, learning-rate reductions, and early stopping. The main model achieved 0.94365 local CV and 0.94513 private leaderboard score, while a three-submission vote deteriorated on private evaluation.

solution_title: Solver, ChatGPT 5.5, and Fable Traces for Cryptarithm
solution_summary: The authors replaced cryptarithm examples in an existing synthetic SFT corpus with programmatically generated search traces and teacher-model reasoning. They trained rank-32 LoRA adapters for Nemotron-3-Nano-30B and compared several trace formats, including forward reasoning and standardized teacher explanations. Search improvements expanded candidate coverage, but voting sometimes selected an incorrect answer even when the correct one was available. The authors report that the model failed to learn the procedure and that cryptarithm accuracy did not improve.

The solution combined three EfficientNet-B0 tile models with an EfficientNet-B4 model trained on resized whole images. HSV-based filtering selected useful tissue tiles, which were assembled into patch images; patch construction and binary cross-entropy were reported as the biggest improvements. Training used AdamW, OneCycle scheduling, gradient accumulation, and mixed precision. A weighted ensemble with patch-mode test-time augmentation achieved a private leaderboard score of 0.920, with labels obtained by counting sigmoid outputs above 0.5.

solution_summary: The solution adapted a public notebook into a traceback-driven code repair pipeline. Regex parsing mapped traceback paths and locations to repository code, with LLM-based search retained as a fallback. DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B generated eight repair candidates per issue using git conflict marker edits, which were applied to a temporary repository to produce valid diffs. solution_title: Rank 60 solution: a first-time RL practitioner’s experience
solution_summary: The solution used self-play reinforcement learning for its four-player arm and behavior cloning for its final two-player arm. An autoregressive action head explicitly modeled launch sequences and stopping, producing cleaner decisions at some throughput cost. Local round-robin evaluation against strong prior bots and exploiters guided promotion, while policy visualization exposed action-space bugs. Exploiter training helped disrupt passive four-player self-play behavior and improved first-place rate by roughly 15–17 points in local tests.

solution_summary: The author reports using an ensemble of three different models and applying cross-validation as much as possible. The post links to code and a README for reproducing the best submission, but does not describe the model families or other pipeline details.
