solution_summary: The author builds on a public baseline and uses leaderboard probes to estimate hidden-test prediction bias when local validation is unavailable. Constant prediction shifts and the RMSE identity reveal well-specific biases, with wells identified by row-count rank across reruns. The best scored submission achieved 6.471, while a fully corrected score of about 6.45 was inferred from the probes. Five final submissions carrying corrections completed reruns but never received scores before the deadline.
compute: Approximately 10-hour submission queues near the deadline.

solution_title: 62th Place Solution - Last Value and Rule-based Multiplier
solution_summary: The final approach forecast from each county's last observed target, adjusted for the new year and multiplied by rules based on its five most recent values. Validation reproduced the test horizon using expanding windows, two-month gaps, and three-month validation periods, with extra folds for year transitions. Linear models, boosted trees, autoregressive models, and Bayesian multiplier optimization did not beat the baseline. The rule-based adjustments produced a significant validation improvement, although exact scores were not recalled.

The solution extracted Phikon embeddings from tissue patches and classified slides with an ensemble of Chowder multiple-instance models. Matching TMA patch resolution to WSI resolution and detecting uncertain predictions as the Other class were especially important. The final submission averaged 65 selected and calibrated Chowder models, achieving public/private scores of 0.64/0.66 in approximately six hours. No extra training data or annotations were added.
compute: Final submissions approximately 6 hours; paired image processing on one P100 GPU with 0.5 GPU and 2 CPU cores per process. Experimental Phikon pretraining took 2.5 days per epoch on 2 NVIDIA P100 GPUs.

solution_title: Telstra Network Disruptions - Predict service faults on Australia's largest telecommunications network
solution_summary: The writeup presents a simplified single-model pipeline using XGBoost and separate scripts for feature extraction, feature importance, and submission generation. The supplied parameters are reported to achieve roughly 0.41 on the private leaderboard, with additional tuning potentially reaching 0.405. The author's competition solution also benefited from model averaging, though the component models and averaging details are not specified.

The agent combines a Producer Lite heuristic planner with logistic-regression behavior-cloning priors learned from high-Elo replays. The priors adjust source ranking and target scores, while physics projections and reinforcement-aware capture requirements guide launches. Player-count-specific presets, especially lowering the four-player ROI threshold to 0.90, were the most effective refinements and produced a score of 1109. A neural ranker and transplanted advanced heuristics reduced game performance despite promising offline metrics.
compute: RTX 4090 for experimental ranker training on 40M samples for 10 epochs; final CPU-only inference under 50 ms per turn.

solution_summary: The pipeline retrieved Wikipedia passages, reranked them with a tuned pretrained reranker, and combined multiple question-answering models with Platypus2 and Xwin. Wikipedia extraction was modified to preserve numerical content, and retrieval operated directly on passages. Reranker training used inference-matched passages and hard negatives, providing a substantial improvement. The final submission scored 0.9284 private, while later ablations showed that removing Platypus2 slightly improved performance.
external_data: ["Wikipedia dump", "sugupoko 70k dataset", "radek1 and cdeotte shared datasets"]

solution_summary: The author describes an LKH approach that achieved a score of 74265.771731100400. Four quadrants of a standard configuration were connected with one-pixel side lines, and the route was formulated as a symmetric traveling salesman problem in pixel space. Allowed steps were one or two pixels horizontally and one pixel vertically. The resulting tour was converted to arm configurations, with larger steps handled by splitting seven free configuration elements into two groups and modifying each group.

solution_title: Public 12th / Private 26th Place Solution for the HuBMAP - Hacking the Human Vasculature Competition
solution_summary: The solution ensembled four Mask R-CNN models with Swin-S and Swin-T backbones using MMDetection. Models initialized from COCO weights were first trained on dataset2 and then fine-tuned on dataset1, with whole-slide-separated validation. ROI-level weighted box fusion and weighted mask fusion combined models, flip augmentations, and folds. Masks overlapping glomeruli by more than 90% were removed, while sliding windows, neighboring-tile context, and rotation TTA did not improve the final evaluation.
models_pretrained: ["COCO-pretrained Mask R-CNN models with Swin-S and Swin-T backbones"]

solution_summary: The solution combined public and private AutoML approaches, with gradient boosting models forming a major component. A multi-input neural network run with 25 seeds supplied additional diversity and robustness. The main models were then retrained with high-confidence pseudo-labeled test rows, yielding a small additional improvement.

solution_title: My Solution to this Competition with Code (Score: 0.58655)
solution_summary: The solution first explored and filtered the signals. It then calculated peaks and constructed other engineered features. Multiple models were combined for prediction, but the post provides no model identities, validation details, or numerical results.

The solution stacked 22 models trained on shared four-fold splits. SVR and Ridge used selected embeddings from pretrained models, with SVR achieving a single-model CV of 0.4467. Repeated pseudo labeling and Ridge/LightGBM stacking provided the largest gains. A weighted average of the two stackers achieved CV 0.4423.

The author built a diverse EfficientNet ensemble using shared leak-free folds and selected members and weights through greedy improvement of out-of-fold AUC. Random crops from higher-resolution images and heavy test-time augmentation reduced overfitting and stabilized AUC. The main submission combined eight image models with a metadata model through a geometric mean and achieved CV AUC 0.9505. Additional submissions incorporated public models, with the final weighted blend achieving private AUC 0.9429.
compute: Most models trained using four Nvidia V100 GPUs; 50+ models trained over two months.
external_data: ["2018 and 2019 external image data", "Public model predictions"]

solution_summary: The solution used YOLOv5l6 models trained only on images containing annotated objects, with three-fold validation grouped by video. Rotation augmentation, multiscale training, and image resolution were central to performance. A simple temporal attention-area rule boosted detections overlapping confident boxes from the preceding frame. The final ensemble combined four models across 11 resolution and rotation configurations using WBF, achieving public 0.648 and private 0.737.
compute: Final ensemble was designed to use as much of the 9-hour inference quota as possible.

solution_summary: The system first localized intervertebral keypoints and estimated axial spinal levels, then classified patch sequences with a 2D backbone and encoder-decoder Transformer. Patch-model pretraining substantially improved convergence, and anatomical symmetry allowed training on individual level-sides while evaluating complete studies. Metadata supplied spatial context, and max pooling combined bilateral representations for spinal canal stenosis. Selected submissions used RegNet or HGNet ensembles with test-time augmentation; the best reported private score was 0.4118.

The solution processed remote-sensing imagery with two independent CNN branches, one for RGB and another for altitude, NIR, and NDVI. ImageNet initialization, heavy dropout, and spatial block-label swapping helped the models handle sparse presence-only species labels. Ten ResNet-50, Inception-v4, and DenseNet-201 models were combined using weights derived from prediction variance across test-time augmentations. Architecture selection, label swapping, and ensembling each contributed roughly two percentage points of improvement, while environmental covariates and more elaborate pretraining did not help.
compute: Training distributed across two workstations, each with a 16-core CPU, 128GB RAM, and RTX 3090, plus an HPC system with a Tesla V100.

solution_summary: The solution combined multiclass and multilabel bird classifiers using mel-spectrogram and PCEN inputs. EfficientNet backbones with noisy-student weights dominated, with a SE-ResNet101 model adding diversity. Extensive audio augmentation, class-specific thresholds, and hierarchical averaging supported noisy-label learning. Final checks used spectral statistics and file-versus-chunk predictions to suppress false positives and identify no-call segments.

The agent used an 8-bit LLaMA-3-8B-Inst with a precomputed question tree followed by LLM-generated questions. The answering bot generated a keyword definition and reasoning to reduce ambiguity, while the guesser retained candidate words and previous guesses in memory. Tree depth and other changes were evaluated through local self-play on 200 selected words, with answer prompts also checked against successful game replays. LLaMA-3-8B-Inst outperformed the tested alternatives, while LoRA fine-tuning severely overfit. An emoji-based resource-exhaustion tactic sometimes disrupted opponents but also appeared to cause losses.
compute: Single RTX 4090 GPU

solution_summary: The final approach blended four diverse LightGBM submissions and two heavily modified XdeepFM submissions. Most tree models used 60–70 features, minimal cleanup, and factorized or count-encoded categories, with AvSigVersion removed from most models. Diversity came from feature selection, hyperparameters, folds, and the different model families. The author favored generic models after filtering, feature engineering, and attempts to exploit the time split produced inconsistent results.

The strongest submission combined six folds of a MuRIL Large model adapted to BigBird for longer contexts. The author initialized BigBird from MuRIL, tiled its position embeddings, and continued masked language model pretraining on multilingual mc4 data before staged QA training. XLM-R, MuRIL Large, and RemBERT were also trained, but a cross-model ensemble did not finish within the submission limit. The long-context model achieved private/public scores of 0.756/0.796, making long-context handling the main improvement.
compute: TPU v3-8; base MLM pretraining for 150k steps, large for 90k steps, batch size 1; Kaggle TPUs for RemBERT.

solution_title: Two BERTs are better than one (2nd place solution)
solution_summary: The solution averaged five transformer models with separate question and answer inputs, using dual and siamese architectures with RoBERTa and XLNet backbones. Ordinal binary targets trained with binary cross-entropy were converted into expected values. Grouped validation repeatedly sampled one answer per question and excluded the unstable spelling target from model assessment. Optimized clipping thresholds created ties at prediction extremes, while differential learning rates and warmup supported effective fine-tuning.
compute: V100 for dual RoBERTa-large training with batch size 1 and fp16; final kernel inference close to two hours.

solution_summary: The notebook trains an unconditional convolutional GAN to generate 64×64 dog images from 128-dimensional latent vectors. It filters annotated dog boxes by size and aspect ratio, crops the dogs, and applies random resized crops, horizontal flips, and normalization. Training uses binary cross-entropy, Adam, and softened real labels, while submission generation samples a truncated normal distribution to produce 10,000 images. The introduction reports an earlier CV score of 40.6601 and leaderboard score of 40.49519; although Gaussian noise is announced, the shown loader constructs images from the original crop rather than the computed noisy array.
compute: Earlier run: about 27,500 seconds for 750 epochs; shown training loop: 600 epochs.

solution_summary: The solution used a single LightGBM model with lag, difference, rolling, and calendar features. A custom time-series split supported validation, and the Poisson objective worked better than Tweedie. Optuna tuning was tried but excluded from the final submission in favor of a robust configuration. The reported public and private scores were 0.61444 and 0.60825.

solution_title: 7th place solution (with inference kernel + training code)
solution_summary: The solution combined four global embedding models using two CNN backbones at two image resolutions, taking the geometric mean of their similarities. Training continued from retrieval checkpoints on 3.2 million images, with seesaw loss and higher resolution contributing to a five percentage point local validation improvement. SuperPoint and SuperGlue reranked retrieved candidates after HRNetv2 removed keypoints on irrelevant semantic classes. Local reranking improved public leaderboard scores by four to six percentage points, although its gains were difficult to validate locally.
models_pretrained: ["Landmark retrieval challenge checkpoints", "HRNetv2 pretrained on ADE20k", "SuperPoint and SuperGlue"]

solution_summary: The solution used a single Whisper medium model with beam size four. Training data was cleaned using host-provided metadata, and roughly 80% of the dataset was presented as paired audio combinations to accelerate training and reduce annotation noise effects. SpecAugment, SpecAugment++, and CutOut provided augmentation. Correctly handling audio longer than 30 seconds and sentences longer than 448 tokens improved the leaderboard score from 0.43 to 0.38.

The author describes an ensemble of more than ten XGBoost models, more than ten LightGBM models, and approximately twenty neural networks. Ten-fold out-of-fold predictions were used with Ridge as the second-level model. The best individual XGBoost scored 1115.89595 on the private leaderboard, while the best neural network scored 1122.06610. The post asks why the combined solution underperformed despite competitive individual models.

solution_title: 76th Private/11th Public - CSIRO Biomass Prediction Pipeline
solution_summary: The pipeline combined two S5-based multiple-instance models with an attention-based uncertainty model using DINOv3 embeddings. Multiscale crops, vegetation indices, and SigLIP semantic similarities supplied complementary information. Grouped cross-validation, fold-specific scaling, and test-time augmentation supported the individual models. Per-target ensemble weights and physical constraints improved weighted R² from 0.7865 for simple averaging to 0.7901.

The final solution equally averaged Qwen3-1.7B-base, a triplet-trained BGE encoder, and three DeBERTa-v3 models, all using online learning. Qwen benefited from prompt refinement and LoRA pretraining on roughly 6,000 synthetic examples checked by a second language model. Hard negative mining improved BGE, while cross-rule negative augmentation improved the smaller DeBERTa models. Local validation correlated poorly with leaderboard results, and slower embedding models and a LightGBM stack were discarded.

The solution extended a public baseline with 89 matchup features describing seeds, Elo, GLM team quality, and possession-based team efficiency. A conservative XGBoost regressor predicted score margins, with overtime statistics normalized before season summaries were built. Leave-one-season-out predictions supported separate men's and women's isotonic calibration and light tail sharpening. Seasonal model margins were averaged for submission, achieving reported out-of-fold margin MAE of 9.2418 and calibrated Brier score of 0.16272.

solution_title: [22nd] place solution: Only Wifi Models + Public Post Processing + Pseudo labels
solution_summary: The solution used only Wi-Fi BSSID and RSSI features, with a sequential RNN as its strongest model. Site-specific LSTMs and an MLP added diversity to the ensemble, which scored about 4.8–4.9 before post-processing. Public post-processing methods with optimized cost minimization improved the score to 3.57. Retraining with post-processed test predictions as pseudo-labels and adding those models to the ensemble yielded a final reported score of 3.43.

The team blended predictions from several public notebook pipelines using fixed weights. They identified extreme essay scores as disproportionately important under RMSE and trained a separate LightGBM classifier to detect essays scoring 6.0. Predictions with high classifier confidence were replaced with 5.5, improving the ensemble; the classifier achieved approximately 0.90 ROC AUC.

solution_title: 1st Place solution of category "BigQuery ML Models built in SQL"
solution_summary: The author built a SQL-only solution using BigQuery's basic machine-learning capabilities. Features represented turns, intersection clusters, and population by ZIP code. Separate detailed and general linear-regression models were trained per target, with the general models handling unknown intersections. No cross-validation or grid search was used, and sandbox quotas limited experimentation.
compute: BigQuery sandbox quotas restricted training to a few models per week.

solution_summary: The author used ten repeats of stratified ten-fold validation to guide feature engineering and model selection. Useful features included kidney-failure, sums of pain-related features, and selected polynomial feature pairs. Variance filtering at 0.1 was applied to five classifiers, which were combined in an unweighted ensemble. The final public and private scores were 0.37089 and 0.52302; clustering did not improve validation.

The solution used separate PCA and SVD transformations for cell and gene features, Gaussian rank scaling, and importance-selected raw feature subsets. Two neural models used ResNet and highway fully connected architectures, trained with Adam, label smoothing, and OneCycleLR. Predictions were averaged across two models, three seeds per model, and five folds, producing a reported score of 0.01609. TabNet, convolutional approaches, non-scored-target pretraining, clustering, DeepFM, and autoencoders did not help.

The author log-transformed all input features and combined six tree-based models through hill-climbing ensembling. Adding a Nyström logistic regression model and then a neural network increased diversity and produced incremental leaderboard gains to 0.79101. The selected submission was another ensemble with a slightly higher public score, whose exact composition was not specified. PCA, t-SNE, clustering, and cluster target encoding did not improve performance.

The team used Network Deconvolution to distinguish direct dependencies in inferred networks. They report that it improved almost every adjacency matrix they tried. The author also published a Python implementation alongside the original authors' MATLAB version. The full submission pipeline is deferred to a separate post.

solution_title: 1st Place Solution for the CAFA 6 Protein Function Prediction
solution_summary: GOAlpha combined seven predictors spanning protein sequence, interaction networks, structure, domains, and biomedical literature. An XGBoost learning-to-rank model integrated their scores with GO term frequency and species features. Model selection used 1,000 held-out experimentally annotated proteins sampled to match the test species distribution. Sequence predictors were strongest individually, while structural and literature evidence added complementary signals; the final private score was 0.52430.
compute: Modern GPU servers; component training under one day, inference within one day, final learning-to-rank integration a few hours.
external_data: ["SwissProt, GOA, and GO functional annotations", "Protein-protein interaction network", "Biomedical literature"]

solution_summary: The solution accelerated candidate scoring through batch evaluation, threshold-based individual rescoring, and a persistent cache. Batched simulated annealing searched word permutations with several neighborhood operations, multiple retained candidates, and partial shuffling. For example 4, beam search supplied strong initial sequences for annealing. Combining complementary sequences from two teammates and refining them reduced the example 5 score from roughly 31.2–31.4 to around 30.0.

The solution combined EfficientNetV2-S and HGUNet sound-event detectors with a ProtoSSM branch built on Perch embeddings. Pretraining on birds and non-birds substantially improved coverage, while carefully selected soft pseudo labels improved training further. Rank blending, temporal and contextual gates, and taxonomic smoothing combined the branches. The selected configuration reported a public score of 0.960, with CPU inference taking approximately 60 minutes.
compute: NVIDIA A100; approximately 8 hours per fold across 4 folds; Kaggle CPU inference approximately 60 minutes.

solution_summary: The author selected two separate notebooks representing marker-based exfiltration and a one-step email confused-deputy attack. The competition took the maximum score of the selected notebooks rather than blending them. Marker-based exfiltration collapsed to zero privately, whereas the confused-deputy notebook transferred from 29.730 publicly to 29.670 privately. Hybrid attack families failed on both evaluations, making separate notebook selection decisive.

solution_title: 2nd Place - Stacking Transformer and Linear Regression
solution_summary: The final approach stacked a transformer on a linear regression model by training it to predict the regression residuals and summing their predictions. The regression used sinusoidal calendar features and effects for GDP, store, product, country, and holidays. The author also described a standalone transformer improved with two rounds of pseudo-labeling and median aggregation across five seeds. Choosing the future annual trend multiplier was particularly consequential; the final submission choices used a constant 1.06 multiplier and a mildly increasing linear multiplier. The stacked model achieved a private score of 0.04498.

The solution combined log-mel spectrograms, temporal waveform statistics, and clip length with a nine-layer CNN. Axis-specific pooling treated time and frequency differently, and some models included squeeze-and-excitation blocks and highway connections. Training used noisy-data pretraining, label smoothing, mixup, random five-second crops, and padding, followed by three-way test-time augmentation. A neural stacker learned class-specific ensemble weights and label correlations, improving CV from 0.89763 for a single model to 0.9108.

The solution ensembles modified RNAdegformer models, a convolutional model with residual base-pair-probability attention and bidirectional LSTMs, and a Transformer with BPP attention bias. RNA sequences and EternaFold BPP matrices provide the main inputs, with ContraFold used in some variants. Training first uses a lower signal-to-noise threshold and then fine-tunes on cleaner examples; predicted reactivity errors also guide pseudo-label selection. Five-fold validation gives the best individual model a CV score of 0.11976 and a private score of 0.14124.

The team ensembled segmentation networks with classification predictions to suppress false positives. Segmentation models used EfficientNet and SE backbones with FPN, LinkNet, and U-Net architectures, while classification was handled through a segmentation network with an additional fully connected head. Classification thresholds and class-specific mask-size filtering produced approximately 0.670 out-of-fold Dice and 0.6783 public leaderboard score. Restoring masks for otherwise empty predictions and taking mask unions increased the public score to 0.6800. An abandoned ensemble variant ultimately achieved their best reported private score of 0.67254 but was not selected.

The solution used a modified DeepAR LSTM network trained with Tweedie loss and recursive 28-day forecasts during training. Inputs combined sales lags and moving averages with calendar, event, price, category, SNAP, and zero-sales features. Checkpoints were selected by their mean WRMSSE across 14 historical periods because scores varied substantially across time. Final predictions combined 43 models, including models trained with and without dropout; alternative architectures, losses, and forecast reconciliation did not improve the approach.

The solution blended separate study classifiers and image detectors using only competition data in its final pipeline. Nine study models across five folds used cross-entropy classification with auxiliary U-Net segmentation, while EfficientDet and YOLO provided bounding boxes. Detection outputs were fused with weighted boxes fusion, and the none score combined box confidence with negative and atypical study probabilities. Study-grouped validation and auxiliary tasks supported generalization; unified classification-detection models were competitive but slightly weaker than separate models.

The author trained LightGBM, CatBoost, and XGBoost regressors using ideas from public notebooks. They then averaged five models, including contributions from public GAM approaches, reaching a public score of 6.58 and a private score of 7.44. Rounding predictions and adding one to every prediction further improved the public score to 5.596 and the private score to 6.47.

The system converted silence-trimmed audio into normalized mel-spectrograms and combined a custom CNN with VGG16 batch normalization. Its four-stage warm-up pipeline moved from noisy data to curated data and then selectively reincorporated reliable noisy samples. SpecMix replaced time and frequency regions between samples, with targets weighted by the contributed pixels. Predictions were averaged across training stages, architectures, and overlapping audio windows; the supplied notebooks achieved public lwlrap of 0.738.
compute: Nvidia RTX 2080 ti, Intel Core i7 4790k, 24 GB RAM; public-test inference under 1000 seconds

solution_summary: The solution combined a raw-waveform HGNetB0 model, a mel-spectrogram EfficientNetB0 model, and a model concatenating both feature streams. Training used random five-second clips, mixup, and binary cross entropy, with spectrum cutout augmentation. A weighted ensemble achieved 0.743960 public and 0.687173 private scores, and inference used OpenVINO.

The solution used an iteratively annotated YOLOv5 detector to crop salient whale bodies before training identity embedding models. ImageNet-pretrained EfficientNet and NFNet backbones used GeM pooling, BNNeck, and ArcFace or AdaFace, with texture-focused augmentation and mixup to reduce overfitting. Iterative pseudo-labeling progressively expanded training data and incorporated body and part models. Concatenated embeddings and cross-fold submission merging produced an ensemble, with reported leaderboard performance reaching 0.886 during pseudo-label iterations.

The solution generated extensive synthetic seismic data by forward modeling blended velocity maps and trained a modified EVA02 Vision Transformer. Its architecture separated early intra-channel processing from later shared processing and decoded spatial predictions with pixel shuffle. Muon with auxiliary AdamW improved optimization, followed by three training stages with increasing resolution and final training on validation data. A weighted blend of stage models used clipping and rounding; correcting an inference preprocessing mismatch yielded public/private scores of 7.96/7.99.
compute: More than 13 TB storage and approximately 5.5 days on 4× A100 SXM 80G.

solution_summary: The post thanks the organizers and expresses appreciation for the Santa competition format. It links to a GitHub repository containing code and an English/Japanese solution explanation. The provided text contains no technical description of the approach.

The solution centered on recovering leaked targets through ordered row and column relationships. The author identified 100 useful column sets of length 40, yielding 7,841 leaky test rows. For the machine-learning component, they used Emmanuel Perry's public kernel reported at 1.37 on the leaderboard. Other modeling experiments and additional column sets were not retained or offered little benefit.

The author describes their detector, image-level prediction, and post-processing contribution to a team solution. Pseudo-labels from the public test set, BIMCV, and RICORD improved the reported YOLOv5x opacity cross-validation score to 0.53870. Data cleaning removed side-view images and validation-related duplicates, while post-processing fused boxes and adjusted confidence using image-level probabilities. The final submission combined Yolotrs-384, Yolov5x-640, and a pseudo-label-trained Yolov5x-512, all with test-time augmentation.

solution_title: My engineering approach to the problem. #49
solution_summary: The author uses a baseline model after abandoning attempts to train their own. Training-set embeddings are precomputed and stored in SQLite to accelerate evaluation. Embeddings from an Open Images subset act as a non-landmark filter, reducing the remaining dataset by about tenfold. The approach scored around 0.6 in tests on 2019 competition data, but transferred less successfully to this contest, and SIFT local scoring offered little benefit.

solution_title: 21st - A Bag of Words is All You Need
solution_summary: The model represented each notebook cell as a single token, disregarding sentence grammar. Cell embeddings came from sparse-dense multiplication of TF-IDF matrices and word or word-ngram embeddings, enabling global attention across every cell in a document. The BERT-like architecture optionally biased attention using an identity matrix or character-ngram similarity. Training took about 20 minutes per epoch, and the highest-scoring notebook used no external data.
compute: About 20 minutes per training epoch; hardware unspecified.

solution_title: 3rd place, team Dmitry&Leustagos, members: Lucas Silva, Dmitry Efimov
solution_summary: The solution trains several model families, including gradient boosting, random forests, logistic regression, glmnet models, and libFM factorization machines. Training scripts indicate multiple feature variants, including frequency and occurrence representations. Models are trained in two successive groups and then combined by a final ensembling script to produce test predictions. The post mainly documents the software environment and execution sequence, without reporting evaluation scores or ensemble details.
compute: Windows 7 Professional x64 or Ubuntu 12.04; hardware and runtime unspecified.

solution_title: We were late for seconds, please accept our writeup
Throughput and Survival: A Source-Verified Model of the JED Attack Benchmark
solution_summary: The author inspected the shipped evaluator and selected attacks using a locally constructed battery of plausible hidden guardrails. The final entry paired a confused-deputy submission with a marker-exfiltration hedge, prioritizing transfer across defenses over public scores. Model-specific prompts minimized generated output so more independent candidates could be replayed within the evaluation budget. The selected deputy scored 24.99 publicly and 25.02 privately, while marker submissions scoring above 90 publicly collapsed to zero privately.

The author built two compact 1D CNN variants with residual connections and dilated and standard convolutions. Training used mixup, while preprocessing diversity came from two bandpass frequency ranges. Averaging the CNN variants and preprocessing variants improved performance, and training on the whole dataset raised the public score further. Stacking with a public-notebook CQT model produced a reported public score of 0.8836.

The final submission averaged several variations of a stacked prediction pipeline. The second-level model was ridge regression, using both out-of-fold predictions and predictions on training examples. Gaussian noise reduced overfitting in this blending stage, while Optuna optimized ridge regularization and feature scales. The final submission scored 0.15665 publicly and 0.15741 privately.

solution_title: 6th place solution - with a visualization of our Jaccard scores over time
solution_summary: The team emphasized architecture diversity and public leaderboard feedback because local cross-validation appeared unreliable. They mapped model logits to character positions so models with different tokenizers could be combined, and normalized logits to account for scale differences. The final weighted ensemble combined Roberta Large, Muril Large, Rembert Large, Xlm Info Large, and Wechsel models. This progression improved the public score from 0.785 for the initial XLM Roberta Large approach to 0.821.
models_pretrained: ["XLM Roberta Large", "Muril Base", "Muril Large", "Rembert Large", "Xlm Info Large", "Wechsel"]

solution_summary: The solution predicted sentence discourse types using Persuade 2.0 annotations and inserted those labels into essays before training neural scoring models. This structural information improved individual models by approximately 0.005–0.006 on both cross-validation and the leaderboard. DeBERTa and Longformer models with varied pooling supplied out-of-fold predictions to a LightGBM stacker alongside essay statistics, spelling-error counts, and features from a previous competition model. Validation balanced scores and topics across four folds, and three LightGBM seeds were blended for stability. The reported stack achieved 0.85891 CV and 0.835 private score, although later analysis suggested stronger performance on Persuade-derived data than on Kaggle-only data.
models_pretrained: ["DeBERTA-v3-small", "DeBERTa-v3-Large", "DeBERTa-Large", "DeBERTa-Base", "Longformer-large-4096", "bigbird-roberta-large", "funnel-large", "Team turing's Feedback Prize - English Language Learning model"]
compute: Discourse prediction initially took around 1 hour for four small-model folds; one large-model fold took another hour. Increasing sentence inference batch size from 1 to 32 reduced inference time to under 20 minutes.

solution_summary: The final solution ensembled XGBoost, LightGBM, a neural network, a field-aware factorization machine, a regularized greedy forest, and public models. Predictions were combined using a geometric mean. The author reported component scores between 280 and 284 and found feature engineering difficult to improve.

solution_title: My solution for the RSNA 2024 Lumbar Spine Degenerative Classification, using only the competition data
solution_summary: The pipeline used YOLO to locate lumbar spine levels and guide condition-specific cropping. Spinal canal coordinates identified the three closest axial slices and established left and right directions in sagittal images. Dedicated EfficientNetB0 backbones processed spinal canal, neural foraminal, and subarticular image groups, with a dense network predicting severity for five categories. The shared pretrained model was then fine-tuned separately for each lumbar spine level.

solution_title: Getting to Rank 25 by Teaching LLMs to Golf
solution_summary: The author used Claude, GPT-5, and Gemini agents to develop and shorten Python solutions for ARC tasks. The final workflow combined task descriptions based on Anchors, Clues, and Transforms with an expanding checklist of code-golf tricks, structured design reviews, and iterative testing. A grammar of grid transformations further constrained solution search toward reusable compact patterns. Approximately 370 problems were primarily golfed by agents, and solutions for at least three problems beat the leaderboard best during the final week.
frameworks_libraries: ["Claude Code", "Gemini Canvas", "GPT5 Codex", "Codex on the Web"]

solution_summary: The solution ensembled seven image-to-sequence models with EfficientNet encoders and LSTM decoders. Training incorporated millions of RDKit-rendered extra molecules, image morphology augmentations, small rotations, and border cropping. Beam search generated candidate strings, which were normalized with RDKit before majority voting and validity-based fallback. The final submission scored 1.32 on the public leaderboard and 1.31 on the private leaderboard.
compute: Local machine with a Quadro RTX 6000 GPU.

solution_summary: The solution uses a flat classifier that first retrieves candidate classes by cosine similarity to class centroids, then applies a separate logistic regression classifier to each candidate. Training examples are assigned to nearby candidate classes to construct the binary classifiers' datasets. Text features use a modified TF-IDF weighting followed by L2 normalization. The combined classifier achieved LBMaF 0.33025, compared with 0.28931 for the nearest-centroid baseline and 0.23088 for k-NN.
compute: 32GB RAM required; prefetch may exceed 15 hours. Reported NCC+BC training time is 15 hours and prediction time is 2 hours.

solution_summary: The author links code for their competition algorithm but gives little detail about the method. They report using the small-image version of the dataset because they started late. They expect better results at the original image size, but provide no supporting experiment or score.

The author shares a notebook about searching for blending weights with Optuna. The post identifies automated blend-weight tuning as its approach. It provides no details about the component models, validation, or achieved results.

The solution combined an ensemble predicting unsafe outcomes with another ensemble ranking event cases, using a probability formula to combine them. The author defined the unsafe target using an event-time cutoff and trained the ranking models on logit-transformed ranks. Logit adjustments and scaling improved the final scores, alongside many AutoGluon models and additional target ensembles. Feature changes were limited to HLA sum recalculation, preserving an unusually informative original column, and rounding age features.

The selected submission combined ResNeXt50, EfficientNet-B3, and ViT models trained with five folds and additional 2019 data. Training used image augmentation, Adam, and cosine annealing after warmup, while heavier test-time augmentation worked best for this submission. It scored 0.8984 on the private leaderboard. An unselected, lighter ResNeXt50 and EfficientNet-B1 submission with light test-time augmentation scored 0.8993; SnapMix, CutMix, and pseudo-labeling did not help.

The pipeline used 3D organ segmentation followed by organ-specific classification pipelines. Liver, kidney, and spleen shared a sequence model, while bowel and extravasation used two-stage training with image-level supervision and frozen feature extractors. Series selection based on aortic attenuation, segmentation-guided crops, and metric-weighted losses were important design choices. Multiplicative post-processing tuned on out-of-fold predictions improved mean CV loss from 0.3994 to 0.3889.

solution_title: What is the secret of getting 0.9363015?
solution_summary: The team optimized gift assignments with Google OR-Tools min-cost max-flow over roughly 100 gift types per run to fit memory. A repeated repair procedure fixed twins and triplets assigned different gifts by reserving their chosen gifts and rerunning flow for the remaining children. Larger optimization blocks made that repair unstable or nonterminating. They also tried mixed-integer programming over about 40 gift types per run, but improvement stopped at 0.9356.
compute: Approximately 16 GB memory; including all unhappy edges exceeded available memory.

solution_summary: The author formulated gift matching as an integer program resembling a transportation model. Assignment variables were restricted to twin-related pairs and pairs appearing in child or gift preference lists to keep the model manageable. Penalized slack variables represented assignments outside those preference lists, and objective coefficients were scaled to integers. The implementation used C++ with Gurobi, with an MPS export supplied for compatibility with other solvers.

solution_title: Solution from Dawnbreaker on steroids in top-40
solution_summary: The solution ensembled ResNet50, DenseNet121, DenseNet169, and SE-ResNext models trained with random crops and horizontal flips. A separate ResNet50 classifier detected non-landmarks using manually labeled examples. The four-network ensemble scored 0.159 on the public leaderboard, compared with 0.139 for three networks. A late distance-based penalty for recognition classes added about 0.002 to the score.

solution_title: 14th Place Solution : pretrained with pseudo labels
solution_summary: The final solution averaged four DeBERTa and ELECTRA model configurations with equal weights using character-level predictions. Its main improvement came from pseudo-labels, used both for intermediate pretraining followed by supervised fine-tuning and for expanding each fold's training data. Training included mixup, random masking, multi-sample dropout, and memory-saving optimization techniques. The selected submission achieved a private score of 0.892; the authors acknowledged some residual pseudo-label leakage in the final CV score of 0.898527.

solution_title: Creatures of Habit:  Neil Schneider on placing second in the dunnhumby Shopper Challenge
solution_summary: The approach modeled customer spending separately by weekday to capture habitual differences in shopping behavior. Spend predictions targeted the highest-density spending ranges rather than conventional regression estimates. SAS handled data manipulation and range construction, while R's gbm package supplied boosted regression models. Inventory-control time series methods and ordinary regression performed poorly.

The solution extended a shared baseline with improved answer parsing and repeated-generation voting. It stopped iterations early when the leading answer had sufficient support, transferring saved effort to later problems. Experiments supported allocating about 20–21 iterations to half the problems and 10–11 to the rest. Student–teacher validation, early difficulty identification, and multiple-choice follow-up rounds were explored but did not produce stable validation and public leaderboard results.

The final submission combined EfficientNetV2-M and EfficientNet-B3 classifiers with YOLO-M and YOLO-X detectors for model diversity. Tuning data augmentation was the main breakthrough in controlling overfitting after a prolonged period of unsuccessful experiments. The four-model ensemble matched the reported LB 6.29 and PB 6.15 scores of the EfficientNetV2-M plus YOLO-X configuration with test-time augmentation. Classification augmentation and YOLO-X hyperparameters remained incompletely tuned.

The author modified an existing ensemble pipeline by replacing stratified folds with multilabel stratified folds. This improved individual model performance but reduced ensemble performance on both public and private scores. They suggested that greater randomness in validation splits might provide more useful ensemble diversity.

solution_title: [5th solution]: Ensemble of CNN1d, Transformer, Mamba models
solution_summary: The solution treated molecular strings as character sequences and ensembled CNN1D, transformer, and Mamba models for three-target multilabel prediction. A small convolution learned character combinations, while tuned batch normalization was particularly important for the large-batch CNN. Different architectures used different folds to improve ensemble diversity within the training budget. Post-competition comparisons suggested that the transformer was the most robust architecture.

Validation followed Radek’s CV strategy, and online training combined train_v1, train_v2, and valid. solution_title: Open sourcing my solution [2D Model, PyTorch]
solution_summary: The team combined 2D images with DICOM metadata to help identify the vertebrae present in each slice. They engineered slice-position features and used geometric, brightness, and distortion augmentations. Training used a cosine schedule with warmup and restarts, and the best submission used six epochs. Segmentation, region-of-interest cropping, and 2.5D modeling were suggested as future improvements.

DMD2's model-card demo provided a strong starting point, with simple parameter adjustments adding approximately 0.02 and showing good stability. solution_title: Sparrow for square packing | 108th Place Solution
solution_summary: The solution selected packing strategies by configuration size, using unrestricted angle optimization for N ≤ 100, CMA-ES optimization of two orientations for N between 120 and 130, and public baselines elsewhere. Modified Sparrow and jagua-rs supported square packing by minimizing the larger dimension, first expanding the smaller dimension and then shrinking both uniformly. A custom C++ simulated annealing implementation further refined small configurations. The final submission improved 67 of 200 configurations and reported a 0.175% improvement over the public baseline.

The author built a hill-climbing ensemble of public notebook approaches, averaged across five seeds and ten-fold cross-validation. Essay reconstruction and word-, sentence-, and paragraph-level length and frequency aggregates improved validation and leaderboard performance. Classification models, synthetic augmentation, oversampling, and several activity-based features did not help. The approach achieved approximately 0.594 CV but suffered a private leaderboard shakeup.

The solution combined a 384×384 Swin Transformer with a larger patchwise TNT model trained on roughly 13 million images, including synthetic renderings of approved extra InChIs. Eight models were ensembled at each decoding step, balancing total weights equally between the two architectures. Beam search with width 16 improved the reported leaderboard score from 0.63 to 0.60, with expensive decoding restricted to about 20,000 images where models disagreed. RDKit validation postprocessing provided a small additional benefit.

LSTM and SAKT training used a custom cross-entropy objective with nearby-area penalties, AdamW, and staged cosine learning-rate schedules. Events were grouped using line-fit predictions and metadata so each group could receive different ensemble weights. Expanding from six to thirteen groups improved the reported leaderboard score to 0.974, with a private score of 0.975.

The solution averaged class probabilities from a default LightGBM, a small neural network, and an autoencoder-based classifier. All input features were standardized without feature engineering. The autoencoder's encoder was frozen before adding classification layers, and the final predictions selected the three highest averaged probabilities. Training used 640×640 images, rotation, crop and dropout augmentations, a polynomial learning-rate schedule, and equally weighted Dice and binary cross-entropy losses. The ensemble scored 0.869 privately and 0.883 publicly; an EfficientNet-based U-Net and an ensemble with an older SSFormer version were evaluated but excluded.

solution_summary: The pipeline restricted CT studies to images before the 400th image and trained EfficientNet-B5 and B3 image models using preprocessed labels. Their features fed multiple sequence models, with sequences subsampled to 200 steps and a deconvolution module maintaining the same CV score as 400-step inputs. LightGBM, Conv1D, and GRU models provided stacking. A heuristic label-consistency postprocess improved CV and public results by 0.002, while the reported private score changed from 0.160 to 0.162.

The final predictor was a weighted ensemble of LightGBM, XGBoost, histogram gradient boosting, random forest, and logistic regression. Ensemble weights were chosen from cross-validation scores, while SVM and linear regression were excluded because they reduced validation performance. Validation grouped observations by season and used a historical training cutoff, with later seasons serving as a test period. Additional features were derived from variables with high LightGBM importance.

Training uses approximately 120,000 generated and participant-shared examples, with varied rewrite instructions and dataset genres. Sentence T5 embedding differences identify tone words, while spaCy supplies content-related words for further customization. At inference, the outputs of the two approaches are concatenated.

solution_title: [Summary] 42nd place - What I did briefly, Single Model
solution_summary: The author trained raster-based ResNet models and selected ResNet34 and ResNet50 as the final submissions. ResNet34 reached a public score of 15.080, while longer training brought ResNet50 to 16.076. ResNet50 performed better on the private leaderboard despite its worse public score, illustrating the mismatch between validation and leaderboard behavior. Averaging predictions with a Polyak-averaged model helped experimentally, but an ensemble was not selected.

The solution blended large BigBird, Longformer, DeBERTa, DeBERTa-v2, DeBERTa-v3, and BART models using Optuna-tuned weights and thresholds. Models predicted seven discourse classes, a no-span class, and a separate span-start output instead of BIO tags. Token dropout reduced overfitting, and sequences of up to 1250 tokens worked well. Shorter-context models benefited from extending positional embeddings by repeating them two or three times, while much longer sequences provided little benefit.

solution_title: ARYA PRAMAN (PSLQ-Arya-1): A Resource-Constrained Multi-Agent Reasoning System

Its selection cascade combined consensus thresholds, diversity filtering, and entropy-weighted arbitration, with additional sampling driven by disagreement. FP8 KV-cache storage and runtime optimizations enabled long-context inference on one H100 80GB GPU. The submission scored 41.5/50 privately; PSLQ variants were excluded from the final system, and verification-heavy experiments performed worse under confounded budget and temperature changes.

solution_title: 1st place solution - Ensemble of diverse Deberta architectures and postprocessing
solution_summary: The solution ensembled DeBERTa token classifiers trained with public synthetic essays and an additional generated dataset. Architectural diversity came from multi-sample dropout, BiLSTM heads, and knowledge distillation, which improved CV and leaderboard scores by roughly 0.005–0.01. A weighted voting ensemble combined ten models in seven groups, with weights and voting thresholds optimized on out-of-fold predictions. Label-specific thresholds and extensive rule-based span repair were central to the final improvement.

The solution combined ViT-Huge and Swin-Large embedding models trained on multiple image datasets. Models used ArcFace or Multi Similarity Loss with CrossBatchMemory, with frozen-backbone projector training for ViT and staged fine-tuning for Swin. The final ensemble used PCA fitted on a selected competition-distributed dataset, which worked better than using the full dataset. The reported final private/public scores were 0.667/0.654.

solution_title: #16 place solution and some questions about it.
solution_summary: The solution combines 25 first-level models built with XGBoost, LightGBM, Keras, and scikit-learn gradient boosting using 10-fold cross-validation. Power and logarithmic target transformations were used, with the power transformation performing better. A second stacking level added the mean prediction and two original features, while seed bagging improved selected models. The final BFGS-optimized weighted average combined first- and second-level models, achieving an out-of-bag score of 1115.66 and a private leaderboard score of 1111.38.

The solution combined cleaned, case-preserving text with concatenated GloVe, fastText, and Paragram embeddings and several text statistics. A unidirectional LSTM and GRU supplied attention and pooled representations to a dense classifier. The model was trained over five folds for four epochs and achieved 0.688 CV and 0.700 public leaderboard scores. The author selected it for its stronger validation reliability despite having other models with better leaderboard scores.

The solution combined extensive used-car feature engineering with an AutoGluon weighted ensemble. Features captured engine specifications, luxury brands, categorical interactions, rare categories, and mileage relative to vehicle age. CatBoost and LightGBM regressors were explored with Optuna, but AutoGluon gave the best results. Additional data further improved the score, although its source and the numerical results were not specified.

solution_summary: The author trained separate spectrogram, waveform-image, and raw-waveform models on examples with at least ten annotator votes to better match the expert opinions represented in the test set. These models supplied blended pseudo-labels for lower-vote examples, after which their embeddings were fused into a single model trained on both groups with extra weight on high-vote data. Waveform preprocessing, waveform-level augmentation, random sampling within EEG recordings, and individual learning-rate tuning supported the approach. The fused model achieved CV 0.246, public LB 0.243, and private LB 0.290; the final submission combined it with additional models.

The final submission ensembled a multiplicative model, a multiplicative linear regression approach, and predictions from a shared transformer. Leap-year corrections and prediction multipliers, particularly for Kenya, were important adjustments to the first model. The regression approach decomposed daily sales into yearly, store, and product fractions, using sine and cosine features for product shares. solution_title: Kaggle Humpback Whale Identification Challenge 2019 2nd place code
solution_summary: The approach trained ResNet101, SE-ResNet101, and SE-ResNeXt101 models on cropped whale images at two resolutions with ArcFace, triplet, and focal losses. Augmentation included treating horizontally flipped whales as additional identities. High-confidence pseudo labels for rare identities improved individual models. The final submission used a weighted average of ten checkpoints and achieved a private leaderboard score of 0.97209.

solution_summary: The team selected a rescaled gradient-boosting submission and a second submission averaging gradient-boosting and convolutional models. The neural pipeline used sliding-window features for a 1D CNN and STFT inputs for a 2D CNN, with signal cleaning and several augmentations. Validation grouped samples by earthquake and later balanced quake groups manually by time-to-failure distribution. Neural out-of-fold MAE was approximately 1.93 and 2.00; the reported submission scores are inconsistent with the later ensemble comparison.

The team combined a transformer regression ensemble with a separately described pairs model. The regression ensemble blended RoBERTa-large, Funnel-large, DeBERTa-large, ELECTRA-large, and RoBERTa-base, using CLS representations and a two-layer regression head. Small learning rates, cosine scheduling, differential layer learning rates, and selective masked-language-model pretraining helped, while weak folds were retrained with adjusted settings. The regression approach scored 0.457 on the private leaderboard, and combining it with the pairs approach improved that to 0.452.

This second part of the solution describes regression models, including RNNs, trained only on the 17,690 training observations. TF-IDF fitting nevertheless incorporated test-set information. Final continuous predictions were rounded using the original coefficients from artgor. Direct use of test data in tree models and several alternative sequence representations did not help.

The submission used three attacks to target the scoring models separately. The author identified positive, negative, writing-related, and model-specific words that destabilized scores, then removed them from the random word pool. They also deliberately used biased word sets in attack prompts. For one attack, the final submission drew from complete prompts that had performed best during experiments.

The author initially used a public DRfold-no-MSA notebook, focusing on running the code and converting predicted XYZ coordinates. They later adopted Proteinx code, reformatted the training data and fine-tuned the model while experimenting with learning rate and crop length. The final submission used the best observed fine-tuning result, although the exact settings were not recorded. Random sequence masking and sliding-window inference for long sequences were proposed but not implemented.

The author combined publicly pretrained RoBERTa-base and RoBERTa-large models after unsuccessful attempts at pretraining. Replacing the base model's linear prediction layer with fold-specific SVR models slightly improved scores, while six large models diversified by pooling and random seed improved further. Adding other public notebook and dataset contributions produced public and private scores of 0.457.

The solution trained separate BERT-base models for question-only input and combined question-answer input. Text preprocessing decoded HTML entities and retained head and tail portions when trimming long inputs. Training used three GroupKFold folds, three epochs, and a combination of binary cross-entropy and margin ranking loss. A LightGBM stacker combined predictions with metadata such as text length, achieving CV 0.3851 and private score 0.41440.

The submission combined 70 dropout neural networks trained in double precision on a GTX Titan GPU. Training took one day and prediction about an hour, while tests suggested that 8–16 networks performed nearly as well. The submission achieved public and private scores of 3.78457 and 3.80581, with cross-validation estimates around 3.82–3.85.

solution_summary: The solution decomposed sales into store, product, country GDP share, weekday, and holiday effects. Product seasonality was fitted with a two-year Fourier series, while holiday multipliers extended up to nine days after each holiday. Annual totals were estimated from GDP with a correction to Kenya's GDP and manually chosen yearly multipliers informed by leaderboard probing. solution_title: [Argus] 14th place solution with full PyTorch pipeline

Biharmonic padding and crop, flip, and color augmentation supported training with a modified Lovasz hinge objective and staged learning-rate schedules. The submission averaged models trained on random folds and mosaic-grouped folds. Mosaic reconstruction, histogram matching, neighboring-mask extrapolation, corner inpainting, and hole filling provided substantial post-processing, while careful validation limited leaderboard overfitting.

The pipeline first selected valuable WSI tiles using a segmentation model, then classified selected tiles with ConvNeXt models; TMA images used a center crop. Tile-selection supervision combined classification confidence with tumor confidence from helper models. External tissue datasets supplied an Other class, and confidence-based pseudo-labeling refined tile training data. Stain normalization, test-time augmentation, and multiscale ensembling helped, while the selected submission excluded EVA02 and scored 0.61 on both public and private evaluations.

solution_title: 8th place solution ... close but no cigar

Sequence cutout was the most important augmentation, alongside mirroring and rotation. Preprocessing included sequence interpolation, body-part normalization, forward-filled temporal deltas, and joint angles. Models trained in PyTorch were converted through ONNX to TensorFlow Lite, with a half-to-float conversion improving inference speed. A promising sequence-wide normalization change failed during submission, while CNN alternatives were unsuccessful or too slow.

The solution combined smaller text models with a large language model, with most development focused on BGE. Multi-fold ensembling and test-time augmentation generated ensemble predictions for pseudo-labeling and a second training round, producing a reported score of 0.911 in two and a half hours. Additional components adapted public DeBERTa, FAISS-based GTE and E5, and Llama approaches. The author avoided synthetic data because of concerns about ambiguous comment labels.
compute: BGE approach achieved a reported score of 0.911 in two and a half hours; hardware unspecified.

solution_summary: The author shares a kernel demonstrating ensembling for cloud segmentation using mlcomp and catalyst. The post identifies ensembling as the approach but gives no model or training details. It reports no validation scores or competition results.

The solution ensembled DetectoRS with ResNet50 and UniverseNet+GFL with Res2Net101 using MMDetection. Heavy augmentation, reconstructed puzzle crops, external SPIKE data, and one round of confidence-filtered pseudo-labeling improved generalization. Inference combined six test-time views and fused rank-scaled detection scores with weighted boxes fusion. Validation grouped images by reconstructed puzzle, but weak correlation with leaderboard results led the team to emphasize public scores; the final submission scored 0.7262 private and 0.7734 public.
compute: Access to GPU servers provided through a HOSTKEY grant; hardware unspecified.

solution_summary: The post shares a link to a final-script notebook and congratulates participants. It reports a public leaderboard score of 0.919 and a private score of 0.917. No modeling pipeline or methodological explanation is provided in the post itself.

The author analyzed the official SDK, scoring predicates, tool-call parsers, and replay limits to develop reliable attack-candidate generation. Public optimization combined model-specific prompt formatting, stable-prefix cache reuse, and live candidate filling constrained by replay cost. The final Best-of-2 selection paired a dictionary-key exfiltration route with an independent confused-deputy email route to hedge against hidden guardrail changes. The exfiltration variant scored 92.090 publicly but zero privately, while the fallback scored 27.270 in both environments.

The approach iteratively improved test pseudo-labels using two LightGBM regressors. The first learned from the pseudo-labeled test set, and its errors on the labeled training set became targets for the second model. Predictions of those errors were added back to the test pseudo-labels at a learning rate of 0.2, with iterations continued while the score improved.

solution_title: 34th place, thoughts on CV and Target Encoding in R
solution_summary: The final pipeline used two LightGBM models, with the second consuming features derived from the first model's predictions. Core features measured grouped click counts, unique counts, and time to the next click, calculated over training data plus the test supplement. High-confidence prediction thresholds supplied proxy targets for grouped attribution statistics, improving the reported score from 0.9806 to 0.9816. Validation trained on days 7 and 8 and evaluated on day 9 before retraining on all data with the same boosting rounds.
compute: Experimented with AWS virtual machines; specifications and runtime were not stated.

solution_summary: The solution used LightGBM with a Tweedie objective, fitting separate models for each store and forecast week. It relied on general time-series, price and calendar features without recursive prediction features. Five temporal holdouts guided validation, and training did not use early stopping. The author prioritized a practical, memory-efficient approach without stacking, blending, postprocessing, multipliers or leaks, despite substantial variation across validation periods.

solution_title: 138th Place Solution for the AI Village Capture the Flag @ DEFCON31 Competition
solution_summary: The author solved a collection of capture-the-flag tasks using exploratory analysis, embedding visualization, adversarial image manipulation, and tailored prompts. Elbow analysis and t-SNE addressed clustering challenges, while pretrained word vectors helped identify semantic targets. Several language-model challenges yielded flags through carefully worded requests, and image pixel replacement revealed a hidden message. Library adversarial attacks failed to satisfy one image challenge, leading the author to implement a custom attack.

The solution combined model-specific adversarial prompts with essays designed to receive either low or high baseline scores. Greedy Coordinate Gradient produced a successful attack against Llama 3.1, while spelled-out numerical representations targeted other judges without affecting Llama. Essays consisted of either 70 sampled positive words or Qwen-generated text, and submission experiments selected seed 42 for the final split.

solution_title: Personalized Medicine: Redefining Cancer Treatment with deep learning
solution_summary: The author compares document classification models using medical text together with gene and mutation information. The pipeline cleans paper-specific references, encodes numbers and variants as symbols, augments documents by deleting sentences, and trains domain-specific Word2Vec embeddings supplemented with Wikipedia gene definitions. Experiments include Doc2Vec, GRU variants, a CNN–GRU model, and hierarchical attention conditioned on gene and variant embeddings. Combining the first and last portions of documents performed best among the sequence configurations, but the supplied text ends before the detailed results table.
compute: 3 NVIDIA K80 GPUs for training

solution_summary: The final submission used a single XGBoost model with 611 features, emphasizing categorical feature engineering rather than ensembling. Original columns and combinations of columns received multiple target-statistic and count encodings, including numerical columns treated as categorical variables. A GPU-accelerated random search retained combinations that improved cross-validation, producing a full model with CV 1.016.
compute: Full feature engineering and training: 6 hours on 1x A100; simplified version: 2 hours on 1x T4; combination search ran for multiple days.

solution_summary: The pipeline extracted PDF bodies, author headers, and references before identifying DOI candidates. Regex handled fixed patterns, while Qwen extracted variable-length identifiers from short text windows and fine-tuned Qwen 14B filtered non-data DOIs and classified their types. Accession IDs used regex and a public classification solution. Two final submissions achieved private scores of 0.613 for the main ML pipeline and 0.647 when the MDC corpus was added to filter false positives.

The team trained all models on a merged 2019 and 2020 cassava dataset and combined EfficientNet-B3, ResNeXt50, ViT, and ResNeSt50d in the final ensemble. SnapMix with linearly increasing probabilities improved cross-validation and public leaderboard scores, particularly for ResNeXt variants. They retained standard cross-entropy loss after noise-oriented losses failed to help. Dataset cleaning, green-content filtering, and class-probability scaling did not yield reliable improvements, while SE-ResNeXt models hurt ensemble performance despite good individual scores.

solution_title: 1609 to 1663: Custom GNN encoder to custom Transformer
solution_summary: The post lists three notebook links for pretraining, a training example, and submission. The pretraining link is described as obtaining a common seed. It provides no substantive explanation of the approach or results.

The pipeline builds three-channel images from neighboring slices and uses manually annotated aneurysm and brain boxes to guide training and cropping. ViT Large and EVA Large classifiers are combined with MiT-B4 FPN models trained jointly for classification and segmentation. Predictions pseudo-label two external datasets and correct high-confidence negative training series before a second training round. Weighted ensembles combine models from both rounds, with the stronger reported submission achieving 0.8823 OOF AUC and 0.89 public leaderboard score.

solution_title: Pokemon TCG AI - Team Magist Solution
solution_summary: The agent combined a replay-based pattern database with a Transformer policy and value network. Supervised training used public-agent matches, heuristic-agent games, and league play, while tactical heuristics broadened the strategies encountered during self-play. Monte Carlo sampling evaluated actions with hidden or random outcomes by averaging value estimates after simulated continuations. The final deck closely followed a strong public deck because genetic-search alternatives were less consistent.
compute: CPU-parallel matches for genetic deck evaluation

solution_summary: The author based the solution on a shared Bengali speech recognition notebook and changed its parameters using another notebook focused on decoding. Parameter changes were the main adjustment described, although the exact settings were not provided. Training a model from scratch reached only 40,000 steps, with that checkpoint scoring around 0.440. A custom 5-gram model also did not work well.

The author built a reproduction of another competitor's approach using presentation materials and AI coding assistance. A 17-model ensemble was evaluated both frozen and with online learning at a learning rate of 1e-4. Online updates increased local weighted zero-mean R² from 0.01413 to 0.01942. Exact reproduction details remain unconfirmed, with differences in update settings and training duration still under investigation.

solution_title: The platform's bug is not a responsibility that contestants should bear. We call on the organizing committee to propose a solution!

solution_summary: The author adapted an existing image-classification kernel, preserving aspect ratio when resizing to 600×850 and training on all available training data without cross-validation. They trained EfficientNet B5, B6, B7 and Inception-ResNet-v2 models, using horizontal and vertical flip test-time augmentation and ensembling. Pseudo-labeling improved the single Inception-ResNet-v2 public score from 0.981 to 0.984 and the ensemble from 0.984 to 0.988. With no validation set, submission selection relied on public scores and a random choice among strong submissions.

The solution ensembled three small image classifiers trained on cropped mammograms at 1536×896 resolution. Training proceeded through competition data, pseudo-labeled VinDr data, and final fine-tuning on competition data. Connected-component cropping, negative downsampling, and careful learning-rate choices were central to the pipeline. Inference used horizontal-flip augmentation and binarization post-processing.

The team used separate pipelines for molecules with shared and non-shared building blocks. Shared-block predictions combined enlarged CNNs, a CNN-GRU variant, fingerprint-based boosted trees, and a graph neural network with protein-specific weights. Non-shared predictions used rank ensembles of ChemBERTa models, with an alternative submission also incorporating XGBoost. Because reliable non-shared validation was difficult, public scores guided those ensembles; the two submissions achieved private scores of 0.275 and 0.277.

solution_title: 8th Place Solution: single model with heavy augmentation + tuned threshold
solution_summary: The author trained YOLOv8x-seg on all training data and all three classes with strong augmentation. Two-fold validation split whole-slide images into separate groups and revealed substantial sensitivity to the mask threshold. Final submissions used thresholds of 0.5 and 0.2, producing private scores of 0.56 and 0.369 respectively. Inference at resolution 768 outperformed 512, while larger training images and rotation augmentation did not help.

solution_title: Nuances of bias in machine learning (In Dimension C-132)
solution_summary: This post discusses machine learning bias through a fictional medical diagnosis scenario. It examines how strong aggregate accuracy can conceal harmful outcomes for underrepresented groups. The author considers simpler models, additional data, augmentation, abandoning deployment, and selective human review. It is an essay about deployment tradeoffs rather than a competition solution.

The solution simplified the simulator's cost and flight dynamics to optimize fuel consumption and flight duration. It computed efficient altitude and airspeed settings for cruise, ascent, and descent at the current aircraft weight. An automatic agent selected among three flight actions at each step. The resulting plans exploited the simulator's unusually efficient ascent-descent cycles.

The solution combined fixed-length and variable-length 1D CNNs with separate hand and lip backbones. Landmark preprocessing centered coordinates between the eyebrows, standardized hand orientation, and removed missing-hand frames. Global max pooling, stochastic depth, strong label smoothing, and stochastic weight averaging supported training. Combining the two sequence architectures provided a larger gain than combining fixed-length models alone, and the best reported blend scored 0.8824 privately.

The team excluded fake test rows when calculating statistics. Their feature engineering addressed locally infrequent histogram values by combining value counts with several distribution-based distances and statistics. They also used a target-separated k-fold procedure for feature handling and data augmentation. The brief post links feature code but does not specify models or numerical results.

The solution combined raw-signal attention models with residual CNNs trained on several spectrogram representations. Neural networks used a weighted MAE and quantile-loss objective, learning-rate decay, early stopping, and five-fold stratified validation. Fold predictions and architecture-specific test-time augmentations fed a stacking stage with XGBoost, CatBoost, and TabNet, whose predictions were averaged. Granular-field images, clustering, and time-series validation did not work.
compute: STFT model: 12 hours training; tabular models: a few minutes.

solution_title: 5th Place Solution : MASt3R is All You Need
solution_summary: The solution shortlisted image pairs with MASt3R-ASMK, computed semi-dense matches with MASt3R, and used COLMAP for geometric verification, reconstruction, and automatic clustering. Adaptive similarity thresholds were tuned on the competition training data and checked through public leaderboard submissions. Pair selection and engineering optimizations made the expensive matching pipeline practical within the inference budget. Alternative similarity methods and explicit pre-clustering performed worse than the selected pipeline.
compute: 2 x T4 GPUs; matching and reconstruction constrained to a 9-hour inference budget.

solution_summary: The solution used a two-stage recommender with diverse candidate generators followed by LightGBM and CatBoost reranking. Candidates came from word2vec, co-visitation, matrix factorization and collaborative filtering, with popularity and temporal weighting improving retrieval. Around 200 features captured session, item, interaction and candidate statistics. Sampling one twentieth of validation sessions enabled fast experiments with stable leaderboard correlation, and the final ensemble achieved CV 0.587 and public score 0.5985.
compute: Approximately 10–30 minutes per experiment using 1/20 sampled sessions.

solution_summary: The solution combined diverse sequence and graph models to predict RNA reactivity and degradation. Sequence, structure, and loop information were encoded separately, supplemented by base-pair probabilities and statistical features. Graph models used node and edge features, with additional attention matrices derived from multiple base-pair probability packages and Gaussian distance expansions. Ensembling models trained on differently filtered datasets helped handle noisy labels and the change in sequence length between training and testing.

The solution combined three EfficientNet-B7 models initialized with Noisy Student weights: two frame-based models and one sequence model with added 3D convolutions. Mixup between aligned real and fake faces was central to reducing rapid overfitting, alongside image augmentation and on-the-fly video compression. Inference used sampled frames, horizontal flips, a confidence-strengthening transformation, and confidence-weighted averaging. Training and preprocessing took approximately five days on a DGX-1, with no external data beyond pretrained weights.
compute: DGX-1; approximately 5 days for training and preprocessing

solution_summary: The author derived tour constraints that allowed conversion into valid arm configurations without extra reconfiguration cost beyond movement distance. A modified GA-EAX-restart generated constrained tours, and LKH-2 improved them using partitioned subproblems and fixed edges near the start. Comparing tours exposed three color-cost improvements that brought the score to 74075.70654. Finally, beam search converted the tour into a valid configuration sequence while retaining candidates separately for each larger-arm angle.
