solution_title: 6th Place Solution for the March Machine Learning Mania 2024 Competition
solution_summary: The submission used Nate Silver's men's and women's ratings to generate pairwise tournament win probabilities. The author manually classified men's matchups by location and added a five-percentage-point advantage when only one team was considered at home. More elaborate models had been explored previously, but time constraints led to this simple ratings-based submission. It achieved a private leaderboard score of 0.05564, with the code taking about one minute to run.

solution_summary: The solution combined aggregate game features, agent components, and features extracted from LudRules with LightGBM and CatBoost regressors. Features were selected separately within grouped folds, and model variants used different feature counts with or without fold-specific TF-IDF. The final submissions used weighted ensembles of either six models without TF-IDF or twelve models including TF-IDF, both scoring 0.437 on the private leaderboard. The author reported overfitting and questioned whether the game-result features introduced leakage.

solution_title: 34th place solution, end-to-end learning with a single neural net.
solution_summary: The post congratulates competitors and thanks contributors for starter scripts and advice. The author says they joined with one month remaining and relied heavily on those resources. It links to an external page without describing the solution in the provided text.

The final blend assigned 40% weight to a TF-IDF method averaging 2–5-gram variants and 60% to an ensemble dominated by 7B Mistral and Llama models. The best submission used an adversarially selected training dataset. A small language model trained on 10% of the data identified difficult examples in the remainder, which were mixed equally with the original PERSUADE dataset. This selection strategy was discovered late, so the final models were trained hastily on the last day.

The author describes separate approaches for several capture-the-flag challenges, including clustering with DBSCAN and KMeans and visualization with t-SNE. The Granny pipeline used MobileNet2 preprocessing, Torchattak, and postprocessing, while Semantile involved manual work and GloVe. Other challenges were addressed with a pickle serialization snippet and specific DNS-related prompts, although several solutions are only shown in images.

solution_title: 247th Place / Silver Medal — A CV-Robust Ensemble of Tabular Models, Local GR
solution_summary: The final solution blended five complementary trajectory estimates, led by a neural local GR refiner anchored to a tabular and physics ensemble. Robust polynomial projection, a semi-Markov decoder, an independent tree ensemble, and structural-surface-guided GR matching supplied additional paths. Well-level nested validation selected matcher variants and conservative nonnegative blend weights. The final pooled OOF RMSE was 8.4064 ft and private RMSE was 8.384 ft, with remaining error concentrated in a few catastrophic wells.

The pipeline used a lung localizer, EfficientDet-D5 disease detection, and separate classifiers to suppress detections on healthy images. Each image-annotation pair was treated independently, and detector outputs were ensembled with weighted boxes fusion. A blend of EfficientNet-B7 and ResNet200d classifiers supplied healthy/unhealthy probabilities that adjusted box confidence scores and added the no-finding prediction. This fusion improved CV from 0.36 to 0.47 and the private score from 0.219 to 0.297; YOLOv5 and external-data pseudo-labeling were unsuccessful.

The selected solution took the median predictions of 15 stratified-fold LightGBM regressors trained on the competition dataset. Inputs combined essay statistics, count-vectorizer features, Universal Sentence Encoder embeddings, and six writing-quality predictions from models trained on the ELL dataset. Five Bi-LSTM models produced those auxiliary features, with ONNX export substantially accelerating inference. The ELL features improved QWK by about 0.01, and the reported solution achieved CV 0.8172 and private score 0.817.

solution_title: GiGPO: A Thought Experiment at Kaggriculture
solution_summary: The approach combined macro farm-state planning with micro control of workers, tasks, and market actions. A spatial bottleneck transformer supplied global grid reasoning, while critic-free GiGPO training combined episode-level and intermediate-state economic credit. A routing heuristic handled final-day liquidation, leaving earlier days to the neural policy. Training exposed difficulty revisiting valuable intermediate states, motivating a proposed reverse curriculum.

solution_title: Would-be 39th place solution with single model (yolov4) from a first time competitor
solution_summary: The author describes a YOLOv4 pipeline, while noting that the team's two final submissions used EfficientDet. YOLOv4 was trained in Darknet at 704×704 resolution for 94 epochs, followed by a short 12-epoch pseudolabel training stage to limit overfitting without mosaic augmentation. solution_summary: The pipeline generated up to 200 candidates using prioritized session items, covisitation, word2vec, and ALS strategies, then reranked them with separate XGBoost models for clicks, carts, and orders. solution_title: Solution #35 : Whoa woke up to a massive jump in rankings!

solution_title: 13th place solution, Imitation learning with language modeling
solution_summary: The final agent used imitation learning, treating game actions as token sequences predicted by an encoder-decoder model. Custom tokenization encoded fleet destinations, split ship counts into two positions, and separated shipyard actions with a dedicated token. A pix2seq-style architecture combined board features from custom ConvNeXt blocks and toroidal convolutions with transformer encoding and decoding. Adding positional information at each attention layer improved convergence, and decoder inputs also included shipyard coordinates and sequence indices.

The solution used a three-stage pipeline: a pretrained 3D nnU-Net segmented C1–C7, a multitask 2.5D U-Net extracted slice embeddings, and an RNN with attention made downstream predictions. The segmentation model trained on 87 annotated cases achieved a Dice score of 0.95 and generated masks for cropping all 2,019 cases. The second stage combined three adjacent axial slices with vertebral-level information and learned five segmentation and classification tasks using bounding-box annotations. Training this stage beyond one epoch hurt downstream performance, while inference VRAM limits restricted ensembling to at most two folds.

solution_summary: The solution customized the previous year's winning image-matching pipeline, matching and correcting rotation for every image pair before clustering. Clusters were connected components of an inlier-count similarity graph after weak edges were removed, with isolated images and small components treated as outliers. Experiments with MASt3R-SfM and track refinement from VGGSfM or VGGT did not improve results.

The author used Gurobi 9.0 to solve a mixed-integer assignment model within narrow bounds around estimated daily occupancies. Those estimates came from a preliminary relaxation augmented with quadratic constraints that restricted occupancy mixtures to adjacent values. This reduced overly optimistic accounting costs and supplied useful occupancy targets before the preliminary model finished. The restricted MIP ran in under ten minutes on a MacBook, while producing the occupancy estimates took about 25 minutes. SCIP through OR-Tools had reached a score of 68910.94.

solution_summary: The pipeline combined chart classification, pix2pix-based segmentation and chart transformation, easyOCR, and extraction logic. Images were padded to squares and resized when necessary, with coordinates resized back during inference. Generating balanced synthetic charts substantially improved the simple CNN classifier, while scatter plots remained difficult because nearby points merged or were confused with noise and text. The solution scored 0.8 locally but could not exceed 0.58 on the leaderboard.

The team tuned public temporal 3D U-Net detection and transformer linking models, then extended the tracking graph with consolidation, mitosis detection, identity repair, and learned recentring. Conservative guards protected existing divisions and topology while learned CNN and LightGBM components repaired missed divisions, links, and positions. The final submissions scored 0.970 public and 0.946 private, with later repair stages contributing more on private than public. A major limitation was that full-chain validation used graphs from networks trained on the same videos, overstating private performance by about 0.03.

solution_summary: The solution ensembled 25 CatBoost models from five-fold stratified cross-validation repeated five times. It combined balanced class weights, metric-aware sample weighting for log loss, ordered boosting, and Stochastic Gradient Langevin Boosting. Optuna tuned parameters, while Bernoulli bootstrapping and row and column subsampling kept training practical. XGBoost, LightGBM, TabPFN blending, feature removal, and post-processing did not improve the approach.

solution_title: XGBoost in Compressed Space | 425th Place Solution Writeup for Open Problems – Single-Cell Perturbations
solution_summary: The solution compresses differential gene expression into 36 TruncatedSVD components and trains XGBoost to predict those components before inverse transformation. Features combine drug-specific averages over other cell types, target encodings, and indicators of which cell types contributed to the averages. Six-fold validation was used, with dimensionality reduction performed before splitting. The unensembled method reported public and private scores of 0.594 and 0.777 in about three minutes, with compression limiting the information it could recover.

solution_title: 20th place solution 🥈  - Ensemble of diverse DeBERTas and external data
solution_summary: The final solution averaged logits from seven fully fine-tuned DeBERTa V3 Large models with varied datasets, learning rates, and maximum sequence lengths. Training combined generated data from nbroad and mpware with competition data, while limiting external dataset size to avoid distribution shift. A 0.99 threshold on the O class provided the only final postprocessing. The strongest single model scored 0.967, and an unselected four-model ensemble achieved the author's best private score.

solution_title: source code & description, 66th place, R, glmnet + xgboost
solution_summary: This post is a collection of links for a Rossmann sales forecasting solution. It points to a detailed blog description, a short strategy document, and source code. No solution methods or experimental findings are included in the provided text.

The solution treated opacity detection as semantic segmentation, training three DeepLabV3+ variants with SE-ResNeXt101 or SENet backbones on resized or cropped images. Ellipses inscribed in the annotation boxes supplied segmentation targets, and training progressively introduced negative images and stronger augmentation. An ensemble averaged 90 predictions across architectures, folds, checkpoints, and input transformations. Thresholded masks became bounding boxes scored by their peak segmentation probability, with thresholds selected using public leaderboard feedback. The reported Stage 2 private score was 0.218, while a later image-resizing experiment reached 0.234.

The team blended individual models, including the author's LightGBM model using passband feature ratios, adjusted sample weights, and 55 selected features. The main contribution described is class-specific probability scaling tuned on out-of-fold predictions, followed by row normalization. This improved the author's CV loss from 0.52 to 0.493 and public score from 0.968 to 0.915. A final confidence-based probability adjustment further improved the team submission from 0.854 to 0.851 publicly and from 0.87021 to 0.86777 privately.

The solution combined public notebooks into a retrieval and selective reranking pipeline. For each comment, it retrieved two semantically similar positive examples and two negative examples, then ran three models with four variations of example context. Qwen2.5-32B handled only the 20% of test rows where the initial predictions were uncertain. Predictions were ranked within each rule before averaging to match the competition's rule-specific AUC metric.

The solution adapted public notebooks with changes motivated by anticipated distribution drift. It used time-grouped validation, joint train/test normalization and quantile transformation, and 15 k-means label features, while removing stock_id from one blended model. Three LightGBM seeds were blended with weights estimated from validation scores. Several changes worsened public performance but were considered possible contributors to better private performance; price-amplitude augmentation did not work.

solution_title: #13: U900 team - PYBOOST is what you need
solution_summary: The team combined multi-target PYBOOST models with several neural-network families, emphasizing target encoding and ensemble diversity. Neural variants included learned SMILES embeddings, separate prediction of three gene clusters, and features derived from aggregated raw RNA counts through PCA and target encoding. Raw-count features contributed diversity rather than stronger standalone performance, while chemical descriptors and pretrained chemical embeddings were excluded from the final ensemble. The report attributes stability to careful validation and diversity control, reporting a public-private score correlation of 0.98.

solution_title: 4th Place Solution: Stabilizing Convergence in Understanding Clouds
solution_summary: The final system averages seven folds of EfficientNet-B4-FPN and three folds of Resnet34-ASPP segmentation models. Training stability under noisy rectangular labels was the main concern, addressed through RAdam, initial BCE training followed by Symmetric Lovasz fine-tuning, and pseudo-labeling on all test images. Training and inference use flip augmentations, with additional geometric augmentation during training. Predictions use a shared 0.4 threshold and a minimum mask size of 5,000 pixels; separate false-positive classifiers were discarded because their cross-validation performance was unstable.

solution_summary: The project provides an open U-Net-based pipeline for salt identification, including metadata preparation, training, evaluation, and inference. Nine reported solution versions improve the listed leaderboard score from 0.745 to 0.849, with the last version reporting CV of 0.853. solution_title: Lost my silver medal and my first lesson on trusting public LB 😥
solution_summary: The author describes submission selection and validation mistakes without specifying the underlying models. The final solution equally averaged character-level predictions from six DeBERTa models. Continued masked language modeling on all patient notes used a corrected token-logit computation and achieved 75–85% masked-token accuracy. Manually correcting roughly 120 noisy annotations improved scores by about 0.003, alongside multi-sample dropout, random masking, and added newline tokens. The ensemble scored 0.889 publicly and 0.890 privately, although feature-text mismatches and omitted models limited the final submission.

solution_title: 23rd private (1437th public, 4 submissions total) - regular expressions

The pipeline first trained all 11 targets, then specialized the model into ETT, NGT, and CVC experts before fine-tuning each expert on pseudo-labeled NIH images. solution_title: # 40th public → 2000th private: an exact LB instrument aimed at the wrong target
solution_summary: The author built a prediction stack on public notebook artifacts, adding spatial components and roughly twenty leaderboard-fitted correction constants. The solution combined lung and tissue segmentation with rich features extracted from CT scans. The final translator used a single ByT5-base model with averaged checkpoints and beam-search decoding. solution_summary: The author encoded order-book and trade data as 60 ten-second intervals and processed these sequences with an LSTM–Dense–GRU network. A separate recurrent model supplied stock-time embeddings, which an attention mechanism combined across other stocks at the same time. These representations, aggregate market features, and one-hot stock identifiers were concatenated into an MLP. Cross-stock attention improved the score by about 0.002, and inference used the 40th percentile of predictions from five folds grouped by time identifier.

The solution used a late interaction mechanism to approximate pairwise toxicity comparisons efficiently, with Muppet RoBERTa Large as the backbone. Pseudo-labels from earlier competition datasets and public notebooks supplied more than 20 labels per comment. Training combined Dice loss, large batches, mixed precision, cyclic learning rates, weight averaging, and EMA. Late interaction raised the public score from 0.844 to 0.872, but its private-score benefit was smaller.

solution_title: BirdCLEF 2026: A Multi-Branch Ensemble Solution (60th Place Private LB)
solution_summary: The final system combined Perch embeddings with a ProtoSSM correction branch, retrained SED models, and multiple EfficientNet branches. Branch outputs were blended in rank space, then adjusted through conservative gating and taxonomic smoothing. solution_title: Silver zone solo, no credits used.

solution_title: 12th place- predict joint probabilities for start & end indices
solution_summary: The solution ensembled two RoBERTa-based models and benefited from initialization with SQuAD2-fine-tuned weights. solution_title: Rank 83rd Silver Solution: DINOv2/3 + Depth Fusion with Uncertainty Calibration
solution_summary: The solution fused DINO RGB features with EfficientNet depth features through learned gates and attention pooling. solution_summary: The solution combined MultinomialNB, SGDClassifier, LightGBM, and CatBoost using a VotingClassifier. Their respective ensemble weights were 0.09, 0.42, 0.27, and 0.94, and the vocabulary size was set to 15 million. Based on a public notebook, the approach achieved a public score of 0.963 and a private score of 0.901.

Most gains came from adjusting output probabilities to compensate for class frequency and match the expected test class counts. solution_summary: The final submission combined LightGBM and logistic regression, selected using out-of-fold validation performance. solution_title: Rank 318 Solution: Replay-Efficient Confused Deputy Search
solution_summary: The final approach specialized in Confused Deputy behavior using short, single-message delegation prompts that induced an email action. Six templates and distinct recipient addresses created diverse scoring cells, and execution traces filtered out unsuccessful candidates. A warm-up interaction and adaptive latency estimates controlled generation under a 950-candidate ceiling, using the same strategy for GPT-OSS and Gemma. The post also describes an unsuccessful broader capability-discovery approach with source profiling and a contextual Q learner.

The approach used nested leave-one-year-out validation to guide model-specific feature engineering and tuning. Adversarial validation motivated removing time features when adding the original dataset, while ratio and annual-relative temperature features improved multiple model families. The selected submissions averaged either LightGBM, random forest, and logistic regression, or four untuned tree models, with the latter achieving 0.90282 privately. A separately reported rank ensemble of XGBoost and LightGBM achieved 0.90669 privately but was not selected by local or public leaderboard performance.

DINOv3 provided the primary biomass predictions by processing two image halves and fusing their representations with a Mamba layer. SigLIP supplied semantic guidance through image-to-text similarity scores. The final blend favored DINOv3, and clover predictions came directly from that branch. Constraint-based post-processing enforced consistent sums among biomass components.

The solution used ImageNet-pretrained six-channel CNNs with combined ArcFace and cross-entropy training, followed by plate-aware linear sum assignment. Progressive pseudo-labeling added confident test examples every epoch while preserving class uniqueness within each plate. The final ensemble contained six DenseNet161 and five DenseNet201 models with flip, rotation, and crop-resize TTA, achieving 0.99763 private and 0.99480 public scores. A reference-image conditioning approach failed to improve ordinary classification.

The solution converts audio into spectrograms and extracts interesting patches through image processing. Template matching generates features, which are merged with the supplied segment histograms and location information before training random forest regressors. Submission files are exported when cross-validation AUC exceeds 0.93. The supplied settings reportedly produce a private leaderboard score around 0.954.

solution_summary: The author combined a custom floor predictor with diverse public coordinate predictions and extensive postprocessing. Coordinate bias correction, snapping predictions to known locations, cost minimization, and temporal leakage methods drove improvements. Blending predictions from different origins and repeatedly applying postprocessing kept the approach roughly 0.4 metres ahead of the best public notebook. Changing the postprocessing order produced a final improvement, and the two selected submissions used different floor models.

solution_summary: The final solution used DenseNet169 on 1024-pixel images, trained across five folds for 50 epochs three times. A sampler selected images with masks 60% of the time, and training combined BCE, Dice, and focal losses with Adam and cosine annealing. DenseNet169 and DPN92 performed best, but DPN92 was excluded because of its large model files. The models were not retrained on the new second-stage training set.

The solution distilled an XGB teacher into the competition-provided RandomForest by training the forest on the teacher's training predictions. Both models used three selected input columns, while XGB additionally received an oxygen mean feature. Threshold-based outlier removal and selective replacement of low oxygen values with missing values improved training data quality. The forest retained a reported 88–90% of the teacher's effectiveness in cross-validation, while IsolationForest filtering performed poorly.

The author implemented seven binary logistic regression models from scratch, one for each fertilizer class. Each model estimated a class probability using a sigmoid and was trained by gradient descent on binary log-loss. L2 regularization penalized large weights to reduce overfitting. The approach supplied probabilities for the competition's ordered three-fertilizer prediction task, but the writeup provided no validation or final score.

solution_summary: The team built two large transaction feature sets using aggregations, categorical frequencies, sequence embeddings, and historical-versus-new transaction interactions. Pairing weakly correlated features and filtering features by missingness, correlation, uniqueness, and model importance improved validation. Around 32 diverse tree models were stacked using Bayesian regression, reaching approximately 3.630 validation RMSE and 3.675 public leaderboard RMSE. An outlier module intersected the top 100 predictions from four classifiers to select 21 outliers, improving the public score to 3.666; both chosen submissions scored about 3.599 privately.

solution_title: Solution Write-up: Unleashing the Healing Potential: Abdominal Trauma
solution_summary: The post describes a tabular exploratory analysis of organ health and injury labels rather than a detailed CT-image prediction pipeline. It cleans the data, examines injury prevalence and correlations, and uses K-means to identify healthy and injured patient clusters. Random Forest, SVM and Gradient Boosting models were evaluated for accuracy, with Random Forest reported at 96%. The validation design and a final competition submission pipeline are not specified.

solution_title: Yirun's Solution (1st place): Training Supervised Autoencoder with MLP
solution_summary: The final submission blended a supervised autoencoder MLP with teammates' XGBoost models. The autoencoder and prediction network were trained jointly within each purged time-series fold to avoid validation label leakage. Multiple response targets, response-magnitude sample weights, and averaged predictions across targets and seeds supported the neural approach. Only models from the last two folds were retained, and the standalone AE-MLP achieved a private leaderboard score of 6022.202.

The solution combined four models with small differences in architecture and target cleaning, assigning extra weight to the fourth model. Its main improvement came from identifying how extra spaces in the original text caused systematic offsets in annotated answer spans. One model reversed this corruption during preprocessing, and final postprocessing reproduced the expected span offsets. The ensemble scored 0.723 publicly before postprocessing and 0.731 publicly and 0.729 privately afterward.

The solution used a transformer with three layers and an embedding size of 480, adapted from public kernels. It standardized each sign sequence using its own mean and standard deviation and engineered distances among approximately 106 selected landmarks. Augmentations such as flipping and concatenation improved cross-validation performance from about 0.76 to 0.78, while increasing model size brought single-model public leaderboard performance to around 0.80. Adversarial weight perturbation, random frame masking, and exponential moving averages helped control overfitting.

The solution treated tissue tiles as sequences, combining an ImageNet-pretrained DenseNet121 feature extractor with two GRU layers to regress ISUP grade using log-cosh loss. Whole-slide rotation, 256 × 256 tissue extraction, and normalization across each image's tiles formed the preprocessing pipeline. Image-hash similarity clusters were kept together during five-fold validation, with Gleason score frequencies balanced across splits. Training alternated frozen and unfrozen backbone stages with different sequence lengths, used batches of two, and repeatedly discarded images whose prediction error exceeded 2.5.

Separate LightGBM models predicted production and consumption through normalized differences from their targets two days earlier. Features combined calendar information, normalized target lags and differences, weather forecasts, historical weather, and weekday/weekend aggregates. Validation used January through May 2023, followed by full-data training with two seeds per task. Feature importance limited production to 300 features and consumption to 400, and both models were retrained at three points during inference.

solution_title: 1st place solution models (it’s not all BirdNet)
solution_summary: The author trained sound-event detection models with EfficientNet and NFNet backbones, contributing them to a final blend that also included BirdNet. Training used 15-second audio chunks, secondary labels, noise augmentation, and weighting to address class imbalance. Pretraining on both competition years was followed by fine-tuning on recordings containing scored birds. Centered five-second inference and checkpoint averaging helped, while fixed thresholds worked better for ensembles than quantile thresholds. Both reported backbones achieved a private score of 0.78.

Coordinate-only nearest-neighbor models with 15, 30, and 45 neighbors were also used in the stack, with 45 neighbors performing best.

solution_title: 7th place solution with no external training data
solution_summary: The author generated soft labels through three GPT-6 astra image-and-report reading protocols, corrected site-dependent Synovitis bias, and blended the result with cross-model teachers. A multiview 2.5D network combined spatially aligned tokens with label-query and attention-MIL heads, using EfficientNetV2-S and ConvNeXt backbones. Label improvements contributed more than architectural changes, while the four-model rank ensemble offered little private-score benefit. The best single model reached 0.958 private AUC, compared with 0.957 for the selected ensembles.

solution_summary: The solution used a two-stage text-normalization pipeline. XGBoost first classified whether each word required changing using two context words on either side. Words requiring normalization were passed to a character-input sequence-to-sequence model built around a memory-augmented neural network. Training lasted four epochs, and resource constraints prevented completing hyperparameter optimization, so the model retained the research paper's parameter settings.

solution_summary: The author built a rule-based agent that scored factory locations using resource access, rubble, open areas, and nearby factories, then adjusted bidding to the quality of available positions. During play, it projected bot positions, canceled conflicting plans, and reassigned actions through a priority scheme. Its broader strategy balanced economic development with attacks on vulnerable enemies and targeted rubble clearing. A late shift toward solar power remained insufficiently polished, while bot congestion and expensive computation limited planning and experimentation.

solution_title: Like Popping Bubble-Wrap: Keith T. Herring on Placing Second in Wikipedia's Participation Challenge
solution_summary: The solution scraped editing histories for approximately one million Wikipedia editors and derived 206 behavioral features. It generated roughly 3,000 randomized decision-tree models with varying random forest parameters. An iterative quadratic optimizer used out-of-bag predictions to select and weight 34 complementary models. Exponentially decayed edit volume with an 80-day half-life was the strongest feature.

solution_summary: The final solution blended two public notebook approaches with the author's own four-fold DeBERTa-v3 base and large models. Metric learning, T5 encoders, further pretraining, target reassignment, GPT-2 likelihood features, and a random-forest vocabulary estimator did not work.

The first approach stabilized training with gradient accumulation to an effective batch size of 128, stronger augmentation, and 1024-pixel training images, achieving 0.586 privately. Mirror padding and morphological repair improved its predictions, while stronger augmentation and pseudo-labeling were excluded after validation and public-score declines.

solution_summary: The pipeline denoised acoustic signals with discrete wavelets and generated quantile-crossing features across multiple decomposition levels and wavelet lengths. Spectrum statistics, peak counts, and autocorrelation features supplemented these inputs to LightGBM. Shuffled folds stratified by time and earthquake guided feature development, with nested validation added later. A final adjustment transferred predictions to the test distribution, while several augmentation and deep learning approaches were unsuccessful.

First-stage predictions from 15 classifiers became meta-features for XGBoost, Random Forest, and Uniform Gradient Boosting, whose outputs were blended using tuned weights. Production relied entirely on conga chains, with safety stocks and inter-factory transfers managing water, metal, and power. Pathfinding and future tile reservations coordinated movement, while role-specific controllers handled production, transport, defense, and attacks. Late attacks were staged and limited to four active lichen attackers per target, although fragile production chains and buggy self-defense remained weaknesses.

Models predicted stride-16 Gaussian heatmaps using a physical uncertainty scale of 200 angstroms and simple FPN necks to preserve fine features. Resampling, large input patches, heavy augmentation, and manually reviewed pseudo-labels supported training on competition and external data. Initial stratified validation guided development, but final models used all available data without local validation after cross-validation performance saturated.

Their final stack contains around 50 models, mostly LightGBM alongside neural networks, factorization machines, and linear models, with original features added to the stacking inputs. Weights-of-evidence encodings and label-aware ordering of tied timestamps provide further gains. Time-window counts, intervals between clicks, and categorical app identity are important features, while standard target encoding did not work.

The solution combined image embeddings, FastText text representations, categorical embeddings, and extensive statistical features in neural networks and tree models. solution_summary: The solution combined separate cell-level and image-level classifiers, using image predictions as context for noisy cell predictions. The solution ensembles five neural networks. Each network is described as resembling an MLM, with no architectural or training details provided in the post. A linked notebook supplies sample code for a single network.

The approach added Gaussian blur to prediction masks from a public notebook. Blur parameters were selected using the public leaderboard score. The author attributed the improvement to increased precision under the competition's F0.5 metric and reported public and private scores of 0.66 and 0.59.

The final solution averaged predictions from five-fold DeBERTa-v3-large models with a sequence length of 1024 and weighted layer pooling. Inputs were reconstructed by joining discourse texts sharing an essay ID and adding discourse-type tags. This representation improved the reported leaderboard score from 0.627 with discourse-plus-essay input to 0.61 with CLS embeddings, then to 0.600 with weighted layer pooling. Longformer training encountered exploding gradients, while unsuccessful RoBERTa MLM experiments discouraged further MLM experiments on DeBERTa.

This enabled six models and 74 total epochs within the two-hour limit. The downstream ensemble mixed a DPCNN with LSTM/GRU architectures and GloVe, Paragram, and news embeddings. solution_summary: The author built dual-stream biomass regressors on a DINOv3 backbone, fine-tuning only its last four blocks. Additional variants predicted quantiles or total biomass plus component ratios, with quantile uncertainty used for weighted ensembling. Segmentation Dice was approximately 0.66, ROI AUC approximately 0.94, and local series-level AUC approximately 0.81; false-positive filtering and a dedicated T2 MRI model did not improve results.

solution_title: #4 solution: Feature engineering made the difference
solution_summary: The solution blended two LightGBM, two XGBoost, and one CatBoost model with weights optimized by Optuna. Original data augmented every training fold, while validation used only synthetic competition examples, and the target was log-transformed. Store-attribute scores and their relationship to store size provided the largest improvement, especially when treated as categorical features in LightGBM. Stacking, inconsistent-value cleanup, and additional model families did not improve the solution.
external_data: ["Original dataset underlying the synthetic competition data"]

solution_summary: The solution used 2,300 engineered signal features and three LightGBM models targeting the full retained data, near-failure segments, and far-from-failure segments. A general model controlled when to blend with or switch to a specialist model. The author excluded earthquake events five and six based on leak information and visual similarity to the test data. Time-frequency and MFCC features improved correlations, while PCA, correlation-based feature pruning, and combinations with other model families were unsuccessful.

The solution combined four image embedding models trained with ArcMargin, CosFace, or ordinary classification objectives. It retrieved hotels through cosine similarity to training images, multiplying similarities across models and selecting five distinct hotels. Heavy augmentation, larger embeddings, and 512×512 images were useful, while several alternative retrieval and training strategies were discarded. The ensemble achieved public and private scores of 0.7273 and 0.7446.
compute: Colab T4 GPU; 2–3 hours per epoch; four models in the final ensemble.

solution_summary: The solution adapted SN-GAN with a projection discriminator and achieved a public leaderboard score of 45.6. It added spectral normalization to the generator, increased the learning rate, and reduced discriminator critic updates following techniques from SA-GAN. Training used batch size 128, decay starting at iteration 18000, and 24000 total iterations. Generating 32×32 images followed by bilinear resizing produced a worse score.

The pipeline used U-Net with bidirectional Conv-LSTM to segment abdominal organs, then classified organ crops with separate 3D ResNet CSN models for solid organs and bowel. Extravasation probabilities came from averaging the highest voxel probabilities of a separate segmentation model trained using supplied boxes. Strong augmentation, EMA, SWA, and gradient checkpointing helped address severe classification overfitting. Four-fold patient-grouped validation achieved an overall competition loss of 0.400; larger batches later improved validation to about 0.39, but submission errors prevented those models from being used successfully.
compute: About 80 hours total training across four folds per stage on a single RTX A6000 Ada; submission inference took 8–9 hours on a single Tesla P100. A100 cards enabled batch-size experiments.

solution_title: 4th Place Solution: ViT-Huge DINOv3 & Multi-Modal Feature Fusion with AUX predic
solution_summary: The solution combined a DINOv3 ViT-Huge backbone with an MLP encoding NDVI and plant height for biomass regression. Manually removing cardboard borders improved both public and private scores by 0.01. A second training stage initialized from the main model learned to predict NDVI and height from images, providing another 0.01 improvement and reaching public/private scores of 0.76/0.66. Weighted SmoothL1 loss, partial backbone freezing, standardized targets and features, and five-fold validation supported training.

The author describes a simple toxicity classification approach using scikit-learn logistic regression. Text was processed with TfidfVectorizer to create features. The post links a kernel but provides no validation setup or numerical results.

The solution converted left-handed sensor sequences into pseudo right-handed sequences and used a triple-tower architecture for IMU, ToF, and combined inputs. Multi-task training and separate temporal attention modules for each target were central design choices, with BERT and bidirectional LSTM variants providing ensemble diversity. Final submissions averaged probabilities across 15 or 20 models trained in five folds, achieving private scores of 0.841 and 0.843. A later flipped-subject detection and correction pipeline improved the 20-model ensemble's private score to 0.854.

solution_title: 1st place solution - Protein as a Graph
solution_summary: The author represented protein structures as residue graphs with distance-based edges and ESM2 sequence embeddings. A three-layer Graph Isomorphism Network combined intermediate representations, global readout, and mutation-site features through an MLP. The selected submission blended a buggy GNN with public Rosetta, Thermonet, RMSD, and pLDDT-difference predictions. Separate corrected GNN and inverse-centrality experiments showed substantial differences between public and private scores.
external_data: ["Public Rosetta score notebook", "Public Thermonet v2 notebook", "Public molecular-dynamics RMSD notebook", "Public pLDDT difference notebook"]

solution_summary: The team trained RoBERTa-base with a maximum sequence length of 168 using eight folds. Correcting selected-text indices for extra spaces improved local CV from 0.711 to 0.717, and validating multiple times per epoch also helped. Inference reversed the preprocessing through post-processing, improving the leaderboard score from 0.717 to 0.724. Alternative formulations, sentiment-specific models, BERTweet, and several cleaning approaches did not work for the team.

The solution modified a public neural-network baseline with bior1.3 wavelet denoising and a two-layer bidirectional GRU architecture. Attention outputs were combined with a separate dense feature branch, using strong dropout to control overfitting. Training used focal loss, cyclic-shift augmentation, ten stratified folds, Nadam, a triangular cyclic learning rate, and loss-based early stopping. It achieved public and private scores of 0.59499 and 0.67159.

solution_title: 638th Place (Bronze): 15 Draws of One Agent, Only 3 of Them Medal
solution_summary: The submission packaged a public Grimmsnarl control agent built around specialist advisors and context-weighted voting, with a deck-coherent greedy fallback. Its main contributions were deployment reliability and measurement of ladder variance rather than stronger gameplay. Fifteen submissions of identical code produced ratings from 721.5 to 860.3, so the authors used repeated submissions and a Monte Carlo analysis to guide final selection. Search repairs, learned value estimation, evolved weights, and alternative decks did not deliver reliable live improvements.
external_data: ["tetsu2131's public Grimmsnarl ex Damage-Transfer Control agent"]

solution_summary: The solution classified each markdown cell into a gap between consecutive code cells using cosine similarities between shared transformer representations, with an LSTM providing code context. It combined one DeBERTa and two DistilRoBERTa checkpoints and selected positions by minimizing expected displacement instead of taking the most probable position. Additional masked language modeling and externally crawled Kaggle notebooks improved performance, while a separate attention model ordered markdowns assigned to the same gap. The base DeBERTa model scored 88.5% on development data, and position postprocessing added roughly 0.8–1 percentage point.
compute: Most experiments used a 3090; final models trained on A6000. MLM took 5 days for DistilRoBERTa and 40 days for DeBERTa-v3-large on a 3090.

solution_title: My personnal journey through the RIID competition - Silver LGB single model
solution_summary: The author built a LightGBM solution centered on feature engineering from user histories. Distinctive features included a Bayesian probability index and a cluster-based feature. Efficient iteration, dictionary and set operations, and column-wise float32 conversion helped control memory and CPU costs.

The solution fine-tuned ResNet152 and DenseNet161 on the 10,000 most popular landmarks and extracted 512-dimensional image features. Five-neighbor retrieval across ten saved CNN checkpoints produced candidate training classes for each test image. Fifteen image-class pair features fed an XGBoost model and a neural network, whose averaged probabilities determined the final class. This pipeline achieved over 0.19 GAP compared with 0.04 for direct classification, while cuML retrieved neighbors for 110,000 test images against four million training images in under five minutes.
compute: KNN retrieval of 5 neighbors for 110K test images from 4M training images took less than 5 minutes.

solution_title: My first kaggle and 11th place solution sharing
solution_summary: The solution averages LightGBM, XGBoost, and random forest predictions and adds Prophet predictions to the final submission. Validation emphasizes two 33-day periods covering New Year and the most recent available dates. Rolling weighted means were particularly important, while holiday-distance and weather features supplied additional context. Adding Prophet improved the private leaderboard score from 0.511 to 0.509.

The team converted four-dimensional images into three-dimensional inputs and trained CNN autoencoders for spatial maps. PCA-based compression produced additional features that were combined with original inputs and site-classifier features. Target binning and feature selection further improved the final pipeline. The reported scores were 0.15663 publicly and 0.15703 privately.

The solution used basic string rules for non-name PII and a staged XGBoost pipeline for names. Name candidates were filtered using external name lists, then classified using neighboring-token features, word TF-IDF, and part-of-speech TF-IDF. Classification thresholds controlled false negatives in the first stage and optimized F5 in the final stage. Two models selected from eight-fold cross-validation achieved a private score of 0.9224 with roughly four minutes of inference.
compute: Around 4 minutes inference

solution_summary: The solution stacked 123 CatBoost, XGBoost, and LightGBM models using a TensorFlow neural network trained on out-of-fold predictions. Training included the original dataset, while validation metrics used only competition rows. Inverting predictions for train/test duplicates delivered the largest reported gain, about 0.0141 on the public leaderboard. Neural stacking improved cross-validation by about 0.0026 over the best single model, while engineered features reduced performance.

solution_title: 2nd Place Solution: Helmet Detection + 3d Impact Detection + Post Processing
solution_summary: The pipeline first detected helmets with YOLOv5, then classified impacts using nine-frame helmet crops and 3D EfficientNet models. Validation grouped videos by GameID, and training combined impact-type targets, class weighting, and resampled negatives. The final ensemble averaged six EfficientNet models on shared detector boxes with horizontal-flip augmentation. Video-level NMS, confidence filtering, and a top-19 limit substantially reduced false positives.

solution_title: A lucky silver medalist thoughts[38th place]
solution_summary: The team used variants of a shared RNA modeling notebook together with a stacker learned from an earlier competition. Training was restricted to samples with SNR above 1.5. The main validation improvement came from adding two to four learnable 4×4 filtered edge-feature matrices to characterize neighborhoods around paired bases. Several manually designed graph-distance and pairing features failed to improve the attention-based graph models.

The author combined a public R generalized additive model with eight additional models optimized for cross-validation performance. Polynomial logistic regression and the GAM supplied diversity relative to the seven tree-based models. Original data helped the tree models but was excluded from GAM and logistic regression training. Final ensemble weights were selected using cross-validation scores.

The author announces that an approach summary and cleaned code are available. The post links to a GitHub repository and refers to an attachment. It provides no technical description of the solution in the supplied text.

The solution combined extensive feature engineering with a multilevel ensemble built from four feature datasets. Features compared manager and building attributes and incorporated leaked listing image timestamps, while diverse classification and regression models supplied cross-validated predictions for stacking. Two third-level ensembles blended XGBoost, neural networks, and Extra Trees, and their outputs were averaged equally. The best single model scored 0.50379 publicly and 0.50500 privately; prior correction provided only a very small improvement.
compute: Computing four expensive features took about four hours; precomputed timeout.csv was supplied to skip this step.
external_data: ["Listing image timestamps shared by KazAnova", "Photo shape metadata in jpgs.json"]

solution_summary: The solution distilled stacked DeBERTa-v3-base and LightGBM predictions into DeBERTa-v3-xsmall. Prompt token, bigram, and trigram matches were encoded as token type IDs, providing prompt context without including the full prompt text at inference. Distillation gradually shifted from pseudo labels to an equal mix of pseudo and true labels over three epochs. Prompt-mean adjustments and target-specific neural/LightGBM ensemble weights completed the pipeline, with a reported runtime of about 15 minutes.
compute: ~15 minutes runtime; hardware and runtime stage unspecified

solution_title: [5th solution]: Ensemble of Bidirectional LSTM based Models
solution_summary: The solution combined compact bidirectional LSTM models trained on low-resolution ClimSim data mixed with either aqua-planet data or a subset of high-resolution data. The aqua-planet models used MLP encoder-decoder features, a bidirectional GRU, and optional physical features, while the high-resolution models used deeper LSTMs with pooling and sometimes attention. Training used Huber loss for the aqua-planet models and weighted MAE/MSE losses with EMA for the high-resolution models, with additional diversity from SWA and checkpoint averaging. A weighted ensemble followed by moisture-tendency clipping achieved a public leaderboard score of 0.79071.
compute: Aqua models: approximately 24 hours on one RTX 4090; high-resolution mixed models: about 12 hours on 6 RTX 4090 GPUs.

solution_summary: The author used LightGBM and a simple feed-forward neural network with shared sales and promotion features. Added features measured zero-sales transitions, zero-sales counts over multiple windows, and time since the latest promotion. The neural network used RankGauss preprocessing, batch normalization, and strong dropout, while perishable and non-perishable products were modeled separately. Features were retained only when they improved both forecast-horizon segments and the public leaderboard, producing steady reported improvements.

The team combined an ensemble of embedding retrievers with fine-tuned listwise LLM rerankers. Three rounds of quality-filtered synthetic questions, expanded misconception descriptions, subject hierarchy metadata, and chain-of-thought inputs improved retrieval and reranking. The final retrieval ensemble used Mistral and two Qwen2.5-14B models, reserving inference time for larger rerankers that refined candidate rankings through sliding windows. Quantization and vLLM optimizations enabled the large-model pipeline, whose reported full configuration reached 0.604 privately and 0.622 publicly.
compute: H100 training: Qwen14B retrievers about 2–3 days, Qwen32B and QwQ retrievers about 5 days; Qwen14B reranker about 2 hours and Qwen72B reranker about 8 hours.

solution_summary: The selected pipeline modeled each well as a smooth geological trajectory, starting with particle-filter alignment and CatBoost residual prediction. Heel-anchored geometry and regional physical estimates supplied additional structure, with confidence models controlling their contribution. A three-scale Bayesian gamma-ray posterior averaged plausible alignment modes and limited corrections to ±4.5 ft. Well-grouped validation, bootstrap uncertainty, and fold consistency favored this conservative policy over more aggressively optimized alternatives. The selected candidate achieved private RMSE 7.522, improving by 1.000 over the public-leaderboard-best submission.

The solution combined weather, calendar, client, and lagged consumption and production features with forward feature selection. Two ensembles were described: segmented LightGBM models including a two-day difference target, and a LightGBM–CatBoost ensemble with temporal model averaging. Models were retrained periodically using the latest 14 months, skipping retraining on unscored periods. The reported public scores were 61.08 and 61.49, while capacity-normalized targets improved validation but failed on the leaderboard.

The author used a single model with a four-part hybrid RAG approach. Initial experiments concentrated on Llama 7B and 13B with LoRA or QLoRA fine-tuning. The final approach switched to DeBERTa v3 because it outperformed those models in the author's experiments.

The author trained SE-ResNeXt50, SE-ResNeXt101, and Xception classifiers using all training drawings, including unrecognized examples. Each 224×224 input encoded progressively longer stroke sequences across three channels, with 500 images per class reserved for validation. Training used cross-entropy, Adam, plateau-based learning-rate reduction, and no augmentation. Averaging the last ten checkpoints, applying horizontal-flip test-time augmentation, and ensembling the three models raised the public score from about 0.947 per model to 0.950.

solution_title: [1100+ score on 7-Jan] Some simple strategy with notebook sharing!
solution_summary: The solution uses both players' current consecutive machine selections and recent selection streak lengths. It also incorporates reward decay, with reward-function design identified as another important factor. The author reports a score above 1150 on January 5 and approximately 1130 at the time of posting.

solution_title: 44th Place Silver - How To Improve Best Public Notebook
solution_summary: The author improved a public landmark Transformer by shrinking its width and sequence length while increasing its depth. These changes enabled an ensemble of four independently seeded models within the submission constraints, using TFLite FP16 quantization. Batch size, training duration, and temporal augmentation were also tuned, while external data and several spatial augmentations did not help. The author reports raising the public score from 0.73 to 0.77, with the published modifications reaching 0.76.

The team used Wi-Fi-based LSTM and MLP coordinate models alongside per-site LightGBM floor classifiers. They removed stale Wi-Fi observations, filled hidden waypoints, and weighted coordinate losses by timestamp alignment. A second training stage added pseudo-labeled test data and removed training examples with large out-of-fold errors. Repeated sensor-based correction, grid snapping, and device-ID leakage post-processing fed a stacked and weighted ensemble of four grid configurations.

The team replaced its initial Stable Diffusion image-to-SVG approach with text arranged under carefully designed dashed masks. This exploited the difference between OCR evaluation before enhancement and VQA evaluation afterward, allowing concealed text to support the VQA score. Efficient letter encoding and column-aware word placement produced a score of 0.652 before further aesthetic tuning. Subsequent work searched exposed letter combinations and adjusted text formatting, while DiffVG optimization failed.
compute: A100 used for the aesthetic letter and number combination search.

solution_summary: The approach used five random folds with EfficientNet-B5 Noisy Student and WSL ResNeXt101 as the strongest models. Training combined AdamW, warmup and cosine decay, Mixup and CutMix, and exponential moving averages. External font data and removal of the 300 hardest examples were also used. Distilling B5 into B3 matched cross-validation performance but performed much worse on the leaderboard, and the author reported a substantial private leaderboard drop.
compute: One machine with 4x GTX 1080 Ti

solution_title: 1st place solution for Algorithm Speed Prize
solution_summary: The pipeline used an SE-ResNet50 classifier to identify images requiring ship segmentation, followed by a modified LinkNet. Connected components were extracted from binary masks, and instances smaller than 80 pixels were removed. Segmentation training progressed through increasingly large crops, while location-based folds and balanced sampling supported both networks. Inference efficiency drove the design: GPU normalization saved about a minute, and the final LinkNet was at least ten times faster than the author's earlier model.
compute: K80 GPUs; kernel had two slow CPU cores. Inference took about 30 seconds for classification, 140 seconds for segmentation, and 40 seconds for instance extraction.

solution_summary: The solution modeled 512 independent subsets using variance-selected features and a sequence of QDA, pseudo-labeling, and Gaussian mixture clustering. Three Gaussian components per class supplied six cluster labels for a final QDA classifier, whose positive-class component probabilities were summed. Validation used synthetic datasets matching the inferred generation process rather than conventional folds. Randomness was deliberately retained, and two runs were selected randomly from 30 submissions; the best selected run achieved a private leaderboard AUC of 0.97588.

The team emphasized diversity across DeBERTa, RoBERTa, LUKE, and embedding-based SVR models, with prompt-based, keyword, multiscale, and contrastive training variants. Hill climbing selected a diverse subset that improved ensemble cross-validation. Carefully sampled pseudo-labeled essays and two-stage training produced substantial gains, with reported CV improvements of roughly 0.003 and 0.002–0.005 respectively. Layer freezing and reinitialization, adversarial weight perturbation, EMA, and recurrent pooling heads provided additional improvements.
external_data: ["Curated unlabeled essay corpus", "FB1 and FB2 essays excluding FB3"]

solution_summary: The solution used a vanilla transformer with separate projections for vertical, global, and handcrafted features, followed by positional encoding. A Fourier neural operator decoder produced per-token targets. Training combined MSE and L1 losses on the low-resolution dataset, with weighted target normalization and bf16 or fp32 precision. Monthly HDF5 storage and transformer-engine improved throughput and memory efficiency.
compute: 8x RTX 4090, approximately 100 GB RAM in DDP; fast M.2 NVMe storage; five to seven training epochs.

solution_summary: The final solution was a weighted average of nine models spanning six BERT variants, a BiLSTM, GPT-2 Large, and XLNet Large. BERT Large Cased was the strongest individual model, with a public score of 0.94482. All final models except the LSTM used a 95% training split and a 5% holdout, while the LSTM used the full dataset. Training used weighted sigmoid cross-entropy with different weighting schemes and target variants, including six auxiliary toxicity subtypes.

solution_summary: SSR used roughly 9,500 reasoning examples with an 80/20 training-validation split. Its five-stage curriculum combined clean examples, structural augmentation, adversarial traps, and self-critique, with clean anchors retained in harder stages. The aim was to teach rule inference and verification rather than algorithm recall. Results were not competitive; the author attributed this to insufficient examples and limitations of the dataset synthesizer.

solution_title: 5th place solution review | quick notes | private 0.917
solution_summary: The final approach blended the author's kinship predictions with several public submissions. The strongest described pipeline trained small neural heads over pairs of Dlib face descriptors, with anchor-based balanced batches and blending across validation folds. The author also trained seven face-description models using VGGFace2 and added their kinship predictions to the blend. The final public AUC reached 0.912, and the author reported that the submission generalized comparatively well to the private leaderboard.
external_data: ["VGGFace2", "Public submissions from hsinwenchang, shivamsarawagi, pasquale, and arjunrao2000"]

solution_summary: The solution focused on feature engineering for XGBoost, especially recent product ownership, product changes, and durations in each ownership state. Customer features included categorical codes, income ratios, age groups, and calendar indicators. Training used selected months from 2015 and 2016, and averaging predictions across random seeds improved performance and stability. Advanced imputation, fecha_alta, and broader ensembling or stacking did not provide useful gains.

The solution trained separate models for the 'is' relationship and all other relationships, using multilabel sigmoid outputs for the former and binary classification for the latter. Inception v4 encoded 128×128 detection crops, and its outputs were combined with box coordinates, geometric features, and relationship and label embeddings. Predictions were scaled using training-set relationship frequencies and YOLOv3 detection scores. Crops were prepared before training and stored in a Mongo database, and the author found that coordinates carried substantial information.
compute: Ryzen 5 CPU, 16 GB RAM, single GTX 1080 Ti

solution_summary: The final submission used a single LightGBM model with molecular fingerprints, selected external data, and additional pretrained embeddings for Rg prediction. Predicted properties were chained as features in the order Rg/FFV, Density, Tg, and Tc. Gaussian-mixture augmentation combined with inverse-similarity sample weights improved the public score, while validation excluded training molecules nearly identical to validation samples. The final LightGBM reported 0.0532 CV, 0.061 public, and 0.088 private, revealing a substantial generalization gap.

The solution built categorical features for tree ensembles and sparse binary features for linear-style models. The sparse representation included individual categories and second- and third-order categorical interactions. Merging rare binary features into fewer pooled features was a critical modification. The shared code covers part of the team's system, whose model outputs were blended.

solution_title: make use of representation learning methods
solution_summary: The submission used a single gradient boosting machine with raw attributes, feature statistics, and user-item interaction features. It also included score features derived from learned vector representations. The author developed a toolkit supporting graph embeddings and matrix factorization to represent network entities and estimate similarities. The post leaves the specific graph construction and embedding method unspecified.

The solution combined diverse models through hill climbing using clean out-of-fold and test predictions from 110 public models and 40 private models. A distinctive component nested neural-network classification of 50 price bins inside five-fold XGBoost regression, using the predicted class probabilities as features. The final hill climbing allowed negative weights and used a tolerance of 1e-5, which the author concluded overfit small validation improvements. Post-competition analysis showed that tolerance 1 improved the private score from 63057 to 63003 despite weaker validation and public scores.

solution_title: Kernel For Training Bert (The real stuff)
solution_summary: The final solution ensembled three BERT uncased large models, four BERT uncased base models, and five GPT2 models. Text preprocessing was minimal and was removed for GPT2. Training normally ran for two epochs with a warmup cosine schedule incorporating warmup restarts. The shared kernel took 2.5 hours to train for half an epoch.
compute: Shared kernel: 2.5 hours for 0.5 epoch; normally trained for 2 epochs.

solution_summary: The final agent uses a unified planner with orbital movement, cached distances, garrison projection and greedy wave planning. A PPO checkpoint gates poor launches, while a behavior-cloning policy breaks ties with a stability setting to limit aggression when behind. The best package used a maximum of 13 waves and achieved a public score of 1142.6. Split routing, static map routing and conservative mid-game changes did not outperform the unified agent.

The author submitted two distinct LightGBM strategies: a simple regression model and an augmented five-class classifier. The classifier expanded the training samples through commodity swapping and lags, used 15 features, and combined two LightGBM models before feature neutralization. Validation used ten chronological folds of 73 days each, but the regression model's stronger mean CV score did not translate into the stronger private score. The two submissions scored 0.242 and 0.385 privately, and deep learning experiments did not improve CV.

The solution used EfficientNet and SE-ResNet image classifiers trained at several resolutions with five-fold cross-validation. Training augmentation included horizontal and vertical flips, random resized crops, and normalization. The strongest reported configuration was a three-model EfficientNet B1-NS ensemble at resolution 512, scoring 0.43 public and 0.49 private without test-time augmentation. Test-time augmentation increased the reported private score to 0.50 for that configuration.

The pipeline fine-tuned a PERCH v2 audio backbone with a four-layer SED Transformer and dual attention and maximum-pooling heads. Training used weighted sampling, binary cross-entropy, cosine learning-rate scheduling, gain augmentation, masking, and mixup. Five-fold models were exported to ONNX and executed through OpenVINO, followed by metadata priors and temporal smoothing. Alternative backbones performed poorly, while the benefit of the small pseudo-labeled addition remained uncertain.
compute: Approximately 10 training epochs; hardware unspecified.

solution_summary: The pipeline used Mask R-CNN-family models pretrained on Livecell and fine-tuned on 256×256 crops. Removing the encoder's initial stride helped preserve resolution for small cells within single-GPU memory limits. Six models per cell type were combined through proposal, box, and mask averaging with flip augmentation. Customized suppression, small-mask removal, and astro-mask corruption refined predictions, producing a final score of 0.348 despite weaker private-set performance.
compute: Machines with a single RTX 2080 Ti; 4,000 fine-tuning iterations.

solution_title: Bronze Medal - 29 Hours of TPU Continued Training（TransUNet）
solution_summary: The author continued training a pretrained TransUNet with a seresnext50 backbone on 160-cubed inputs, reaching 830 epochs. TPU training was separated from CPU inference, with memory safeguards and validation-Dice checkpoint management. Three-level overlapping sliding-window inference, seven-fold test-time augmentation, and tuned postprocessing produced a single-model public score of 0.565 and private score of 0.582. Multi-checkpoint fusion slightly improved the public score but underperformed the single model privately.
compute: 8 TPU cores for training and CPU for inference; baselines used approximately 25 TPU hours and 40 hours on a T4 GPU.

solution_title: 5th Place Solution - A Compilation of my Code
solution_summary: The post shares a link to the author's challenge code. It says the code covers every challenge except crop2. No methods or results are described in the post itself.

The author implemented an agentic math solver that turns reasoning into executable Python and uses execution results to produce answers. A strict system prompt requires step-by-step reasoning, code generation, and verification. A template layer, solver engine, and execution tool form an iterative pipeline integrated with Kaggle inference. The post reports qualitative improvements across several mathematical domains but provides no numerical scores, model identity, or controlled comparisons.

The solution created almost 6,500 transaction features, including compressed identifier counts, monthly purchase aggregates, ratios, smoothed histories, and transaction timing statistics. Boruta, model importance, and adversarial validation produced different feature subsets. CatBoost was the best single model, with five-fold stratified validation scoring 3.645. The final approach stacked separate collections of models trained with and without outliers, then used an outlier classifier to combine predictions by replacing 10,000 values.
compute: Almost 8 hours for Boruta to select 500 features.

solution_summary: The solution combined around 45 base models trained mostly with similar hyperparameters but different seeds and learning rates. Cyclical features improved both validation and leaderboard performance for the MLP models. A shared target-encoding function was also helpful. The reported CV score was 0.97734 and the private score was 0.97757.

solution_title: Kernel for my (relative) beginner's 561st place solo submission
solution_summary: The author built a single-model LightGBM pipeline covering preprocessing, feature engineering, cross-validation, training, prediction generation, and post-processing. The cross-validation implementation incorporated target encoding intended to prevent data leakage. The solution did not use stacking and achieved a private leaderboard score of 0.79506. The accompanying kernel was presented as an end-to-end example for beginners.

solution_title: [379th]Public-state transaction graph for Pokemon TCG AI Battle
solution_summary: The final Ogerpon/Crustle agent used public-state rules organized as a transaction graph, with route arbitration, resource dependencies, and legal-action fallbacks. Behavior cloning and recurrent PPO experiments supplied useful parsers and diagnostics but did not become the submitted strategy. Improvements were promoted through replay audits, regression exams, matchup benchmarks, and packaging checks. The frozen submission scored 976.6 publicly, recorded 33 wins and 22 losses in filtered public replays, and passed 298 of 317 exam questions with no integrity or runtime errors.

solution_summary: The solution prioritized model diversity and combined ResNeXt50, ViT-B/16, EfficientNet-B4, and an unfine-tuned CropNet model. CropNet supplied particularly valuable diversity despite similar standalone accuracy. Cross-validation guided ensemble selection, and the final combination first averaged ViT and ResNeXt probabilities before summing them with EfficientNet and CropNet outputs. The ensemble scored 91.36% publicly and 91.32% privately, while a gradient-boosted stacking classifier failed to generalize adequately.
