solution_title: Pretrained model benchmark + 0.769 Private LB solution
solution_summary: The post benchmarks pretrained toxicity, hate-speech, offensive-language, and sentiment classifiers distributed as offline datasets. It also describes blending these models with Ridge Regression. The blend reportedly achieved 0.78959 public and 0.79641 private scores, but the authors did not select it for submission.

solution_title: 5th place solution: A thousand Epochs and a Crazy Transformer
solution_summary: The solution classified pressure values using deep transformers with handcrafted features and a learnable convolutional frontend. Its strongest architectural choices were substantial overparameterization, heavy dropout, ReZero residual weighting, and convolutions between encoder layers. Shortening sequences to 40 steps accelerated experiments without reducing cross-validation performance, and separate output heads handled the two u_out regimes. Models trained on the full dataset for 1,000 epochs across 15 seeds achieved 0.0999 public and 0.1022 private leaderboard scores.
compute: Five Google Colab Pro+ accounts enabled 15 parallel TPU sessions; 1,000 epochs took approximately 22 hours per model.

solution_summary: The solution used an EfficientNet-B3 encoder and LSTM decoder to predict SMILES strings, which were converted to InChI during inference. Predicting the shorter SMILES representation improved the reported error from 6.31 to 2.22. Training used approximately one million synthetic images, 288×288 inputs, and an adaptive sampler that favored examples with higher losses. Freezing the encoder for a final decoder-only training stage further improved the reported error from about 1.8 to 1.6 while enabling larger batches. Mixed precision helped accommodate training on a single 2080 Ti GPU.
compute: Single NVIDIA 2080 Ti GPU

solution_summary: The author selected 158 engineered features describing previous assessment performance, activity-word counts, and event-code game time. The final ensemble combined a LightGBM regressor, a neural network, and a classification model augmented with unused test assessments. Repeated random selection and truncation of installation histories supported QWK evaluation and tuning. Class-probability weights, blending, and thresholds were optimized using this validation setup.

The solution reshapes the 200 original variables into a long table containing a value, its count, and a categorical feature identifier, then trains LightGBM on those rows. Multiplying row predictions by customer produced about 0.9258 local AUC and 0.924 leaderboard AUC, with further gains from logistic regression over prediction aggregates. Standard scaling, reversing features with individual AUC below 0.5, and removing uninformative variables helped the approach. The long representation reduced opportunities for boosting to learn spurious interactions between otherwise independent variables.

solution_title: Why everybody uses `MultilabelStratifiedKFold` WRONG: unveiling the DECEPTION
solution_summary: The author focused on improving multilabel stratification across the target and several metadata columns. They reported that using categorical strings directly produced poorly balanced folds and advocated one-hot encoding the labels before stratification. Applying this validation approach to a public modeling kernel improved the reported private score from 0.49 to 0.41. The initial kernel submission explicitly omitted post-processing.

The solution used single-frame 512×512 U-Net segmentation models with EfficientNet encoders and averaged human annotations as soft targets. Orthogonalizing and standardizing all nine spectral channels improved global Dice by about 0.007–0.008. Five models with different encoders, losses, and augmentations were combined using weighted logits and eight-way test-time augmentation. Validation-tuned thresholds produced an ensemble private score of 0.71337.

solution_title: 226th (?!) Place Solution & Two-cents from a First-timer
solution_summary: The pipeline generated candidates from three item co-visitation matrices and ranked them using either rules or event-specific XGBRanker models. It selected 40 candidates per event type and built item, session, and interaction features, retaining a subset under computational limits. The learned ranker outperformed the author's rule-based approach but showed overfitting, while larger co-visitation neighborhoods added noise. Final submissions blended the author's rankers with public submissions using weights based on public scores. The stronger blend achieved 0.57855 on the private leaderboard.

The author used predictions from models trained on four dataset segments to study event errors and distinguish signal from noise. They then built two randomly sampled signal databases and one noise database, retaining the first 600 pulses per event while removing unnecessary fields. Three specialized models were trained and combined through direction-kappa-weighted aggregation, with a confidence threshold controlling the noise model's contribution. The revised databases occupied 809 GB, and the two signal models individually achieved reported leaderboard scores of 0.995 and 0.997.
compute: Signal models trained for 49 and 60 epochs; noise model trained for 40 epochs.

solution_title: Congratulations to the top teams and summary of the experience - top3%
solution_summary: The author combined an XGBoost model based on the classic raddar approach with a logistic regression model using different features. Both used only competition-provided data, with features selected for historical performance and sensible directional effects. Predictions were combined by increasing confidence when both models strongly agreed, which occurred alongside 94% overall agreement. The final submission contained no manual overwrites and still struggled with major tournament upsets.

The solution combined ten LightGBM runs, thirty neural-network runs, and a hand-built signal model in a weighted ensemble. Both learned model families used the original features, time-level feature averages, and selected investment-level rolling-mean deviations. The hand-built model contributed a small weight to improve directional behavior, while repeated learned models reduced initialization randomness. Validation on the last quarter of the data scored around 0.17, final full-data training scored around 0.15 on the leaderboard, and asymmetric prediction scaling added a small improvement.
compute: Kaggle notebooks with a 16 GB memory limit; split the dataset into two to fit.

solution_title: Draper Satellite Image Chronology: Pure ML Solution | Damien Soukhavong
solution_summary: The solution aligned and masked image sets, extracted general image features with ImageJ, and scored candidate chronological orders using XGBoost. Enumerating all 120 permutations of each five-image set converted ranking into regression and expanded the training data. Custom objectives, ranking-aware evaluation, and five theme-based validation folds supported model selection. External image tests showed limited generalization, while deep learning and random forests struggled with convergence or overfitting.
compute: About 1.5 hours for the initial pipeline, plus 10 minutes for five-fold validation.
external_data: ["Google Earth imagery for validation", "Personal photographs for validation"]

solution_title: Idea: use of precalculated genes embeddings - variation on Makotu (3-th place) theme
solution_summary: The post proposes representing each cell by averaging or summing biological embeddings of its most highly expressed genes. It discusses embeddings derived from expression datasets, biological graphs, and gene descriptions, while attributing a related word2vec approach to another participant. The authors report using description embeddings for feature selection and finding some useful protein-interaction feature candidates. A further untested suggestion is to apply PCA or SVD to a binary matrix marking each sample's top features.

The pipeline first extracted DOI and accession identifiers with regex and training-informed filters, assigning selected patterns directly to Primary. It then filtered candidates against an external corpus and used quantized Qwen models to identify document sections, extract metadata, and classify DOIs as primary or secondary. Classification prompts depended on whether a passage came from the body or references, and decoding used logit restrictions. Broad accession patterns produced many false positives, while an additional LLM validity filter offered little improvement and was omitted.

solution_title: Top 9th Solution: Simple but complete approach.
solution_summary: The team used a two-stage pipeline that detected characters and then classified crops around their predicted centers. Detection evolved from a U-Net center heatmap model to an Hourglass detector producing heatmaps and character dimensions, while an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet18 handled classification. Grouped validation, image augmentations, MixUp, and background training examples supported generalization, with classification validation accuracy reaching 94.6%. Low-character predictions supplied blank pseudo-labels to address drawings, while a proposed geometric ensemble failed because of implementation bugs.
compute: Detection training: 20 epochs

solution_summary: The solution uses variance-based feature selection and kernel PCA, then adds distribution features named GMM_PRED, GMM_SCORE, and HIST_PRED. A first layer of diverse classifiers feeds LightGBM and an MLP, with predictions from both layers averaged. Duplicating some GMM features unexpectedly improved leaderboard scores, and the linked kernel achieved a public score of 0.97491. Standard PCA, SVD, and autoencoder variants failed, as did an attempt to select models using simulated public and private datasets.

The post announces the availability of code and documentation and links to a GitHub repository. It reports reproduced scores of 0.0029 for the best single model and 0.0023 for an ensemble. The supplied text does not explain the models or pipeline.

The solution combined four-fold eca_nfnet_l2 and efficientnet_v2_m models using 512×512 inputs from channels 0, 2, and 4. Training used geometric augmentation and mixup, while inference used five test-time views. SHOT and pseudo-labeling addressed the training-to-test domain shift, with ensembles combining models trained on all pseudo-labels and only highly reliable pseudo-labels. Larger images improved both cross-validation and leaderboard performance, while several alternative losses, domain adaptation methods, and preprocessing ideas were unsuccessful.

The solution detected cell centers with two 3D U-Net heatmap models and linked candidates using a public Transformer edge predictor and ILP tracking pipeline. Sparse-label weighted BCE, background references from FOCUS-3D, and iterative pseudo-labeling from tracking output supported detector training. The final blend equally averaged ResEnc-L and Kinetics-pretrained ResNet3D-18 logits, while a second selected submission used ResEnc-L alone; both scored 0.943 privately. Detector changes produced the larger private gains, whereas several public improvements from post-processing did not transfer, and shared localization errors remained unresolved.
models_pretrained: ["Kinetics-400 pretrained R(2+1)D-18", "Kinetics-400 pretrained ResNet3D-18", "FOCUS-3D", "UNet-Transformer edge predictor", "ResEnc-L with MAE-pretrained encoder"]

solution_title: 18th solution. Single swin transformer with custom head, with code.
solution_summary: The author used a single Swin Large architecture trained across ten folds in plain PyTorch. Its distinguishing feature was an ordinal-style regression head with fixed bin boundaries. Validation used RMSE computed over all out-of-fold predictions, giving 17.25. Further training on pseudo-labeled data from the previous PetFinder competition produced only a tiny improvement, and submissions using either checkpoint set or both scored similarly.

The solution ensembled 14 U-Net and U-Net++ segmentation models with ResNeSt and EfficientNet encoders. Models jointly predicted four masks derived from different levels of annotator agreement. Training also used pseudo-labeling and rotation, brightness/contrast, dropout, and grid-shuffle augmentation.

The team solved cubes by repeatedly applying an existing solver to 5×5×5 subproblems, then greedily aligning remaining interior pieces with three-point rotations. They handled differently labeled cubes through recoloring and the same procedure. Globe puzzles were decomposed into single-layer problems with restricted flips and three-point swaps, while wreaths used a simple heuristic. Postprocessing and parallel runs with different parameters substantially improved the score.

The final solution averaged four BERT base-uncased models and retained the beginning and end of texts exceeding the sequence limit. Its representation combined BERT pooled and sequence outputs with global average pooling. Validation used ten multilabel-stratified folds, and selected target predictions were mapped to the training target distributions. Numerous alternatives, including external pretraining, other transformers, and architectural changes, did not help.

The solution used four levels: image models, tabular models combining image scores and metadata, a second stacking layer, and final logistic regression. Four image models were diversified through sampling ratios and training duration, while repeated undersampling and bagging supported the later levels. Patient-grouped, stratified 10-fold validation guided experiments, and final models were retrained on all data. Metadata engineering and combining image scores with tabular models delivered the largest gains; the final stack achieved 0.183 CV and 0.169 private score.

solution_title: 5th place: Finding the SigNeedle in the NoiseStack
solution_summary: The author built ensembles from 25 models using AutoGluon and ridge regression. The AutoGluon ensemble achieved the lowest CV error, but its larger public leaderboard gap suggested overfitting, so the author preferred a ridge ensemble with a more typical gap. The final submission blended the author's ensembles with a strong public notebook and achieved a private leaderboard score of 38.63455.
compute: Mostly used Kaggle notebooks; encountered GPU and memory limitations.

solution_summary: The team combined graph neural networks and recurrent models for neutrino direction reconstruction. Graph models used normalized detector measurements, ice properties, and hit-relation features, while recurrent models used four LSTM/GRU layers and staged fine-tuning. Rotation test-time augmentation, uncertainty-based expert models, and recurrent-model weight averaging strengthened the component predictions. The final blend used regression-tree-defined bins to adjust angular blending weights, improving on constant weights and fixed angular bins.
compute: Datasaurus: 2× RTX 3090, 128 GB RAM; preprocessing ~8 hours on 32 threads and ~1 TB storage; GPS ~11 hours/epoch. Isamu: RTX 3090, 64 GB RAM, 8 TB HDD, 2 TB SSD, Colab Pro. Remek: initially 2× A5000, later dual Xeon and A6000.
external_data: ["DeepCore DOM quantum-efficiency information", "Published ice scattering and absorption lengths"]

solution_title: Deep Q* Learning with simplified game ~1200
solution_summary: The agent used deep Q-learning with a model of roughly 20 million parameters. The game representation centered the head, oriented it north, and reduced actions to three movements. Training used a league of agents with Elo ratings, while inference applied horizontal and adversary flips. MuZero and vector-quantized planning were future directions rather than implemented components.

solution_title: 699th Rank for Bengali.AI Speech Recognition Challenge!
solution_summary: The author fine-tuned pretrained OpenAI Whisper-small for Bengali speech recognition using the Hugging Face trainer. Training ran for up to 200,000 steps with a learning rate of 1e-5 and batch size of 12 on a 12GB RTX 3080 Ti. Audio was normalized and randomly augmented through pitch changes, speed changes, and MUSAN background noise or music. These augmentations provided little scoring benefit, and the author identified data cleaning and better coverage of test domains as priorities for improvement.
compute: 12GB RTX 3080 Ti; training up to 200,000 steps.

solution_summary: The final submission combined a regularized generalized linear model, a random forest, and bagged linear support vector machines using a weighted average. The linear model used Lasso or elastic net regularization. The teammates developed separate feature sets that both combined time-domain and frequency-domain information.

solution_title: Long live Wikipedia: Dell Zhang on placing third in Wikipedia's Participation Challenge
solution_summary: The solution modeled recent changes in users' edit counts and numbers of edited articles. Choosing suitable temporal scales made these behavioral dynamics highly predictive. OpenCV's gradient boosted trees outperformed the other tested methods, with parameters tuned on a large validation dataset shared by another participant.
external_data: ["Validation dataset shared by Twan van Laarhoven"]

solution_summary: The solution used a two-stage pipeline combining a 3D U-Net ensemble with heuristic probability extraction. A ResNet3D backbone predicted 13 heatmaps supervised by Gaussian kernels centered on aneurysm coordinates. Non-maximum suppression identified peaks, and candidates below the top three were suppressed with an exponent of 1.5 before computing an overall presence probability. Five-fold validation scored approximately 0.75, while both public and private leaderboard scores were 0.73.

solution_title: [URGENT] Write-up reverted to Draft after adding teammate before deadline

solution_summary: The solution combined a pretrained wav2vec2 speech recognition model with a six-gram KenLM language model. ASR training began with Common Voice, Fleur, and Bn data, followed by stages described as using 10% and 20% data. Audio augmentation included speed, volume, reverberation, and noise changes, and training used learning-rate warmup. Inference applied Bengali character-combination corrections, while the language model used competition text and external training data.
external_data: ["Common Voice", "Fleur data", "Bn data", "Unspecified external language-model training data"]

solution_summary: A shared-backbone XLM-RoBERTa-large biencoder retrieved 50 content candidates, followed by a multilingual BERT crossencoder trained on out-of-fold retrieval results. Language-matched batches and candidates, bidirectional cross-entropy, and a positive-class margin improved retrieval, reaching 91% recall@50 on CV. Positive oversampling and differential learning rates improved the crossencoder, which achieved 63.6% CV and 68.3% private leaderboard scores. Post-processing supplied a nearest neighbor for empty predictions and reused contents from matching topic hierarchies.

The solution used a GRU encoder-decoder with explicit seasonal lags and page-level features to forecast web traffic. Lagged observations outperformed the more complex attention approach and allowed shorter encoders. Training used random temporal windows, a smoothed SMAPE loss, and COCOB with gradient clipping. Walk-forward validation guided tuning, while final models trained without validation. Averaging 30 checkpoints across three seeds, with averaged weights within each checkpoint, reduced variance and produced future-data SMAPE similar to historical validation.

The solution used XGBoost trained on June and December 2015 accounts that added products. Eleven months of lagged product ownership and other engineered features were central to the approach. A 100-model ensemble provided only a small additional gain. The author also provided runnable binary and multiclass single-model variants reported to exceed 0.0305 on the public leaderboard.

solution_title: A throughput floor plus a genuine multi-step search
solution_summary: The author built a three-phase attack search guided by direct inspection of the competition SDK and hosted gateway code. It allocated budget to a public guardrail argument-ordering exploit, a confused-deputy mechanism, and novelty-driven exploration of fixture cross-references. The best public score was 19.560, but the private score was 0.030, attributable to one surviving confused-deputy finding. Benign priming and reward-weighted archive selection were tested and reverted after lowering public scores.

The final speech recognition pipeline combined a single Wave2Vec model with an N-gram language model. An initial model trained on external speech datasets identified noisy competition samples, excluding those with WER above 0.5 before a longer training stage. Dataset caching, increased warmup, and an MSD output layer helped, while additional fine-tuning led to overfitting. Adding the language model improved the reported public leaderboard score from 0.407 to 0.396.

The solution emphasized diversity by combining nine 2.5D segmentation models trained along three axes with three 3D models. Validation used five folds grouped by case. Averaging model outputs and applying a 0.3 threshold improved the public score from a best single-model score of 0.875 to 0.889. Removing predictions smaller than 50 pixels increased it to 0.890.
compute: Z by HP Z8G4 Workstation with dual A6000 GPUs, 48 GB per GPU; used to train many models.

solution_summary: The solution trains XGBoost with both competition data and original data while controlling their distribution mismatch through sample weights. Original observations receive prognosis-dependent weights to reproduce the competition data's prognosis distribution. A grid-searched multiplier further controls the relative contribution of the two sources, and weights are also supplied to evaluation sets. Original data supports fitting and early stopping but is excluded from model selection; the author reports that one submission performed well on both public and private evaluations.

The solution combined DeBERTa-v3-large models trained on different mixtures of competition and external data. Overlapping tokenizer windows covered long essays while word IDs mapped predictions back to essay tokens. A fixed holdout guided model-specific thresholds, after which voting combined the models. Custom synthetic data, Longformer, LLM predictions, weighted averaging, and class-weighted losses did not help.

The solution used three levels of models to detect six movement events from EEG while preserving temporal causality. Subject-specific first-level models extracted covariance, evoked-potential, and low-frequency signal information. Global second-level models learned event relationships and temporal structure from prediction histories, with bagging improving robustness. AUC-optimized weighted ensembles formed the third level, and the final YOLO submission averaged 18 such ensembles, achieving 0.98109 private AUC.
compute: Workstation with 12x3.5GHz cores, 64 GB RAM, 120GB SSD, and Nvidia GeForce Titan Black; level one takes 3–4 days and level two 1–2 days.

solution_title: 4th Place Solution - Split images into tiles and do 3D CNN
solution_summary: The solution removed large white background regions from very large pathology images before splitting them into tiles. A 3D CNN learned from the resulting tiles. The author reported stable local cross-validation without post-processing.

solution_title: 38th place (silver): what actually moved the score
solution_summary: The solution improved report-derived targets by applying clinical thresholds and distinguishing below-threshold findings from explicit negatives and omissions. A training-only site bias absorbed reporting habits, while complementary whole-knee and landmark-crop models supplied different anatomical views. Conservative nested validation screened changes before a percentile-rank ensemble combined surviving model legs with timeout protection. The reported final scores were 0.964 public and 0.952 private.

The solution combined EEG signals with supplied and EEG-derived spectrograms in three models: EfficientNet-B1, ResNet-1D plus EfficientNet-B1, and WaveNet plus EfficientNet-B1. Training used patient-grouped five-fold validation, two-stage training, label refinement, and CutMix. The three model predictions were combined with weights of 0.34, 0.32, and 0.34. Teacher and student models were both retained to mitigate possible drift from two-stage training, with reported public scores of 0.29 and 0.27.

The solver served gpt-oss-120b through vLLM and generated eight independently seeded, Python-enabled attempts per problem. Minimal prompts replaced elaborate reasoning scaffolds, while inverse-entropy voting selected answers and four matching attempts triggered early stopping. Adaptive time budgets gave difficult problems additional time within the notebook limit. The public score rose from 40/50 to 45/50 after prompt and configuration changes, with no isolated attribution; retries and several verifier-based pipelines did not improve the final configuration.
compute: Single H100; notebook runtime limit 17,400 seconds, approximately 4 hours 50 minutes.

solution_summary: The solution blended many Regularized Greedy Forest tree ensembles using a generalized linear model with exponential loss and nonnegative coefficients. It mostly retained the supplied features, added features from new particle combinations, accounted for physical symmetries, and removed unhelpful phi features. Submodels estimated either the weighted signal-to-background ratio directly or its class-probability and conditional-weight components separately. The two target formulations performed similarly individually, while blending them gave the best results; the blend was fitted on seven-fold out-of-fold predictions.
compute: Used Amazon EC2 m2.4xlarge instances; recommends 8+ CPU cores and 64+ GB RAM with about 2 days per training script. Each script trains 8 models in parallel.

solution_summary: The solution combined an EfficientNet-B6 binary classifier with YOLOv5, EfficientD6, and VFNet detectors. Weighted boxes fusion consolidated training boxes, and customized fusion at postprocessing improved mAP by 0.015. YOLOv5 training used multiple mosaic variants and quadruple mean teachers with a ramped consistency-loss weight. The classifier achieved AUC 0.992 and AP 0.96, while mean teachers improved detection cross-validation by about 0.02 mAP but added little ensemble diversity.

solution_title: Jack of Trades, Loser of Cryptarithm
solution_summary: The writeup describes synthetic problem generation and structured reasoning traces, reserving all supplied training examples for validation. Generators reproduce observed ranges, noise, vocabulary, and problem formats across five puzzle families. The most detailed work constructs byte-consistent bit-manipulation reasoning using primitive operators, valid continuations, and compact encodings. An initial exhaustive reasoning format performed poorly through hallucinated rules and fallback answers; the excerpt ends with formatting revisions rather than a complete final training recipe.

solution_title: Megatron: LoRA Fine-Tuning of Nemotron-3-Nano-30B for Structured Reasoning
solution_summary: The author fine-tunes Nemotron-3-Nano-30B using rank-32 LoRA initialized from Kien's public tinker-adapter. Conservative delta scaling anchors updates to the initial adapter, and Unsloth supports training with offline dependencies and fallback Mamba operations. The short 150-step run achieved 0.86, compared with 0.85 for a 3,000-step run using broader adapter training and cosine decay. Local generation validation failed because of GPU memory pressure, making competition evaluation the source of reported accuracy.
compute: Single NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition, 94.97 GB; both runs completed within nine hours; peak memory 73.8 GB and 94.4 GB.

solution_title: 15th place solution - Don't Test At Home
solution_summary: The agent uses an Extra Trees-style ensemble inspired by an earlier decision-tree agent. It fits randomized trees with one candidate feature for as much of each turn's time budget as possible. An internal timer limits fitting to the first 950 milliseconds, adapting the number of trees to server load and fitting cost. Accumulated tree probabilities then weight random action selection.
compute: 950 milliseconds of tree fitting per turn; tree counts varied from 100 to over 800 with server load and fitting steps.

solution_title: Public -> 254 rank, Private -> 42 rank, and Potential Top 15 solution
solution_summary: The submitted approach stacked nine AutoGluon models with a RidgeClassifier and combined the resulting predictions by mode. The AutoGluon models used different collections of CatBoost, XGBoost, and LightGBM models. A basic CatBoost baseline treated every feature as a string without cleaning and achieved mean out-of-fold accuracy of 0.94059 across 15 folds. An alternative AutoGluon stack using 24 base models trained over 20 folds was evaluated but not selected.
compute: Single CatBoost 15-fold run: CPU total 1h 4min 50s; wall time 2min 48s.

solution_title: 8th place solution. And gold on last attempt
solution_summary: The solution ensembled sound event detection models with an EfficientNet-B0 backbone across several preprocessing and training variants. Manual removal of segments without bird sounds, audio chunking, secondary-label targets, and inference-time class weights improved the earlier models. A later variant used normalized Kaldi filterbank features, random five-second crops, per-class sampling, and scheduled mixup, followed by mean-median aggregation and class-specific prediction boosts. The final submission averaged the best previous ensemble with a model trained on confidence-filtered recordings, achieving a private score of 0.79 compared with 0.78 for the previous best.

The final submission closely followed a public notebook, replacing DeBERTa-v3-base with DeBERTa-v3-large. Training ran in Google Colab. Masked-language-model training, adding prompt material to the input, and feeding manual features into the NLP head did not help. The author identified the small number of training prompts and the absence of shared prompt IDs between training and test data as central challenges.
compute: Training performed in a Google Colab notebook; hardware and duration unspecified.

solution_title: 6th place solution in 3 days - AutoGluon + AutoXGB
solution_summary: The solution combined AutoGluon pipelines with an independently tuned XGBoost model using weights based on cross-validation scores. One AutoGluon pipeline used eight folds and one stacking level, while another used pseudo-labels from the first models. Both the original and generated datasets were used. AutoGluon training took about 13 hours, and XGBoost hyperparameter tuning took about 24 hours.
compute: Approximately 13 hours for the two AutoGluon solutions and approximately 24 hours for XGBoost hyperparameter tuning; hardware unspecified.

solution_summary: The pipeline first segmented organs in 3D to define study crops, then classified injury using 2.5D CNN or CoaT backbones with GRUs. Organ visibility from segmentation masks supplied slice-level soft targets, while auxiliary segmentation losses stabilized training and improved scores. Predictions were maximized across slices and ensembled across folds, architectures, and preprocessing variants. The reported ensemble OOF score was 0.31x, compared with 0.326 for the best single four-fold model.

solution_title: Compact description of the competition problem(958th place)
solution_summary: The author frames surface classification as reconstruction of a directed graph whose nodes represent sensor series. Manually labeled connections from orientation data train a connectivity classifier, while a separate classifier estimates probabilities for eight surface types without orientation features. These edge and label probabilities define a graph reconstruction problem, but the post does not provide a completed reconstruction algorithm or quantitative results. It also suggests using reconstructed motion extents to distinguish two hard-tile classes.

The solution generated candidate word arrangements with large simulated annealing runs, then refined them through smaller local searches. Refinement used local windows and replacements of n-grams up to length four. For ID 4, strings and perplexities were cached to avoid repeated computation. Once perplexity fell below 70, the first ten and last four words were fixed during further annealing.

The team generated full-resolution CT images using publicly shared windowing and extracted image metadata. CNNs first predicted image-level pulmonary embolism, followed by an LSTM producing image- and exam-level predictions. They used five-fold validation and optimized the sequence model directly for the competition metric. EfficientNet experiments suffered from overfitting.
compute: Used a cloud provider for remaining experiments after encountering Kaggle kernels' 5GB disk limit.

solution_summary: The author created additional binary toxicity labels and more-toxic/less-toxic pairs, then trained several pretrained language models. Models used either binary cross-entropy or margin-ranking loss, with larger models generally performing better in cross-validation. Training used a maximum sequence length of 256, AdamW, and a linear warmup schedule over one to three epochs. Optuna tuned weighted ensemble predictions using out-of-fold pair-ordering accuracy.

solution_title: A quick summary of Team Mystic (3rd place) solution
solution_summary: The solution combined historical demand statistics and recent weekly measurements with interaction signals learned by linear and factorization models. Features were generated from earlier weeks, and models trained on a later week predicted subsequent weeks. A single XGBoost model using both feature groups achieved the reported public leaderboard score.

The pipeline used breast ROI detection followed by four ConvNeXt-small classifiers at 2048×1024 resolution, trained with additional mammography datasets. Positive oversampling, extensive augmentation, dropout, and soft positive labels supported training on the imbalanced data. YOLOX-nano supplied breast crops, with thresholding and whole-image fallbacks. A later ablation found that external data improved F1 by about 0.02, while soft positive labels did not clearly outperform standard label smoothing.

solution_title: 9th place - Custom CUDA kernel for wave propagation
solution_summary: The solution used CaFormer and ConvNeXtV2 models with an emphasis on efficient experimentation and augmentation. A custom batched CUDA wave propagation implementation regenerated seismograms from augmented targets about 100 times faster than the original CPU implementation. Training runs were continued at a constant learning rate before cosine-scheduled refinement with extra weight on difficult classes. Predictions were combined using a median across recent checkpoints followed by a mean across runs.
compute: GPU wave propagation with a custom CUDA kernel; approximately 100x faster than the original CPU implementation.

solution_summary: The post proposes post-processing predictions with a target-specific array of rater counts. Each prediction column is first min-max normalized. Predictions are then rounded to discrete increments determined by the corresponding rater count. The author invites others to test the method but provides no measured improvement.

The final system retrieved context with TF-IDF over a Wikipedia STEM corpus expanded by 159K articles, then ensembled three DeBERTa-v3-large models. Retrieval improvements mattered most: sublinear term frequency and corpus expansion each produced measurable leaderboard gains. Models used different training and validation subsets, including question-length matching to the competition data. The ensemble favored strong, weakly correlated models and simple weight combinations after validation-based weight optimization proved unreliable.

The authors trained four network models with different random seeds for the Galaxy Zoo challenge. Their best reported score was 0.08246. Training took about six days on two NVIDIA Titan cards, but the post gives little architectural or inference detail.
compute: 2 NVIDIA Titan cards; about 6 days of training for 4 models

solution_title: 4th Place – Residual XGBoost + Meta NN + Hill Climb Opt
solution_summary: The solution centered on XGBoost residual models, engineered delta features, and Optuna parameter tuning. Fourteen XGBoost models incorporated shared out-of-fold predictions as additional features, followed by a neural network meta-blender trained with 17 seeds. Hill climbing optimized ensemble weights, and final blending combined the strongest neural and hill-climbing results. Reported cross-validation improved from 0.05598 initially to 0.055821 after hill climbing.

The author built the agent using HandyRL, although input and model details are absent from the provided text. Inference summed outputs from the three best leaderboard models and selected the highest-scoring legal direction, excluding reversal of the previous action. Each checkpoint was evaluated over 100 games against one imitation-learning agent and two copies of a public reinforcement-learning agent. The highest-scoring new checkpoint each day was submitted.

The final solution trained a BigGAN with a 10M-parameter generator and an 8M-parameter discriminator to generate 64×64 dog images. It removed extreme-aspect-ratio and intruder images, used the supplied bounding boxes, and applied random crops and horizontal flips. BCE loss, Adam, label smoothing, and truncated noise sampling were used without EMA. Earlier DCGAN and AC-GAN variants performed worse; the final reported scores were 31.09602 public and 55.42142 private.
compute: 130 epochs, 32-image batches, 32,400-second maximum kernel runtime

solution_summary: Customers were divided into recent buyers, historical buyers without recent purchases, and customers with no purchase history. Customers with history received candidates from nine retrieval methods, while customers without history received popular items. Each retrieval method supplied 100 items per customer before deduplication. LightGBM ranking and binary models used item and customer aggregates, purchase-window interactions, recency, and retrieval scores, followed by an ensemble based on a linked public method.

The author adapted a starter pipeline to a three-channel 1D ResNet using the accelerometer signals. Training used 1000 ms cuts with 50 ms of future context and a plateau-based learning-rate scheduler. Five models trained on the notebook's folds were ensembled for submission. Cross-validation was approximately 0.30, with public and private scores of 0.351 and 0.356.
compute: RTX 3060; about one hour per model including validation.

solution_summary: The solution used LightGBM with regular-season statistics and a rating derived from averaged system ranks. Added basketball efficiency features included true shooting percentage, the Four Factors, points per possession, and possessions. Four models each held out one season from 2016–2019 while training on the remaining seasons from 2003–2019, and their probabilities were averaged. Neural networks did not work, and the reported competition score was 0.56346.

The team used out-of-fold teacher predictions to softly relabel about 500 suspicious training images, improving EfficientNet B4 cross-validation accuracy from 0.899 to 0.915. They added deduplicated 2019 cassava images and confidence-filtered, pseudo-labeled Mendeley plant images exclusively to training. Six pretrained architectures were trained across five folds using strong augmentation, progressive resizing, and mixed precision with gradient accumulation. Their two final submissions used prediction averaging or maximum-confidence selection, achieving private scores of 0.896 and 0.897 respectively.

solution_title: How I missed a gold medal in my first kaggle competition (could've got 13th place)
solution_summary: The author described a dataset-mention extraction notebook that achieved a private leaderboard score of 0.444 but was not selected for final evaluation. It split training text into 256-token chunks, retained all positive chunks, and discarded half of the negative chunks. The model initialized a binary classification head from the O and MISC output weights of a CoNLL03-fine-tuned XLM-RoBERTa model and trained for three epochs. The selected submission instead came from a leaderboard-probing notebook whose method was not detailed.

solution_title: 31th/5k+ with 1 single model without stacking and blending possible, wow!
solution_summary: The author expresses satisfaction with their competition result as a beginner in machine learning. They thank the participants and competition organizers. The post provides no modeling, training, or validation details.

The solution used RGB images and an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet50 with a two-layer classification head. External data and oversampling were particularly helpful, with binary cross-entropy outperforming focal loss. Training used five folds and progressed from 256-pixel to 512-pixel images, with layer-specific learning rates and a cyclical schedule. Averaging eight test-time augmentations and applying a 0.2 threshold produced public and private scores of 0.595 and 0.523.
compute: Tesla V100; approximately 35 hours training

solution_title: 3th on Public and 6th on Private, A Very Simple Solution: Big Pretrained-Model is All You Need!
solution_summary: The pipeline randomly selected 1,000 tiles per image, duplicating tiles when necessary, and extracted 768-dimensional features using pretrained iBOT-ViT-Base weights. Chowder multiple-instance learning models classified these image-level feature sets. Seven models were ensembled, with average prediction entropy and an adjusted threshold used to identify the other class. Ensemble uncertainty estimation raised the public score from 0.59 to 0.65, while a PathDINO patch-selection method did not improve results.

solution_title: 51th place solution. Single Model. Private Score 0.35175, Public Score 0.24019.
solution_summary: The author adapted shared competition code and used cropping and padding to reduce overfitting to sequence lengths in the public and private data. Cropping plus padding achieved the best reported score, 0.35175, compared with 0.35215 without either operation. Cropping alone produced a slightly worse score of 0.35274.

The author blended LightGBM, XGBoost, CatBoost, and DenseLight predictions from two complementary feature sets. One set contained 1,504 engineered features, while the other combined public tabular features with DistilRoBERTa predictions from reconstructed essays. Compressing repeated q characters into run lengths improved transformer tokenization, and all tabular models were averaged over ten folds and five seeds. The final weighted blend achieved CV 0.5870 and private score 0.563; later DeBERTa experiments showed additional possibilities beyond the submitted approach.

The solution used a two-stage retrieval and reranking pipeline based on FlagEmbedding, with Qwen2.5-32B for both stages. Each model was trained sequentially on two external datasets and then competition training data. Stage-specific retrieval models generated hard negatives for the corresponding reranker stages, and cross-device negatives improved retrieval training. Reranking the top 18 candidates increased the public score from 0.582 to 0.623.

solution_title: Try to improve your solution with the leak
solution_summary: The author improved predictions from an existing public kernel without training any models. The main improvement exploited the observation that examples sharing an incidence angle almost always shared a label. Predictions agreeing with training labels were pushed toward clipped certainty, while disagreements were resolved through majority voting within angle groups. Extending certainty to consistent groups with angles absent from training improved the public score but not the private score.

solution_title: 10th place: BC + PPO on a Single RTX 5090
solution_summary: A single 21.83M-parameter policy learned from recent leaderboard replays through behavior cloning and then approximately 370M PPO environment steps. Its architecture combined a ResNet map encoder, attention, and autoregressive unit and market heads with legal-action masks. Fresh imitation data, larger networks, realistic recorded opponents, and game-aligned action representations drove the largest gains. Training took approximately 23 hours on one RTX 5090, and inference used greedy decoding without search or ensembling.
compute: One RTX 5090; approximately 23 h total, including 3.5 h data preparation/BC and 19 h PPO; approximately 18 ms per turn locally.

solution_title: 41st Solution to AI Agent Security: Multi-Step Tool Attacks
solution_summary: The public approach used model-adapted prompt structures, reliable singleton candidates, and compact URL variations to maximize replay throughput against synthetic tool guardrails. Moving candidate variation late in prompts and ordering candidates by token-prefix similarity improved opportunities for persistent KV-cache reuse. The public POST family scored zero privately, while an orthogonal synthetic email CONFUSED_DEPUTY strategy achieved a private score of 26.85. Deferred Harmony Injection demonstrated control-token materialization on GPT-OSS without reliable behavioral takeover, and multi-action variants failed to outperform singleton flooding.
compute: Local 15-run replay comparison: approximately 1.58 s with earlier domain novelty versus 1.13 s with novelty moved toward the end.

solution_title: 0.480 public LB solutions! (ensemble of 7 fingerprint/SMILES/atom-level features models)
solution_summary: The solution combined molecular fingerprint neural models, feature-mixture models, and fingerprint-based LightGBM. Individual models scored 0.615–0.650 under 15-fold validation, while their public leaderboard scores varied substantially. Ensembling all models reached approximately 0.480 on the public leaderboard. The author attributed the weaker graph model performance partly to omitting bond features and suggested SMILES-based models were better suited to the private leaderboard.

solution_title: First solo gold, 7th place solution: transformers with convolution/deconvolution
solution_summary: The solution used ConvTransformerEncoder models that combined local convolutions with global self-attention. Convolved base-pair probability and distance matrices supplied attention biases, while deconvolutions restored dimensions for residual stacking. Sequence-reconstruction pretraining and variation in model depth, kernel size, and training-data quality thresholds supported a diverse ensemble. The final ensemble used only models without positional encoding and averaged the central portion of predictions with beta=0.7, improving the reported score from 0.34701 to 0.34550.

This post describes one contributor's portion of a larger ensemble, combining different preprocessing pipelines with boosted trees and neural architectures. Features included integer and raw inputs, temporal aggregations, 50 PCA components, and products of globally ranked features sharing a trend. Models comprised LightGBM with a combined focal and log loss, XGBoost, fully connected networks, and a dual-input fully connected plus Transformer model. The hybrid model alternated training its branches while freezing the other branch for roughly 30 epochs per stage.

The approach focused on avoiding overfitting, selecting models with local five-fold cross-validation, and then training on all available data. Averaging five models improved the private score from 99.180 to 99.280, and pseudo-labeling increased it further to 99.420. Several training and inference tricks produced no significant improvement.

solution_title: Pseudo Data Augmentation (27th place short writeup)
solution_summary: The author created two predictive features by training models on previous loans and applying them to current applications. One LightGBM model estimated whether a previous loan had payments more than three days late, using all installments, while another predicted mean days past due. Previous-loan attributes replaced corresponding application fields during training. Together, the two generated features improved cross-validation performance by about 0.003.

The author trained 24-class audio classifiers on log-mel spectrograms, starting with masked binary cross-entropy on verified positive and negative annotations. Repeated soft pseudo-labeling and retraining raised initial scores from about 0.86 to the 0.96 range, with verified regions sampled half the time to limit confirmation bias. A normalized frequency-coordinate channel improved local metrics, and the final ensemble combined EfficientNet and ReXNet models across four folds. Inference used half-second sliding windows, maximum pooling over each clip, and averaging across models.

The author trained a modified Qwen2-VL model to convert ARC grids into object-based Python representations using roughly 850,000 synthetic grids. Its visual embedding was adapted to discrete colors, and its input arrangement preserved two-dimensional positional information. The resulting representations supported induction and transduction solvers trained on filtered BARC puzzles. Combining several models scored 8 hidden-test points, and merging with a public notebook increased that notebook's score from 26 to 27.

The author used pageviews, mobile status, channel grouping, country, metro, and an aggregated new-visits feature. Categorical features were one-hot encoded and reduced to 24 columns with PCA. LinearSVR performed best among the tested regression models, including nonlinear SVR and several tree-based alternatives.

The post recounts a broad experimental search rather than specifying the final team pipeline. The author trained 96 full-fold models and obtained reasonable progress with shallow four-layer 1D networks before exploring many alternative representations, augmentations, and architectures. Trials included gravitational-wave injection, pretraining, constant-Q transforms, signal transformations, and transformer models. Some approaches had explicit limitations, including poorly converging 2D networks and extended-signal whitening that did not improve performance.

solution_title: Aevion Nemotron v0.19 — P100 sm_60 blocker, pretrained adapter packaging, and Open Contribution write-up
solution_summary: The final v0.19 submission packaged a public pretrained LoRA adapter for the competition's Nemotron base model without additional training. The notebook copied the adapter files, normalized the base-model and inference metadata, and generated submission.zip. An earlier locally trained notebook adapter scored 0.85 public and 0.84 private, but subsequent training attempts failed because the allocated P100 was incompatible with the installed software stack and lacked sufficient memory. The final packaged adapter's score was still pending.
compute: Failed training attempts: Tesla P100-PCIE-16GB (sm_60). Final packaging notebook: no GPU required, completes in a few minutes.

solution_summary: The author primarily represented comments using character n-grams and trained logistic regression with scikit-learn. These features and the linear classifier formed the core of the reported solution. The post points to published code and a blog discussion but provides no validation details or numerical results.

The solution used Ben's radius-based cropping and affine, flip, and contrast augmentations to produce 256×256 inputs. First-stage SE-ResNeXt and SENet models were trained with regression loss on the 2019 training data plus the 2015 dataset. Their weighted predictions supplied pseudo labels for a second stage initialized from first-stage weights and trained with fold-specific portions of the 2019 test set. Averaging the second-stage predictions achieved public and private leaderboard scores of 0.826 and 0.930.

technique_summary: Uses GPT-OSS-120B, an open-weight MoE LLM with about 12B active parameters per token, run on a single H100 80GB.
Wreath puzzles were deprioritized because simple beam search finds short solutions; the text does not detail what was submitted for them.
Focal loss with weight 1.0 is one component of the combined training loss.
LightGBM was tried and tuned but performed worse than XGBoost.
All experiments use 50 warm-up steps then linear decay to 10% of a 4e-6 peak learning rate.

technique_name: Species pseudo-classes from unique trait vectors
technique_summary: Training observations were grouped into 17,396 species classes by their unique trait values, following a public notebook, to enable classification heads.
Vision transformers underperformed convolutional encoders, which the author partly attributes to his own setup.

technique_name: Appending a metric-exploiting token string to predictions
technique_summary: A fixed suffix with repeated 'lucrarea' tokens, whose sentence-t5 embedding is close to the end-of-sequence token, was appended to predictions, pulling cosine similarity toward a high focal value and adding up to +0.05.
Selected the middle 10k/15k/20k outputs and resampled them with scipy.signal.resample rather than linear interpolation.
CatBoost is used as a base model in the ensemble.

technique_name: Parallel inference over scene subsets on two GPUs
technique_summary: The submission used Kaggle's T4 x2 environment and ran the pipeline in parallel on scene subsets split by dataset to fit more image pairs into the time limit.
High-entropy predictions were labelled 'Other'; the threshold was tuned on the public LB since no outliers were given. Authors report this raised public LB from 0.59 to 0.64.

technique_name: Solution described only in an external repository
technique_summary: The writeup contains no method description; it only points to an external code repository with an English/Japanese explanation of the solution, so no concrete technique can be extracted from this text.
CoT SFT used AdamW at 1e-4 learning rate with weight decay 0.01 and batch size 1024.
DINOv2 ViT-B and ViT-L backbones were used for image feature extraction.
Focal loss caused a noticeable score decrease compared with CE.
Cross-entropy with softmax was used since samples nearly always have a single label among 182 classes.
Supplemental external or simulated data did not work and was not used in the final solution.

technique_name: Manual injury adjustment of team ratings
technique_summary: For men only, player impact ratings were weighted by injury status (1.0/0.75/0.5) and subtracted from team net ratings.
Custom losses did not beat the standard binary focal loss, which the author found sufficient.
Xeno-Canto recordings (under 60 s) of extra Insecta/Amphibia species trained a dedicated model; extra target-species Xeno-Canto data usually hurt and was used by only one ensemble model.

technique_name: Blending position score and game outcome (WDL) as target
technique_summary: Stage 2 targets mixed a position score derived from lc0 Q values with the game result (WDL); stage 1 used only scores from a 5k-node search.
Random subsets were augmented with spelling correction, character edits, synonym replacement, obfuscations, back translation, random capitalization and sentence swaps.

technique_name: Patch cap per slide with Ray parallel processing
technique_summary: WSIs were capped at 200 patches and Ray processed two images at once on one P100 (detection, tiling, feature extraction), bringing runtime under 7 hours; RAM was the limit.
A GNN classifier built a KNN graph (25 nearest neighbours, Euclidean distance) over samples and used GraphSAGE to fit the target.
Used injury reports, manually entered player ratings and AP poll data in addition to competition data.

technique_name: Place cameras on a circle around transparent objects
technique_summary: For transparent scenes, ordered images are assigned evenly spaced camera poses on a circle facing the object instead of running SfM.
A dense autoencoder with a 4-node hidden layer trained with MSE denoises the dip spectrum; per-planet normalization and moving-median smoothing of the input were important.

technique_name: Pure chain-of-thought model with majority voting
technique_summary: Stage-1-only CoT models with maj@32 were limited (best 8/50 public) and discarded in favor of the TIR recipe.
Considered LEB128 variable-length encoding because most 16-bit weights fit in 8 bits, but the author found its compression insufficient.
Four lightly tuned XGBoost models (two target transforms by production/consumption) sharing the same 600 features formed the tree part of the solution.
Automated hyperparameter tuning with Optuna is noted as a missed opportunity.
A post-processing attempt to repair I-URL_PERSONAL predictions did not work.

technique_name: Target differenced and normalized by installed capacity
technique_summary: Models were trained on two target transforms: the 2-day difference divided by installed capacity, and target divided by installed capacity.
7-fold cross-validation split by experiment (tomogram); mean F4 over folds correlated well with the leaderboard.
An extra head predicts each target's loss (trained with MAE); a model with it reached 0.79159/0.78869 versus 0.78945/0.78631 without.
Model weight files were read before initialization so they sit in the Linux page cache, reducing disk access and startup latency.
TF-IDF and LSA text features did not work well.
A custom 3D MixUp implementation allowed longer training while preventing overfitting.
Features from raddar's notebook: provided data, seeds and seed difference, season-average box-score statistics for team and opponents, Elo ratings and a team-quality estimate.
Main loss predicts mean and variance (variance via softplus plus 1e-3), automatically downweighting high-variance samples; the author's ablation credits it with improving accuracy.
Unigram and trigram language models trained on the NLTK Brown corpus with the Llama tokenizer supply additional token probabilities.
Kept only three features for men and four for women, reporting their correlations with the outcome.
Submitted model used SmoothL1 for regression plus cross-entropy for interval classification (classification weight 0.3).
Used Leela Chess Zero training-run data (best from smaller T77/T79 networks) plus Stockfish-generated data previously prepared in binpack format by the author.
Augmenting the data with rare or multinational names did not work.

A seed-and-expand clustering using farthest point sampling and iterative MASt3R matching was built, but it gave no clear benefit over COLMAP multiple reconstructions and scored lower on public/private, so it was dropped.
Selected OOFs were combined with a Ridge meta-model, chosen for stability with correlated predictions and lower overfitting.
Gradient clipping threshold raised to 64.0 for both models, following earlier LMSYS solutions.
Scalar (non-level) features use simple mean/std standardization.
TabM is one of the strongest single models and was heavily hyperparameter-tuned.
RegNetY-008 and RegNetY-016 backbones were used; the final ensemble has two RegNetY-016 models from iteration 4 and one supervised RegNetY-008.
Llama 7B and TinyLlama 1.1B replaced OpenAI models for Ghostbuster token probabilities; fine-tuning TinyLlama on PERSUADE gave a small boost.
Transformer models such as DeBERTa-v3 were tried for external score prediction but never beat TF-IDF + LightGBM.
Models trained on different datasets served as teachers for a student on other data with the same folds, using weighted CE plus temperature-scaled KL loss; reported +0.005-0.01 CV/LB.
Simulated annealing selects a set of candidate subqueries joined by OR; moves add or remove one subquery with equal probability and the score is the number of target patents retrieved.
Stage 2 data was synthesized by prompting GPT-4 for ToRA-style solutions with code execution feedback, approximating the DeepSeekMath Instruct/RL data.
Tversky and Dice losses were listed under what did not work; weighted cross-entropy was kept.

technique_name: Time and frequency masking on spectrograms
technique_summary: XY (time/frequency) masking augmentation was applied to spectrograms.
Plain log(x) normalization did not work, distinct from the log-style representation that was used.
Tournaments are simulated 5000 times to produce the portfolio of brackets required by the 2024 format, approximating the rating-implied probabilities.
Added Moire patterns, flares and overlaid non-rectified images to harden training and improve robustness.
Trained with SmoothL1 loss and AdamW (lr 1e-4) at batch size 1.
Enabled DeepCache (cache_interval=2, cache_branch_id=0) to accelerate diffusion sampling.
Feeding multiple days instead of a single day to the GRU did not work.
CatBoost on the base+bin+digit+categorical feature set was among the frequently selected models.
DeBERTa-v3 large (occasionally base) regression models with 1024 context are the backbone; final ensembles were mostly DeBERTa large.
CoT SFT used 10% linear warmup then decay to 1e-7; TIR fine-tuning used a constant 1e-5 learning rate for 400 steps.
The neural model was LightAutoML's DenseLight dense network (with some library bugs fixed by the author); no larger model beat it.
The segmentation architecture is a U-Net from segmentation_models_pytorch with a ConvNeXt-Tiny encoder.

technique_name: Filter samples by annotator vote count
technique_summary: The shared validation strategy lists a vote count of at least 10 as a criterion; the text does not detail it further.
Added three visible characters in the top-left corner; a search over three-letter combinations selected the string with the best average aesthetic score without hurting VQA.
Gemini-generated prompts and community reasoning templates were evaluated but the original notebook prompt was used instead.
Dice loss with weight 1.0 is part of the combined loss.
Training combined the BELKA train set with an external DEL dataset from a published paper, preprocessed by another participant.
Instead of image retrieval, image pairs are kept when they have at least 30 matches for a single detector and 100 across the detector ensemble, filtering pairs gradually.
Soft and hard pseudo-labeling did not improve CV.
The regression target was efs_time ranked and normalized separately within the efs groups.
Weighted cross-entropy over 7 classes with positive particle pixels weighted 256 versus 1 for background to handle the very small number of positive pixels.
Six early-round men's games where the model was not confident in the higher seed were manually pushed toward ~0.95-0.98, citing expert opinion.
A diverse set of template-based and template-free models was combined; authors believe diversity helped on harder private targets without close templates.
Each tomogram was resized to a fixed (128, 704, 704) volume with scipy.ndimage.zoom.
Used 1000+ per-tile features on the 24x24 map; features were encoded both as normalized continuous values and as binned one-hot vectors.
Extracted integer digit positions and leading decimal digits from numeric variables as extra features (BIN+DIGIT sets appear in top single models).
LightGBM with DART boosting is a base model; DART improved LightGBM by about 0.004 CV and 0.003 LB at a 5-10x training-time cost.
Besides balanced sampling, class weights were applied in the cross-entropy loss to handle subtype imbalance.
A genetic algorithm over islands arranged on a ring, with mechanisms that exchange genetic material while preventing any single solution from dominating the population.
Few-shot prompted Llama 3.1 70B and Qwen 2.5 32B generated additional rulesets; most failed to compile or were low quality, leaving 93 in the extra data.
Blended long lead II into lead II and, when relations nearly hold, softly enforced II = I + III and aVR + aVL + aVF = 0; authors report this added about 0.06.
Protenix provides one prediction for short sequences and two for sequences of 1000 nt or more.
Final solution ensembles 3D segmentation U-Nets with MONAI object detection models (SegResNet and DynUnet backbones) from the teammate's detection pipeline.
7B models were fast but scored lower on CV and LB; 32B CoT models fit but scored close to 14B, so 14B was kept.

technique_name: Weighted voting ensemble of token classifiers
technique_summary: Final predictions came from weighted voting over 7 model groups (10 models), mixing fold and full-fit models for diversity.
MAE loss outperformed MSE despite the R-squared metric, converging faster and more stably; the author calls it the main non-leak secret.
Oversampling hard negatives by OOF log-loss difficulty was listed as not working.
Genetic diversity is the minimal per-tree transformation between solutions (modulo mirror/90-degree rotation), computed with the Hungarian algorithm or a faster approximation in CUDA.
Team strength came from Nate Silver's external power ratings for men's and women's teams rather than a trained model.
Feature set 1 (best for neural nets) includes cyclical features taken from public notebooks by another competitor.

technique_name: Extra detector keypoints matched with MASt3R
technique_summary: Inspired by MP-SfM, ALIKED (1280px, 4096 kpts) and SuperPoint (1600px, 4096 kpts) keypoints are additionally matched using MASt3R features alongside the semi-dense matches, which improved the score.
The inference pipeline hit GPU memory and disk limits even with two models; a ChatGPT-assisted redesign made a 4-model ensemble feasible.
Using betting or prediction-market odds was identified as sensible but not done.
Tried many shaped rewards (relic points, damage, deaths, sensor range, exploration, etc.) before moving to a sparse match-result scheme.
Unlabeled soundscapes were pseudo-labeled by the best previous ensemble and used in Noisy Student-style self-training for 4 iterations with progressively larger backbones, each boosting public LB.
Because of high seed variance on ~4.5k fine-tuning samples, every model was averaged over 3 seeds at train and inference; only the fine-tuning stage was re-run per seed to save compute.
A 4-layer GRU modeled each stock's 55 time steps within a day, predicting all steps at once from the shared 300 features.
Each final ensemble uses its own probability threshold (0.20 for Set 1, 0.26 for Set 2).
Transformer variants, including one from a prior winning solution, were tried without success.
More TMA patches via 30-80% overlapping sliding windows greatly increased runtime (many notebook timeouts) and did not improve performance.
Open-source LLMs were fine-tuned on PERSUADE via metadata instruction tuning, held-out-prompt generation and span-wise generation to produce new writing styles.
TF-IDF features were reduced to 64 dimensions with truncated SVD.

technique_name: Judge-specific score splitting via prompt injection
technique_summary: Built three families of essays, each designed so one judge model gives 0 while the other two give 9, maximizing disagreement among judges.
Hyperparameter tuning of the best models (RealMLP, TabM, GBDTs) while saving OOF predictions from every trial and adding them to the ensemble improved LB from about 8.5335 to 8.5309.
Models are optimized with AdamW.
Training uses the RAdam optimizer for 210 epochs, evaluated every 6 epochs.
Pseudo labels were listed among approaches that did not work.
Out-of-fold image model predictions became features for the GBDT models; at test time predictions from same-type models were averaged.
ResNet34 is one of the two encoder backbones used in the 3D U-Net segmentation models.
Quantized the model (FP8 in the final pipeline per the TL;DR) for faster inference than BF16 and more KV-cache memory; INT4 was measured with notably lower accuracy.
RNN architectures were tried without success.
Several model variants were trained, and heads from different models were combined with manually chosen weights in a mixture-of-experts style.

technique_name: Surface fitting to remove grid-point outliers
technique_summary: Improved the rectification step with sub-pixel grid point estimates via weighted averaging and surface fitting to drop outlier grid points and fill gaps.
Using top CatBoost-importance features, a Local Outlier Factor score per lesion within each patient captured how atypical a lesion is for that patient; improved CV and LB.

technique_name: Averaging overlapping framewise predictions across chunks
technique_summary: Instead of taking only the central 5 s, framewise SED outputs from overlapping 20 s chunks were averaged (like sliding-window segmentation/TTA), with edge padding removed afterwards.
Used a modified fishtest dev server running SPRT tests to measure Elo changes, plus quick local fixed-node checks with fastchess, as the main way to quantify engine progress.

technique_name: Unsplit agent strings as categorical features
technique_summary: Using whole agent strings as categorical features did not work well.
Back-translation augmentation did not work.
CatBoost parameters were tuned with Optuna on tabular-only features and not retuned after adding image-model features; other models were not tuned.
An auxiliary deep-supervision head on the second-to-last feature map contributed to the loss.
Added a pool of older frozen agents as opponents once pure self-play plateaued, to improve robustness and avoid overfitting to one self-play style.
Held out the first ten training IDs, using three image types each (30 images) for validation.
CatBoost trained up to 1000 iterations with early stopping (od_wait 100), with parameters chosen by Optuna on tabular data.
A simple 2.5D model was tried for severity but MIL performed better in the end.
Mixed precision on the T4x2 hardware significantly reduced image matching time.
Because Chowder is sensitive to initialization, each fold trained 50 Chowder models differing only by init, which was more stable than a single model.
Separate bird-call detection models performed close to random/constant prediction.
Implemented mixing behavior-cloning batches from replays of a strong team into RL batches, but did not use it because RL alone was already improving strongly.
A logistic regression on ImageNet ResNet18 thumbnail features classified test images as TMA vs WSI to choose the tiling setup.

technique_name: Hash size tuning under RAM limit
technique_summary: Measured error-loss rates versus hash size near the 5mb RAM limit and chose an 896kb hash for the final submissions, accepting a 3-4% error-loss rate.
Computed possessions, pace and offensive/defensive/net efficiency per game from box scores as inputs to a custom team rating.

technique_name: Periodic online retraining during test period
technique_summary: Models were retrained on newly revealed data every 12 days; the best submission hit the time limit, so only 4 updates ran, and online learning improved test scores in the reported table.
Half-cosine learning-rate decay schedule from a 1e-3 peak.
Predictions were centered by subtracting the stock-weight-weighted mean rather than the plain mean, consistent with the target definition.
Adding external data did not work.

technique_name: MLM pretraining from scratch with small vocabulary
technique_summary: Training DeBERTa-v3-xsmall from scratch as an MLM with a 55-token custom vocabulary on q-masked text failed to get below 0.63.
Regressor training weighted efs==1 and efs==0 samples 0.6:0.4.
BCE and focal losses gave similar results when tuned but were slightly worse than CE, so they were not used.

technique_name: Local LLM judge proxies for validation
technique_summary: Candidate essays/attacks were validated locally against three judge LLMs (Gemma, Qwen, Phi) assumed to mirror the hidden judges.

technique_name: Noise injection for selected race groups
technique_summary: Adding noise for some race groups improved CV considerably but did not help on public or private LB.
Plain averaging of all OOF predictions hurt performance compared with selected subsets.
Final inference matched patch height/width to the volume and slid only along depth with 0.875 overlap, about 4x faster than the original pipeline at similar score.
Images were only scaled by dividing by 65535 (16-bit range) with no other normalization.
Each model's outputs were calibrated with a logistic regression fit on its internal validation split, which slightly improved public LB.

technique_name: Predict traits via species classification lookup
technique_summary: A classification head predicts the species and outputs that species' trait values.
Training used the first 500 days with the remaining days as a holdout, which tracked the leaderboard well; only the overall ensemble score was monitored.
The main trick: a short Ludii MCTS search (UCB1Tuned, random playouts, ~15 s) on each game's starting position yields game-balance features, improving ~0.045 CV and ~0.012 LB.
LLMs were loaded as AutoModelForSequenceClassification with max length 1024, 2 epochs and global batch size 64.

technique_name: Monthly retraining on newly revealed data
technique_summary: Expecting 8 more months of data in the private period, the author traded a larger ensemble for fewer models retrained monthly; updates improved test scores in the reported table.
Mixup was applied to every training sample.
During inference, generated code blocks were executed in a sandbox and the output or error trace appended before generation continued.
Changed quantization constants from the defaults (QA=255, QB=64) to QA=101, QB=160, trading weight precision against the size limit.
A physically motivated wind magnitude from u and v components was added; it neither helped nor hurt.
Nonlinear stacking meta-models overfit and did not improve CV.
Applied the community ptend trick for a range of moisture tendency targets (ptend_q0002_2 to 26).

technique_name: Transposing weight layout to improve compression
technique_summary: Observed that storing correlated weights sequentially compresses better, so transposing the feature-transformer weight matrix reduces binary size; whether it was in the final build is not explicitly stated.
tf_efficientnet B0/B3/B4 (Noisy Student weights) backbones were used across stages; the final ensemble included B4, B3 and a B0 Amphibia/Insecta model.
Mel spectrograms (224 mel bins, large hop size for speed with long chunks, 0-1 normalized) repeated to 3 channels formed the input; more mel bins helped distinguish narrow-band species.
Label-dependent epsilon-insensitive L1 loss gave their best single model on private LB but was not in the submitted model.
Each full 630x630x184 tomogram is standardized by its mean and standard deviation before patch extraction.
Models were exported via JIT or TensorRT for inference, reported as a 200% speedup that allowed a slightly larger ensemble within the time limit.
The final NuminaMath-7B-TIR model was fine-tuned from DeepSeekMath-Base 7B, which the team found hard to beat because of its math-focused continued pretraining.
Inputs were generated two ways: homography to 3200x2400 then grid remapping, or remapping directly on the rotated image; a one-image local test favored high-resolution remapping over low-resolution.
A DINOv2 ViT pretrained on PlantCLEF 2024 southwestern European flora (Pl@ntNet images) gave a significant boost.
TRL SFTTrainer packing concatenated samples into 2048-token chunks to speed up training.
Repeated (3x) stratified 5-fold CV with an inner 75/25 train/validation split; folds were designed so test folds held at least 60% of TMAs, keeping most TMAs for evaluation.
Tuned engine parameters with SPSA for sudden-death time controls, using 20s instead of 10s to account for delay and pondering.
Applied stochastic dropout for regularization of the encoder.
Newline and double-space tokens were added to the tokenizer, following a tip shared by another participant.
No effective method for separating touching sheets was found; the team relied on nnU-Net itself to limit them.

technique_name: Different opening verb per model for diversity
technique_summary: Each model was prompted with a different opening verb to diversify the concatenated predictions, raising the score from 0.70 to 0.71.
GBDT was weak alone and as a second stage added nothing over the ensemble plus thresholding, though limited time was spent on it.
A multi-sample dropout DeBERTa variant gave smoother training curves with fewer spikes; listed among variations tried for the ensemble without explicit confirmation of final use.
Model was a U-Net-like 3D network with a single deconvolution block in the decoder before the segmentation head.
Listed as an idea the author did not get around to trying.
TabM tabular neural network was one of the classifiers, also in a rank-loss variant, used in the classifier-regressor combinations.
TabNet (CV 0.609) was included among the NN base models.
An external English Word Frequency dataset supplied one of the signals for keyword priors.
Each model block averages the 20 models from 10-fold CV repeated for 2 seeds, instead of a full-data refit.
Stage-two pre-training predicted 2048-bit chiral ECFP fingerprints from SMILES with frozen embeddings; though MAP was only ~0.4, the author credits it for learning useful representations.
A play-level model with a 3-layer Transformer encoder over up to 22 players models inter-player interactions, using player masks for variable counts and SwiGLU FFNs.
Rebound and free-throw rate (and most other tried features) made the model worse and were dropped.
The winning submission averaged predictions of 65 Chowder models from selected CV repetitions/folds rather than all 750 trained models.
Tomograms were ranked by max predicted value and the lowest quantile predicted as no motor; the quantile was tuned on public LB (0.565 public optimum, 0.560 private).
A boundary loss (arXiv 1812.07032) with small weight 0.01 is added to the combined loss.
SIFT, GIMSuperPoint and DaD were tried as additional keypoint detectors but not adopted because ALIKED+SuperPoint gave the best LB score.
XGBoost was tried but did not work well.
Reimplemented the metric's image processing pipeline more efficiently so candidate SVGs could be scored locally.
Final essays are reconstructed from the keystroke logs using public essay-constructor notebooks and used for text features and NLP models.
Delta-shift TTA, borrowed from the 2nd place BirdCLEF 2023 solution, was applied at inference.
Larger dimensions (64), smaller (16), and models deeper than 6 layers did not perform as well as the small 32-dim, 4-layer encoder.

technique_name: Template-based structure modeling via sequence alignment
technique_summary: Global pairwise alignment against train+validation structures, keeping length-compatible top-30 templates; TBM is the primary predictor for sequences of 250 nt or more.
Initial approach used 3D Gaussian balls as segmentation targets; it was replaced by single-pixel targets after analysis of the detection model.
Because disk loading was slow, all augmentations except rescaling ran on the GPU; rescaling used fast order-0 zoom.
1D-CNN models were tried but did not work.
Three-fold CV with folds grouped jointly by state and sampling date; single-fold models were trained.
